overview:
The master reference for every FX chain in the template — the routing model, the theory behind chain order, the conventions every chain note follows, and the index of all chains. Built around the actual rig: Apollo MkII + UAD Console (Unison), Ableton Live Suite, the Plugin Index collection, Neumann TLM 102 + Shure SM57, Strat / Yamaha acoustic / Hofner bass.

## The routing model

```
TRACK ──→ GROUP ──→ BUS ──→ MASTER
  │          │        │
  └──────── sends ────┘──→ RETURNS ─┬─ dedicated to one family ──→ that family's BUS
                                    └─ shared / mix-wide ───────→ MASTER
```

**Division of labor — each level exists to answer a different question:**
- **Track** — "what does this *sound* like?" Corrective + character work on one source. The only level where surgery belongs.
- **Group** — "how do these tracks relate *to each other* and to the other groups?" Carving, internal balance, section glue. (Steps 4–5 of the process.)
- **Bus** — "what's the *finish* on this section?" Broad, gentle, analog-flavored: glue comp, tape, density. If you reach for surgery at bus level, the fix belongs upstream.
- **Returns/sends** — shared spaces and parallel treatments (reverbs, delays, crush, dirt, width). Shared = coherent: everyone in the same room, one dirt flavor, blendable per-track via send levels.
  - **Return routing rule:** a return that serves ONE family routes into that family's bus ([Delay Send Slap](#/chain/delay-send-slap), [Delay Send Other](#/chain/delay-send-other), [Reverb Send Long](#/chain/reverb-send-long) → [Vocal Bus](#/chain/vocal-bus)) — the bus glue melts wet into dry, and a bus fader ride carries the space with the voice. A return shared mix-wide ([Reverb Send Room](#/chain/reverb-send-room), [Saturation Send](#/chain/saturation-send), [Width Send](#/chain/width-send), [Parallel Comp Send](#/chain/parallel-comp-send)) stays → master — folding it into any one bus would drag every other sender through that bus's chain. Handle shared returns *at the return* (band-limit, duck); the [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain) is the only processing they pass through, and that's correct.
- **Master** — the final 10%. ±1–2 dB moves only; two modes (mix-into-it vs export loudness) — see [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain).

## The recording process (6 steps)

1. **Input** — external sources through the Apollo: Unison preamp + UAD comp + UAD EQ printed on the way in, like tracking to analog. *Conservative*: 2–4 dB GR peaks-only, HPF + a dB of air max — you can always add later, never remove. Internal/digital sources get the UAD plugin equivalents in Ableton (no Unison impedance magic, same gain-staging discipline) — digital instruments are still instruments.
2. **Initial processing** (bounce-in-place) — corrective EQ, de-noise, first saturation. Commit when dialed.
3. **Track effects** — character, delays/reverb sends, per-track color. Bounceable once stable.
4. **Group processing** — EQ *against the other tracks/groups*: decide what stands out, cut the interference **from the other group**, not by boosting yourself.
5. **Group effects** — section-level glue/width/duck.
6. **Bus + master** — finish and loudness.

## Core principles (the theory the chains are built on)

**Chain order: corrective EQ → compression → saturation/color → tonal EQ → de-ess/cleanup.**
- *Cuts before compression* — the comp shouldn't waste its GR chasing rumble and mud you're throwing away anyway.
- *Saturation after compression* — a leveled signal hits the saturator consistently, so the color is even across the performance. (Exception: 808s/sound design, where saturation *generates* the tone — see [Digital Bass Track](#/chain/digital-bass-track).)
- *Boosts after compression* — boost before and the comp just compresses your boost back down.
- *De-ess/soothe last* — sibilance and harshness are regenerated by every comp and saturator; clean up after the mess is made, not before.

**Gain staging: ~0 VU (≈ −18 dBFS) into everything.**
- Analog-modeled plugins (UAD, Decapitator, Kramer, API-2500…) are calibrated to hardware sweet spots — hit them at −18 dBFS average and they sing; slam them and they choke.
- **Meter sandwich convention:** Utility (gain in) + mvMeter2nogpu (VU) at the chain head, Utility (trim) + meter at the tail, extra meters between sections on long chains. Target ~0 VU average; peaky sources (drums) average 0 with peaks flying; background elements can run looser.
- **Unity through every device:** set each device's output so bypassing it doesn't change loudness — otherwise "louder = better" psychoacoustics fools you on every single knob decision.

**Compression in stages, never in one bite.**
- Tracking 1176 (2–4 dB peaks) → track comp (3–5 dB shape) → group/bus glue (1–2 dB) beats one 10 dB squash: each stage works gently, so none of them pump. The record ends up *more* controlled and *more* dynamic-feeling at once.

**Serial vs parallel.**
- Serial (inserts) trades dynamics for control. Parallel (sends: [Parallel Comp Send](#/chain/parallel-comp-send), [Saturation Send](#/chain/saturation-send), [Width Send](#/chain/width-send)) adds density/size *without* the trade — dry keeps the transients, the return brings the wreckage underneath.

**Space is EQ'd, ducked, and shared.**
- Returns run 100% wet, band-limited (HPF 200–300, LPF 4–8k) — space without spectral cost.
- Pre-delay 15–25 ms separates dry from tail = upfront *and* placed.
- Big tails duck under the dry vocal (sidechain) = size without smear.
- Low end never gets reverb, never gets width, and lives in mono below ~100–120 Hz.

**The masking hierarchy.** Every carve decision flows from one ranking: **lead vocal → drums backbeat/kick → bass → hooks/leads → everything else.** When two elements collide, the lower-ranked one moves (dip, duck, pan, or drop an octave). Dynamic EQ keyed from the winner beats static carves — full sound when alone, automatic space when it matters.

## Note format (Producer Pal phase 2 contract)

Every chain note is machine-parseable for future Producer Pal automation:
- **Frontmatter:** `type: chain` · `chain_type: track|group|bus|send|master|style|foundation` (`foundation` = a reusable neutral front-end block prepended to a family's track chains before role/character decisions — currently [Vocal Foundation](#/chain/vocal-foundation)) · `family` · `source` · `routing` · `uad_console` (the Step 1 recording chain — Unison preamp, UAD compressor, UAD EQ; UAD-plugin-equivalent front end on digital sources) · `signal_chain` (ordered Ableton device list, musical devices only — the meter sandwich is implied by this doc)
- **Section structure (track chains — the 6-part standard, 2026-07-16):** `## 1 — Recording Setup` (mics/DI, placement, room, monitoring, gear links) → `## 2 — Tracking Best Practice` (double-track or not, mono/stereo, take-stacking variations — the decisions that shape the mix later) → `## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD Console)` (Unison preamp + UAD comp + UAD EQ printed on the way in; software instruments swap this for instrument choice + UAD-equivalent front end) → `## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing` (corrective/bounceable) → `## 5 — Track FX (optional)` → `## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)` (routing + send levels). Every UAD plugin name starts with **UAD** and links to its plugin note (UAD UA 610-B, UAD Teletronix LA-2A, UAD Pultec EQP-1A, UAD UA 1176LN, UAD Neve 1073) so console-side vs Ableton-side is unambiguous. Every named plugin/gear/technique is a `wikilink`, and every adjusted parameter gets a concrete starting value. **ALL track chains converted (2026-07-16).** Software-instrument chains use the adapted parts — `## 1 — Sound Selection` (instrument/sample choice IS the recording step) and `## 2 — Programming Best Practice` — and their §3 is `Source → Ableton (UAD front end)`: no mics, but the UAD plugins still act as the console input (preamp → comp → EQ, printed at ~0 VU), so digital sources get the same tracking discipline as recorded ones.
- **Body grammar:** stages are `### N. Device Name — role`, settings as bullets beneath, rationale on a `**Why:**` line. Device names match Live's Device Lister names where possible (`UAD UA 1176LN Rev E`, etc.).
- Phase 2: Producer Pal reads `signal_chain` + stage headings → instantiates devices in order on the right track/group/return → applies starting-point settings → human fine-tunes (`uad_console` is console-side, listed for the human).

chains.title: Vocal Foundation
chains.routing: prepends §4 of every vocal track chain (Main / Double / Harmony / Backup / Ensemble)
chains.body:
**The identical first step in every vocal chain.** Drop this on any vocal — lead, double, harmony, ad-lib, ensemble stack — *before* you've decided how the part gets treated. It does only the neutral, corrective work that every vocal wants no matter its role: get level right, correct pitch, cut what's wrong, level the dynamics, tame resonance. Nothing here shapes character or commits to a sound.

**Why a fixed block:** you don't always know at record time whether a take becomes the lead, a stacked double, or one voice in an ensemble. This block is the same regardless, so you can commit it immediately and postpone the creative calls ([lead](#/chain/main-vocal-track) vs [double](#/chain/double-vocal-track) vs [ensemble](#/chain/ensemble-stack-track)) until you actually hear the arrangement. The UAD Console front end (UAD Neve 1073 → comp → EQ, printed on the way in) is already the same across vocals — this is the Ableton-side equivalent: a shared, printable starting point.

**Where it sits:** this *is* the front of `## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing` on each vocal track note. Everything after the hand-off point below is per-role and decided later.

## Prep — before the block (same as any vocal)

- **Clip-gain to ~0 VU / −18 dBFS average** by hand — pull the big jumps down first so the comp works on musical dynamics, not editing you skipped (Gain Staging).
- **Chop dead space between phrases** (keep natural breaths, never clip word edges) — every downstream comp raises the floor of what you leave. **Editing is gain-staging** — Kenny Beats, [Recording Vocals the Right Way](https://youtu.be/3Nw1d37nluo).
- Fix pops/mouth noise and do Melodyne-level pitch surgery here, before the chain — no plugin fixes a sloppy comp.
- 🎬 **Mic distance is an intentional intimacy/bass-boost dial (the proximity effect), not just placement trivia** — moving a directional mic closer raises low-frequency response; roughly a fist's distance is a good default, closer (a finger's length) for deliberate warmth/intimacy on a specific line. Decide per-take, not just per-session. — Synthet, [how to make love music](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vGxAodP1-dc)

## The block

Meter sandwich implied by the head/tail Utility + mvMeter2nogpu — target ~0 VU average in and out (Gain Staging).

### 1. Auto-Tune Pro — Pitch (neutral default)
- Key/scale: **match the song** · **Retune 45–50** (natural, "invisible support") · **Humanize 100%** · **Flex-Tune 0** · **input voice type set to the actual voice** (Low Male / Alto / Soprano — a range switch; wrong = it misreads everything)
- Keep it invisible here. Hard-tune (Retune 0–20 / audible ~7) is a *character* choice — make it downstream per song, not in the foundation — [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c).
- **Why:** First so everything downstream reacts to corrected pitch.

### 2. Pro-Q 4 — Corrective EQ (subtractive only)
- HPF 24 dB/oct @ **80–100 Hz** · cut mud **−2 to −4 dB @ 200–400 Hz** · check **2–5 kHz** for harshness/nasality and dip if needed · **Natural Phase** mode (tracking is done)
- No boosts here — presence/air/tone shaping is a later, per-role move.
- **Why:** Cuts before compression so the comp doesn't spend its GR fighting rumble and mud.

### 3. Pro-C 2 — Leveling compression
- Style **Vocal** · attack **10 ms** · release **auto** · **3–5 dB GR** · range slider caps GR ~5 dB so it can't overreact
- Second-stage leveler — the CL 1B opto at tracking (§3 of the track note) was stage one; this fast digital comp catches the transients the opto let through (Compression Staging).
- **Why:** "Some compression" — musical control, not squash. Staged beats one deep comp.

### 4. Soothe2 — Resonance suppression
- **Soft mode** · sharpness/selectivity default (~3) · raise depth until clearly working, back off slightly · focus **1–6 kHz** · delta mode to audition what it removes
- **Why:** Dynamic harshness control static EQ can't do — this is still corrective, so it belongs in the foundation. Placed before any color so you're not exciting resonances downstream.

## Hand-off — everything past here is a later, per-role decision

The foundation stops at neutral. These get chosen once you know the part's job — see the role notes:

- **Color / saturation** (Saturn 2, Decapitator, Kramer Tape) — density + attitude, and it re-pushes sibilance, which is *why* it lands after the foundation
- **Tonal EQ boosts** (presence @ 3–5 kHz, air shelf) — Pro-Q 4 additive pass
- **De-ess** (Pro-DS) — the finishing de-ess goes *last*, after color has regenerated the S's; don't bake it into the foundation. (Pull a *light* corrective Pro-DS in here only if a source is genuinely too essy to comp cleanly.)
- **Air** (Gem Dopamine / Fresh Air)
- **Role & width:** lead upfront/mono ([Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track)) · doubles hard-panned ([Double Vocal Track](#/chain/double-vocal-track)) · harmonies ([Harmony Vocal Track](#/chain/harmony-vocal-track)) · ensemble spread + [Width Send](#/chain/width-send) ([Ensemble Stack Track](#/chain/ensemble-stack-track))
- **Space:** [Reverb Send Room](#/chain/reverb-send-room) / [Delay Send Slap](#/chain/delay-send-slap) — group/bus sends, per the routing model

## Producer Pal note

`chain_type: foundation` is a new type: Producer Pal instantiates `signal_chain` as a **saved device rack** ("Vocal Foundation") it can prepend to any vocal track chain, then the role-specific stages append after. The meter-sandwich Utility/mvMeter2nogpu pair is included explicitly here since this rack is the chain head.

## Sources

Kenny Beats — [Recording Vocals the Right Way](https://youtu.be/3Nw1d37nluo) · [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c) · [Vocal Template](https://youtu.be/X_iDENABLmk) — chain-order theory in [FX Chain System](#/chains/system) · Compression Staging · Gain Staging

chains.title: Backup Vocal Track
chains.routing: Backup Vocal → Backup Vocals Group → Vocal Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Ad-libs, gang vox, response lines, shout layers — anything that answers or hypes the lead rather than doubling it. Backups can take far more character/degradation than the lead — *differentness* is what makes them read as a separate element.

**Chain philosophy:** tune → band-limit → crush → character → de-ess.

## 1 — Recording Setup

- **Neumann TLM 102** for clean stacks; the **Shure SM57** is a great choice for grittier ad-libs — its mid-forward bite separates naturally from the TLM lead. (Handheld SM57 with monitors up = the Dijon/Dua Lipa energy lane.)
- Same room/latency discipline as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §1.

## 2 — Tracking Best Practice

- **Stack discipline (Kuk Harrell):** stacks come in **fours**, panned hard L/R *as you track them* — check the first take's tightness in mono before the pan spreads it wide, and keep every added stack's level identical to the last while tracking so the blend judgment stays honest (see [1 Double Vocal Track](#/chain/double-vocal-track) for both steps in full); sung softer than the lead, with a softer "give it to me sexy" unison direction when the lead is already powerful (see Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs); **one shared FX chain across all stacks** — reverb, delay, a little doubler, EQ, compressor, then "the driver" (unconfirmed device), dialed in once and reused for the entire record's stacks, not reinvented per line — simplicity makes a stack read as one instrument. Kuk Harrell (Mix with the Masters), Creating vocal stacks with Kuk Harrell.
- 🎬 **The Kenny ad-lib architecture: pan-L track + pan-R track + phone-filter track (center)** — two takes alternate sides; the band-limited phone-filter lane cuts through *between* the mains without being louder — [New Vocal Chain 2022](https://youtu.be/-SvBNOBWJ_8) → Masking and Carving.
- 🎬 **The moving center ad-lib** — a third lane running PanMan, drifting between the wide pair: static width + one moving element — [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c).
- 🎬 **Vary the tune per lane** — ad-libs Legato when mains run Soft EFX (smoother bed), or *more* retune on reaching stacks — never one setting across mains + ad-libs — [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c).
- 🎬 **Syllable/consonant sync separates professional from sloppy stacks** — a stacked phrase where one take's consonant lands a fraction off from the others reads as unprofessional; sync syllable timing across takes while tracking, or manually nudge it afterward. Stacking itself also has a performer-facing benefit worth knowing: a self-conscious singer finds their own take easier to accept layered than exposed alone — one more reason to track doubles even on a rough idea. → Vocal Harmony — Synthet, [the vocal trick to like yourself](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dulq8IJR9nI)

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD Console)

Same console pass as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §3; for gritty SM57 ad-libs, drive the UAD Neve 1073 harder — attitude on the way in is on-brand here.

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

**From the [Vocal Foundation](#/chain/vocal-foundation) →** keeps the skeleton (tune → corrective EQ → level) but is the **one role that deliberately breaks the foundation's "no color" rule *in-chain*** — for backups, *differentness* is the job, so character gets added here instead of deferred. The deltas:
- **Neutral default → varied/off** (§4.1 — match the lead for polished stacks, off for shouted ad-libs, or vary per lane; never one setting across mains + ad-libs)
- **Corrective HPF/cut → telephone-ish band-limit** (§4.2 — HPF 150–250, LPF 8–10k; they live at the edges)
- **Leveling 3–5 dB → crush 6–10 dB** (§4.3 — flat and steady)
- **Drop Soothe2; add RC-20 Retro Color in-chain** (§4.4 — degradation pushes backups behind the lead and gives ad-libs attitude; this is the foundation's deferred "color" stage pulled *forward* on purpose)
- **De-ess harder** (§4.5) than the lead

### 1. Auto-Tune Pro — Pitch
- Match the lead's setting for polished stacks (or vary per §2), off for shouted/spoken ad-libs.

### 2. Pro-Q 4 — Band-limit
- HPF 150–250 Hz · LPF 8–10 kHz — telephone-ish is fine, they live at the edges.

### 3. Pro-C 2 — Crush
- 4:1–8:1 · **6–10 dB GR** — flat and steady.

### 4. RC-20 Retro Color — Character (optional but on-brand)
- Lo-Fi or Tape mode · mix 20–40%
- **Why:** A little degrade pushes backups behind the lead and gives ad-libs attitude — especially hip hop.

### 5. Pro-DS — De-ess
- Standard split-band pass — de-ess stacks *harder* than the lead; width should never come with stray S's.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- **Phone filter** on the center ad-lib lane (band-limited beats louder).
- Decapitator pushed for the screamed lane (Shure SM57 → UAD Neve 1073 slammed → Decapitator Punish, no cleanup — the Dijon move).

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Backup Vocal → [Backup Vocals Group](#/chain/backup-vocals-group) → [Vocal Bus](#/chain/vocal-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)** — the stack-bus chain (group saturation → 1176 → EQ → Decapitator → group de-ess) lives on the group.

- **Delay treatment:** ad-lib **throws** are inserts on a dedicated throw track (loud EchoBoy, high-end cut, subdivision per throw) — the signature backup move, drag the last word to the throw track. **Cohesion** delay for the whole stack rides the shared group send ([Delay Send Other](#/chain/delay-send-other)), sidechain-ducked to the lead → Sidechaining. Cohesion → group send · moment → insert. · [Reverb Send Room](#/chain/reverb-send-room) to sit the stack together.

## Variations

- **Trap ad-libs:** hard-tune + [Saturation Send](#/chain/saturation-send) pushed, pan hard L/R alternating, delay throws on line-ends.
- **Gang/crowd vox:** no tune, wide pan spread across takes, [Reverb Send Long](#/chain/reverb-send-long) for size.

## Sources

Kuk Harrell (Mix with the Masters) — Creating vocal stacks with Kuk Harrell · Kenny Beats — [New Vocal Chain 2022](https://youtu.be/-SvBNOBWJ_8) · [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c) · Disclosure — [Remix Stems Stream](https://youtu.be/IOSPhXcXT_8) (stack-bus chain on [Backup Vocals Group](#/chain/backup-vocals-group))

chains.title: Double Vocal Track
chains.routing: Double Vocal → Main Vocal Group → Vocal Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Unison double(s) of the lead — thickness, not a second voice. Band-limit dramatically, compress flat, mix in until you only notice it when you mute it (tucked −6 to −10 dB under the lead).

**Chain philosophy:** tune tight → bandpass hard → crush → de-ess → tuck.

## 1 — Recording Setup

- Same setup as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §1: Neumann TLM 102, same room/latency discipline, ghost latency track armed.
- **Performance note:** sing doubles slightly *softer* than the lead — a softer unison layers in as sweetness instead of competing.

## 2 — Tracking Best Practice

- **Record a real L+R pair, panned hard (35–50 L/R)** — the doubles are the vocal's width layer; a single mono double sits ~10–15 off-center instead.
- 🎬 **Pan hard the instant a stack is tracked, and judge the FIRST take in mono before anything else** — Kuk Harrell tracks the first stack, immediately pans it hard, and specifically checks tightness *in mono* first ("I'll start panning left and right away so I can tell if it's tight in mono... it's definitely there, so it's so tight"); the wide image only comes after the mono check confirms the take is genuinely tight, since looseness that reads as "fine" in mono can still be barely-there once split — Kuk Harrell (Mix with the Masters), Creating vocal stacks with Kuk Harrell → Width and Stereo.
- 🎬 **Keep every added stack's level EXACTLY the same as the one before it while tracking, specifically to judge whether the vibe is matching** — "I keep the levels exactly the same because if I start pulling down what they did now I can't really tell if the vibe is matching"; level-match during the tracking pass, not after, so blend problems get caught rather than hidden — Kuk Harrell (Mix with the Masters), Creating vocal stacks with Kuk Harrell.
- **On big hooks, stack in FOURS** — two per side, never two total ("if you stack something you always want to do four, don't do two — because if you do two you've just got three there and it really doesn't create anything special. So always just do an even number of four" — Kuk Harrell (Mix with the Masters), Creating vocal stacks with Kuk Harrell; two sounds like three voices, four becomes a texture). 🎬 Kenny's stepped-pan version: duplicate the hard pair at ~25L/25R, again at ~15L/15R — one harmony per slot, a big stack with zero wideners — [New Vocal Chain 2022](https://youtu.be/-SvBNOBWJ_8).
- **Real doubles beat doublers** — Kenny ran a ~20% Doubler2-style on everything for years ("bigger, not doubled"), then dropped it entirely for real takes — [Vocal Template](https://youtu.be/X_iDENABLmk). When you *do* want a fake double, that's **Artificial Double Tracking (ADT)** — the Beatles/Lennon trick (MicroShift or Doubler2 with detune + delay + modulation on).
- **Editing before processing (the real secret):** align the double's timing and pitch to the lead first — manually or VocAlign Ultra AU — and keep S's/T's aligned or edited off (the lead carries the consonants). No plugin fixes a loose double; a tight double barely needs processing.

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD Console)

Same console pass as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §3 (UAD Neve 1073 → UAD Tube-Tech CL 1B mkII → UAD Pultec EQP-1A), printed conservatively.

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

**From the [Vocal Foundation](#/chain/vocal-foundation) →** the double keeps the block's *skeleton* (tune → corrective EQ → level) but is the most aggressive departure from its neutral defaults — every setting pushes toward *band-limited, crushed, tucked* rather than transparent. The deltas:
- **Retune 45–50 → 18** (tighter than the lead so it fuses instead of chorusing)
- **Corrective HPF/cut → hard bandpass** (§4.2 — kill lows *and* air; the double owns neither)
- **Leveling 3–5 dB → crush 6–10 dB** (§4.3 — no dynamic life of its own)
- **Drop Soothe2; swap in a hard Pro-DS** (§4.4 — a band-limited crushed double doesn't need resonance surgery, it needs its S's gone since the lead carries consonants)
No color, air, or width stages — the double's whole job is invisibility, so the foundation's hand-off *toward* character is declined here.

### 1. Auto-Tune Pro — Pitch
- **Retune 18** (① — tighter than the lead so the double fuses instead of chorusing out of tune) · **Humanize 100%** (③) · **Flex-Tune 0** (②) · **Key/Scale = song key** (④).

### 2. Pro-Q 4 — Hard bandpass
- HPF 180–250 Hz · LPF 8–10 kHz · dip 3–5 kHz −2 dB (presence belongs to the lead)
- Flavor call: **warm/dark doubles** for soft wide hooks, airy for bright pop — opposite of whatever the harmonies get
- **Why:** Doubles that keep their lows and air smear the lead; tighter band = one thick voice.

### 3. Pro-C 2 — Crush
- 4:1–6:1 · fast-ish attack · **6–10 dB GR**
- **Why:** Doubles should have no dynamic life of their own — flat layers glue.

### 4. Pro-DS — De-ess hard
- Range 6–10 dB · or edit/nudge the double's S's and T's off the lead's instead.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- Nothing, usually — differentness belongs to backups/harmonies; the double's job is invisibility.

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Double Vocal → [Main Vocal Group](#/chain/main-vocal-group) → [Vocal Bus](#/chain/vocal-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)** — the group has the chain; these tracks stay dry.

- Little or no reverb of its own — it rides the lead's space. A touch of [Width Send](#/chain/width-send) only if a single mono double needs spread.
- **Delay:** rides the lead's shared group delay send at a *low* level, sidechain-ducked with the lead → Sidechaining — a double lives tight to the lead, so much delay of its own pulls it off into a separate voice. **No per-double throws** — a word-throw belongs on the lead track's throw insert, not here. Cohesion → shared group send · moment → the lead's insert.

## Variations

- **Hook-only doubles:** automate them in for choruses — verses stay single-voice (Arrangement and Song Form subtraction logic).
- **Wide pop doubles:** pan the pair 25–35 L/R and let more air through (LPF up to 12 kHz).

## Sources

Kuk Harrell (Mix with the Masters) — Creating vocal stacks with Kuk Harrell · Make Pop Music (stacks) — link in [FX Chain System](#/chains/system) · Kenny Beats — [New Vocal Chain 2022](https://youtu.be/-SvBNOBWJ_8) · [Vocal Template](https://youtu.be/X_iDENABLmk)

chains.title: Ensemble Stack Track
chains.routing: Ensemble Stack (each layer) → Ensemble Stack Group → Vocal Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** The **per-layer prep** for a self-stacked vocal ensemble — the tune/align/band-limit/level work applied to *each individual layer* you record, whatever its role in the stack. There is **no fixed take count**: you build the ensemble from a menu of layer-roles (core, doubles, octave anchor, air, harmonies…) and add blocks as the section needs. The arrangement/roles and the glue live on [Ensemble Stack Group](#/chain/ensemble-stack-group); this note is what makes any single layer sit right.

This is distinct from [Double Vocal Track](#/chain/double-vocal-track) (one lead + one double) and [Backup Vocal Track](#/chain/backup-vocal-track) (elements that *answer* the lead). A stack can be run two ways — decide per song (see the group note): a **fused ensemble** (no single lead, everything level-matched into one source — Bon Iver/Imogen Heap) or a **lead + support stack** (a front vocal with doubles/octaves/harmonies underneath — standard pop). The building blocks are the same; only the balance differs.

**Chain philosophy:** `tune → align → band-limit → level-match` (per layer) ▸ `EQ → glue → saturate → de-ess → shared space` (on the group). **Unify per-layer, glue on the group.** What fuses a stack is *consistency of tuning, timing, and space* — not per-layer processing. Keep the *performance* differences you tracked on purpose (a soft approach vs a full one, ahead vs behind, vowel shape), but lock pitch and time and match tone. In a fused ensemble, **level-match ruthlessly so no layer becomes an accidental lead**; in a lead+support stack, the support layers deliberately sit lower.

## 1 — Recording Setup

- **Same mic for every layer** — Neumann TLM 102, shock mount, pop filter ~4" out, 48V on. One consistent source is half of what fuses a self-stack; don't swap mics between layers the way you would for *contrast* on backups.
- **Consistent distance and position per layer-role.** Keep mic distance identical across a role (esp. whisper/air layers, which expose distance changes). Step back slightly and sing softer for gang/choir layers to keep peaks controlled.
- Same room/latency discipline as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §1 (phone silenced, HVAC off, track through the UAD Console to sidestep latency).

## 2 — Tracking Best Practice

- **Record in role-pairs, and know each layer's job before you sing it** (full menu in [Ensemble Stack Group](#/chain/ensemble-stack-group) `## Layer roles`). Doubles get tracked as **L/R pairs** so the stereo image is built at the source; harmonies get **doubled per part**; the octave-down anchor is usually a **single centered take**.
- **Match what a layer is doubling.** A double should copy the tone, phrasing, and timing of the take it doubles as closely as possible, with **softer sibilance and transients** so it blends under rather than flams against the source — [Sage Audio](https://www.sageaudio.com/articles/how-to-stack-vocals).
- **Sing core/unison layers with intent, not identically.** For a rich single source you want the *performances* varied (soft/breathy vs full/chest, slightly ahead/behind, different vowel emphasis) while pitch and time get locked afterward. Tuning + alignment can't *add* richness — that has to go in at the mic.
- **Octave layers are felt, not heard** — sing them relaxed; they add weight (down) or sheen (up), and they'll sit low in the mix, so don't oversing them.
- **Kuk-Harrell stack discipline:** track a role in one pass, judge tightness against the panned image as you go, sing the stack softer than a normal lead, and run **one shared chain across the whole role**. Cross-reference [FX Chain System](#/chains/system) and [Backup Vocal Track](#/chain/backup-vocal-track) §2 rather than re-deriving it.

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD Console)

Same console pass as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §3 (UAD Neve 1073 → UAD Tube-Tech CL 1B mkII → UAD Pultec EQP-1A), printed conservatively. Keep the print **matched within a role** (same preamp gain and 2–4 dB opto GR across all the doubles of a part) so no layer arrives louder or brighter than its siblings — matched prints are what let layers fuse. The octave-down anchor and air layer can print at their own level since they occupy different registers.

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing (per layer)

**From the [Vocal Foundation](#/chain/vocal-foundation) →** a stack takes only the block's **front half** per layer — gain-in → Auto-Tune Pro → corrective Pro-Q 4 — and **deliberately drops the foundation's Pro-C 2 and Soothe2 at the layer stage.** Per-take leveling/resonance work fights fusion (it re-separates the voices), so those two move *downstream*: the glue comp is one opto over the whole stack on [the group](#/chain/ensemble-stack-group), and Soothe2 runs once on the [Vocal Bus](#/chain/vocal-bus). In their place the layer adds **VocAlign Project 5 AU** (§4.2 — the timing/fusion knob a single voice never needs) and **level-matching** (§4.4). Net: the ensemble still runs the foundation's full logic — it's just spread across **track → group → bus** instead of piled on each take.

> **Per-take is deliberately minimal — this is the point, not a gap.** A stack fuses when the *sum* is processed once, not when each take is compressed/saturated/de-essed on its own (per-take character work actively fights fusion — it re-separates the voices). So each layer only gets **tune → align → band-limit → level**. Everything else is distributed downstream:
> - **Compression:** the console/tracking print already applied the CL 1B on the way in (§3); the *glue* comp is one opto over the whole stack on [the group](#/chain/ensemble-stack-group).
> - **Saturation, composite carve EQ, de-ess, shared space** → [Ensemble Stack Group](#/chain/ensemble-stack-group).
> - **Program leveling (UAD Teletronix LA-2A), tone EQ, final de-ess, resonance (Soothe2 — one instance, not per-take), air** → inherited from the [Vocal Bus](#/chain/vocal-bus) the group routes through.
>
> Net: the ensemble runs the *same* full chain the lead does — it's just spread across **track → group → bus** instead of piled on each take.

### 1. Auto-Tune Pro — Pitch
- Every layer to the **same key/scale** (④), **Retune 25** (① — medium). Consistent pitch centers are what make separate takes fuse. Vary retune only subtly; unison/double layers usually take **more aggressive** tuning than a lead so they lock tight — [Sage Audio](https://www.sageaudio.com/articles/how-to-stack-vocals). Harmony layers follow the harmony line, not the melody.
- **Why:** First so everything downstream reacts to corrected, matched pitch.

### 2. VocAlign Project 5 AU — Timing (the master width/fusion knob)
- **Doubles align to the take they're doubling** (not to one global reference) so each pair reads as one thick voice. For a fused unison ensemble with no source take, pick one layer as the reference and align the rest to it.
- **Tighter alignment = more fused / mono-leaning; looser = wider, more natural ensemble.** This single control largely decides Variant A vs B on the group. Leave the octave anchor and air layers unaligned (their register already separates them).
- **Why:** Timing consistency does more for the single-source illusion than any EQ or comp move. Manual/aligned timing beats leaving it to chance — [Sage Audio](https://www.sageaudio.com/articles/how-to-stack-vocals).
- *(Owned substitute for VocAlign Ultra AU, which hangs Live on automated load — Project 5 does the same align-a-dub-to-a-guide job. If it also stalls, fall back to manual: warp each take's transients to the reference, or use Melodyne's time tool.)*

### 3. Pro-Q 4 — Band-limit (role-dependent)
- **Core/doubles:** HPF ~80–120 Hz (stacking builds low mud); gentle LPF only if harsh.
- **Octave-down anchor:** HPF *lower* (keep its weight, ~40–60 Hz) but carve any boom; it lives under everything.
- **Octave-up / air / whisper:** HPF *higher* (~150–300 Hz) so they sit as sheen above the core without adding mud.
- Keep moves small and roughly identical *within* a role.
- **Why:** Clears the summed low-end buildup and slots each role in its own register before the group glue comp.

### 4. Level-match (clip gain, per the chosen philosophy)
- **Fused ensemble:** clip-gain every core/double layer so **none dominates** — a composite, not a stack-with-a-winner.
- **Lead + support:** the lead sits at reference; supporting layers tuck under it, and **octave layers land ~−8 to −12 dB below** ("felt more than heard") — [Twisby](https://twisbyrecords.com/post/how-to-layer-vocals-like-a-pro/).

### 5. Keep per-layer color minimal (two optional exceptions)
- No per-layer **saturation/character** passes on core/double layers — similar tone + one shared space (on the group) is what reads as a single source. (Deliberate degradation belongs on *backups*, not a fused ensemble.)
- **Optional — gentle per-take leveler:** if a take is *wildly* dynamic, a light Pro-C 2 (2–3 dB GR, fast-ish) *after* clip-gain evens it before it hits the group glue comp. Keep it subtle — clip-gain does most of the work, and a heavy per-take comp fights fusion.
- **Optional — light per-take de-ess before the group:** for very sibilant stacks, a gentle Pro-DS on each take *and* the composite de-ess on the group is the "de-ess before AND after" move (Disclosure's group-vocal approach — [Backup Vocals Group](#/chain/backup-vocals-group)). Only reach for it when the single group de-ess can't tame the stacked S's.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

Usually nothing per layer — fusion and character come from the group. Resist adding per-layer color; it pulls a layer out of the composite.

- **Exception — specific-word delay throws.** When *one word or phrase* should catch/repeat, that's a **per-layer** move, not a group send: drag the word to a dedicated effects/throw track with a **loud EchoBoy insert** (high end cut, subdivision per throw), or automate a delay send on just that layer for that moment. Ambient/glue delay for the *whole* stack stays a shared group send — see [Ensemble Stack Group](#/chain/ensemble-stack-group) `## Delay / echo`.

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Ensemble layers → [Ensemble Stack Group](#/chain/ensemble-stack-group) → [Vocal Bus](#/chain/vocal-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)** — "the group has the chain." Every layer stays dry; the glue, saturation, de-ess, and the shared reverb + delay sends all live on the group so the whole stack sits in identical space and treatment. The only per-layer time-based FX is a deliberate word-throw (§5).

## Variations

- The layer-role menu, the two philosophies (fused vs lead+support), and the three width treatments all live on [Ensemble Stack Group](#/chain/ensemble-stack-group). The per-layer levers that feed them are the **VocAlign Project 5 AU tightness** (§4.2) and **role-based HPF/level** (§4.3–4.4).

## Sources

Kuk Harrell stack discipline (via [FX Chain System](#/chains/system)). Layering best practice: [Sage Audio — How to Stack Vocals](https://www.sageaudio.com/articles/how-to-stack-vocals), [Twisby — 7 Layers You Need to Record](https://twisbyrecords.com/post/how-to-layer-vocals-like-a-pro/), [Synchro Arts — Vocal Layering](https://www.synchroarts.com/posts/vocal-layering). Self-stack references: Bon Iver "Holocene", Imogen Heap, HAIM, gospel self-stacks. Spec: `spec-131-ensemble-vocal-stack-chains`.

chains.title: Harmony Vocal Track
chains.routing: Harmony Vocal → Main Vocal Group → Vocal Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Harmony parts around the lead (3rds/5ths/6ths), pushed further back in the depth field. Harmonies carry *pitch information, not tone* — strip everything that isn't the note.

**Chain philosophy:** tune → tightest EQ of the stack → compress flat → de-ess → wide + wet.

## 1 — Recording Setup

- Same setup as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §1: Neumann TLM 102, ghost latency track.
- Sung **softer than the lead**, same mic position as the lead session for fused timbre.

## 2 — Tracking Best Practice

- **Pan L/R pairs at ~35–42 L/R** (Live's 0–50 scale) — just *inside* hard-panned doubles so layers don't stack on the same spot (no doubles in the section? harmonies can take the outside). **Block harmonies come in fours** (L/R per note), each note balanced to the chord.
- **Time-align to the lead, keep their own pitch** — harmonies match *timing* (manually or VocAlign Ultra AU) but never pitch-match to the lead's notes.
- 🎬 **Blend later stack layers down in level for balance, rather than matching the first pair at full strength.** After the first two stacks are level-matched and mono-checked while tracking (see [1 Double Vocal Track](#/chain/double-vocal-track)), a third/fourth note gets pulled down slightly — "this particular note is blended down just a little bit because [they] have to be balanced properly" — the level-matching discipline is for judging the blend honestly, not for the final print level of every layer — Kuk Harrell (Mix with the Masters), Creating vocal stacks with Kuk Harrell.
- 🎬 **Fifthy/medieval harmonies are a flavor** — Khalid's "very fifthy, quite medieval-sounding" stacks; parallel fifths break the rules and sound modern — Disclosure, [Making Beats + Talk](https://youtu.be/1GhqAf9lc3A).
- 🎬 Consider **more tune on harmonies than the main** when the singer is reaching (Smino logic) — Kenny Beats, [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c).

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD Console)

Same console pass as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §3, printed conservatively.

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

**From the [Vocal Foundation](#/chain/vocal-foundation) →** keeps the skeleton (tune → corrective EQ → level) and pushes it toward *tightest, flattest, and wettest* of the whole stack — harmonies carry pitch info, not tone. The deltas:
- **Retune 45–50 → 22** · **scale set to the harmony's notes**, not song-key chromatic (§4.1)
- **Corrective HPF/cut → the tightest band-limit of any vocal** (§4.2 — HPF 200–300, LPF 7–9k; keep only the band the note lives in)
- **Leveling 3–5 dB → flatten 6–10 dB** (§4.3 — pad-like sustain, "a synth pad made of voice")
- **Drop Soothe2; add an aggressive Pro-DS** (§4.4 — stacked sibilance adds up fast)
Character is *deferred, not declined*: the harmony earns its own seat later via the texture-split brightness in §5 and running wetter/wider than the lead in §6.

### 1. Auto-Tune Pro — Pitch
- **Retune 22** (①) · **Humanize 100%** (③) · **scale set carefully** (④ — the harmony's notes, not just song-key chromatic).

### 2. Pro-Q 4 — Tightest band-limit
- HPF 200–300 Hz · LPF 7–9 kHz · dip lead presence 3–5 kHz −2 to −3 dB
- **Why:** Keep only the band where the harmony note actually lives.

### 3. Pro-C 2 — Flatten
- 4:1 · **6–10 dB GR** · release auto
- **Why:** Even pad-like sustain — harmonies behave like a synth pad made of voice.

### 4. Pro-DS — De-ess
- Aggressive — stacked sibilance from multiple takes adds up fast.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- **Texture split trick:** EQ harmonies **brighter/airier** when the doubles went warm (or vice versa); give a second harmony layer its own flavor (a little Decapitator + chorus smear) — different textures = each layer gets its own seat.

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Harmony Vocal → [Main Vocal Group](#/chain/main-vocal-group) → [Vocal Bus](#/chain/vocal-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)** — dry tracks, chain on the group.

- **More [Reverb Send Room](#/chain/reverb-send-room)/[Reverb Send Long](#/chain/reverb-send-long) AND more delay than the lead** — harmonies run wetter on purpose; depth = behind. [Width Send](#/chain/width-send) for spread on big hooks.
- **Delay treatment:** the extra delay is **cohesion delay via the shared group send** ([Delay Send Slap](#/chain/delay-send-slap)/[Delay Send Other](#/chain/delay-send-other), hotter than the lead), sidechain-ducked to the lead → Sidechaining so the wetness blooms in gaps and tucks under words. A one-word harmony catch = a throw-track EchoBoy insert, not a per-note delay on this track. Cohesion → group send · moment → insert.

## Variations

- **Beatles block harmonies:** less tune (retune 40+), LALA instead of Pro-C 2, mono-ish placement, drier — the blend comes from the takes.
- **Pad harmonies (ooh/aah beds):** treat as [Synth Bed Track](#/chain/synth-bed-track) — heavier LPF, long reverb, sidechain-duck under the lead. 🎬 **Non-singer-friendly build method:** record (or reuse) a single sustained tone with variation minimized, pan it center, then duplicate and pitch-shift copies to different scale degrees to build the harmonic backdrop — the pitching does the harmonic work, not vocal performance, so it doesn't require an actual multi-note take. A rough demo tone is enough raw material to start from. — Synthet, [All producers should do this](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8t3Ep4e_dyE)
- 🎬 **Synthesized harmonies (Henry Saiz method):** skip singing the harmony takes entirely — route a MIDI chord/melody track → vocoder (lead vocal as modulator) → a MIDI-playable vocal synth (Neptune's "voice synth" mode) as the carrier, so playing the chord track live re-pitches the vocal into a harmony stack. Keep the lead vocal itself minimally processed (light multiband comp + delay/reverb only) so it reads as distinct from the synthesized layer underneath — same BED Slot role as a pad harmony, but MIDI-controllable instead of comped from takes. Nate doesn't own a MIDI-playable vocal synth yet — see Plugin Wishlist. — Henry Saiz, [How Henry Saiz gets crazy vocal effects](https://youtu.be/tzS2ogFszuI)

## From videos

- 🎬 **A full-mix AlterBoy-based harmony chain, run wetter/heavier than the lead's on purpose:** built as the second of a two-line vocal stack, this layer runs Little AlterBoy's "vocal chorus" preset → EQ → AlterBoy again (formant shifted down, mix 100%, Drive boosted) → ValhallaVintageVerb's dark vocal room preset (size down, mix ~90). No pitch shift at all on this layer — unlike the main vocal's pitched-up/50%-mix ghost double, this harmony gets full-strength character processing plus a reverb tail, consistent with harmonies running wetter/further back than the lead (see §6 above). → Little AlterBoy, ValhallaVintageVerb, Pitch and Formant — loner, [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo)

## Sources

Same source set as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) · Disclosure — [Making Beats + Talk](https://youtu.be/1GhqAf9lc3A) · Kenny Beats — [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c) · Henry Saiz — [How Henry Saiz gets crazy vocal effects](https://youtu.be/tzS2ogFszuI) · loner — [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo) · Kuk Harrell (Mix with the Masters) — Creating vocal stacks with Kuk Harrell

chains.title: Main Vocal High Track
chains.routing: Main Vocal (high) → Main Vocal Group → Vocal Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** High lead layer (octave-up or high harmony that reinforces the lead). Sits *with* the lead in the center — tucked under it, never competing. A support layer earns its place by being *narrower and more controlled* than the lead.

**Chain philosophy:** tune tighter → band-limit harder → compress flatter → de-ess.

## 1 — Recording Setup

- Same setup as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §1: Neumann TLM 102, ghost latency track, tempo/key locked.
- Falsetto/octave-up parts sit closer to the mic's sweet spot at lower level — drop input gain ~3 dB so the thin register doesn't ride the preamp hot.

## 2 — Tracking Best Practice

- **Track it right after the lead take it supports**, same mic position — matched timbre fuses; a different session's tone reads as a separate voice.
- Sing softer than the lead; the layer is reinforcement, not a feature. 🎬 Set Auto-Tune Pro's **input voice type to the register actually sung** (Soprano for falsetto) or the tracking misreads — Kenny Beats, [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c).
- Center, mono — width belongs to doubles/harmonies.

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD Console)

Same console pass as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) §3, printed conservatively.

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

### 1. Auto-Tune Pro — Pitch
- **Retune 22** (①) · **Humanize 100%** (③) · **input voice type = register actually sung** (④ — Soprano for falsetto) — tighter than the lead
- **Why:** High layers expose pitch drift; tighter tune keeps it fused.

### 2. Pro-Q 4 — Band-limit
- HPF up to 150–200 Hz · LPF/high-shelf cut above 10–12 kHz · dip the lead's presence zone (3–5 kHz) −1 to −2 dB
- **Why:** The lead keeps the full range; this layer keeps a narrower window so they never fight.

### 3. Pro-C 2 — Flatten
- 4:1 · attack 5–10 ms · release auto · **4–8 dB GR** — more than the lead
- **Why:** Support layers want near-zero dynamics so they sit still under the lead.

### 4. Pro-DS — De-ess
- Harder than the lead (range 6–8 dB) — stacked S's multiply.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- Nothing, usually — invisibility is the job.

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Main Vocal High → [Main Vocal Group](#/chain/main-vocal-group) → [Vocal Bus](#/chain/vocal-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)** — dry track, chain on the group.

- Share the lead's reverb/delay sends at slightly *higher* send levels — pushes the layer back in depth.
- **Delay:** cohesion delay via the shared group send (a touch hotter than the lead for depth), sidechain-ducked with the lead so tails sit behind → Sidechaining. A specific-word throw stays an insert on a dedicated throw track (EchoBoy), never this track's send. Cohesion → group send · moment → insert.
- 🎬 *From video:* on a hook/chorus this layer can also be pushed hard and *audible* rather than tucked-back cohesion — a large-room ValhallaRoom verb, deliberately heavy, as a featured chorus-uplift effect, not glue. This is the exception to "invisibility is the job" above, reserved for a chorus moment — Kevin Davis (Mix with the Masters), [Mixing Vocals from 'Dancing With A Stranger' with Kevin Davis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQIZONdZvk8)

## Variations

- **Falsetto pad use:** widen with [Width Send](#/chain/width-send) and pan a recorded pair L/R instead of center.
- **Trap octave layer:** hard-tune (retune 0–10) + more [Saturation Send](#/chain/saturation-send).

## From videos

- **Octave-up doubled vocal drenched in a large room reverb as a deliberate, audible chorus-uplift effect — the opposite of this track's usual "invisibility is the job" treatment.** On Sam Smith's chorus ("Dancing With A Stranger"): "there was this high octave vocal verbed out, we used the large room — that's just his vocal, octaved up... nothing major, just to uplift the chorus slightly." Paired against a Vocoder treatment on the song's second lead vocalist for the same job (uplift the chorus) but a deliberately different color — "it's just a different color for the chorus." *(qualitative only — no decay/mix given)* → ValhallaRoom, Vocoder, Reverb (effect) — Kevin Davis (Mix with the Masters), [Mixing Vocals from 'Dancing With A Stranger' with Kevin Davis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQIZONdZvk8)

## Sources

Same source set as [Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track) · Kenny Beats — [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c) · Kevin Davis (Mix with the Masters) — [Mixing Vocals from 'Dancing With A Stranger' with Kevin Davis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQIZONdZvk8)

chains.title: Main Vocal Track
chains.routing: Main Vocal → Main Vocal Group → Vocal Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** The lead. Center, loudest vocal element — everything else in the vocal stack supports it.

**Chain philosophy:** tune → corrective EQ → leveling comp → resonance tame → color → tone EQ → de-ess → air. Corrective before compression, saturation after compression, de-ess near the end (sibilance is shaped by everything before it).

## 1 — Recording Setup

- **Mic:** Neumann TLM 102, shock mount, pop filter ~4" out, 48V on. Room: phone silenced, fan/HVAC off (or Gate at −40 dB in the monitor chain to clear what's left — Kenny's number).
- 🎬 *From video:* a singer's own mic technique can do most of the tracking compressor's job before the signal ever reaches it — Al Schmitt's vocal chain barely engaged compression at all because the singer "leans in and backs off" (proximity effect, self-managed live) — "makes my life so much easier." Worth checking for on any singer before assuming §3's CL 1B stage needs to work hard: good mic discipline at the source means lighter GR downstream, not a settings problem to chase. → Vocal Mic Technique, UAD Neve 1073 — Al Schmitt (Mix with the Masters), Recording techniques with Al Schmitt
- 🎬 *From video:* pick the mic to add warmth on an already-good singer, not just to correct a weak one — a distinct rationale from this note's own condenser-for-detail framing. Go-to pair: Sony C800 or Elam 251, chosen specifically "because it has warmth to it" on singers already strong enough to sing with minimal correction. Owned equivalent: TLM 102. → Vocal Mic Technique — Kuk Harrell, Radio-ready vocal effects with Kuk Harrell
- **Before anyone sings: lock the TEMPO and the KEY** — wrong tempo = un-loopable stems and a session reset mid-take; unknown key = no Auto-Tune Pro when someone asks. Find the key at a piano if nobody knows it — Kenny Beats, [Recording Vocals the Right Way](https://youtu.be/3Nw1d37nluo).
- **Latency:** buffer **128** (64 if the machine allows), driver error compensation to ~0 ms, Pro-Q 4 in Zero Latency mode while tracking — see Latency-Free Tracking. (Monitoring through UAD Console sidesteps this; the settings matter when the monitor chain runs in Ableton.)
- **Track vocals in a separate session from the beat** — bounce the beat to a 2-track first: CPU stays fast at low buffer, and the bounce commits you ("imperfections you were gonna fix end up making the song") — Kenny Beats, [Vocal Template](https://youtu.be/X_iDENABLmk).
- **Monitoring:** Audio-Technica ATH-M50x closed-back. Interface: Universal Audio Apollo Twin MkII, peaks −12 dBFS, average ~−18 (Gain Staging).
- 🎬 *From video:* put a heavy "slappy" delay on the monitor chain BEFORE the vocal is written/tracked, not after — the singer performs against the audible repeats and the delay shapes actual phrasing/syllable placement, not just space added later. Finneas on Billie Eilish's "Birds of a Feather": she "was able to sing with that while we were writing the song and have the delay to feed off of." → Delay (effect) — Finneas, Behind the Track - 'BIRDS OF A FEATHER' by Billie Eilish

## 2 — Tracking Best Practice

- **Record every take on TWO tracks at once** — the monitored FX track *and* a ghost **latency track** (zero plugins, monitor off, out to a spare hardware pair, not the master). Keep the ghost take — it lands on the grid; drag it into [Main Vocal Group](#/chain/main-vocal-group), which carries the chain — Kenny Beats, [Recording Without Latency](https://youtu.be/Gj4_IvHFn6g) → Latency-Free Tracking.
- 🎬 *From video:* a related dual-channel variant with a different purpose — an "auxiliary input" setup where one channel carries the plain take (the actual keeper, what gets comped/edited) and a second channel carries a live-autotuned/processed monitor feed used only to judge in the moment whether more takes are needed, never as the edited source. Stated side benefit: the setup keeps the control room quiet during takes instead of interrupting the singer to react to each pass — see Vocal Mic Technique. → Latency-Free Tracking — Mix with the Masters (Andrés Torres and Mauricio Rengifo), Vocal production with Andrés Torres and Mauricio Rengifo
- **Mono, one lead.** Doubles/harmonies/ad-libs are their own chains ([Double Vocal Track](#/chain/double-vocal-track), [Harmony Vocal Track](#/chain/harmony-vocal-track), [Backup Vocal Track](#/chain/backup-vocal-track)) — don't stack on the lead track.
- **"Do enough takes, you can make it sound good"** — Howard Lawrence's comping confidence rule (it made SG Lewis a singer); 3–5 takes then comp, don't chase the perfect single take.
- **Different mics for different SECTIONS** — build hook-vs-verse contrast at the source: Disclosure cut a hook into a harmonica mic (crushed lo-fi) with clean upfront verses, and Lavender's released lead is an **SM-58 → Distressor → distortion** ("it sounds banging"). Owned lo-fi lane: Shure SM57 → UAD UA 1176LN slammed → Decapitator — [ENERGY Release Party](https://youtu.be/fMqPuf1UVzI).
- **Playback psychology:** make the group chain slightly nicer than the headphone chain — artists hear the drag-down sounding *better* than the take felt and push harder — Kenny Beats, [New Vocal Chain 2022](https://youtu.be/-SvBNOBWJ_8).
- 🎬 *From video:* 070 Shake tracks full continuous takes and explicitly avoids comping — redoes the WHOLE take rather than punching in, aiming for "one expression and one flow" (a harder-line version of the "do enough takes" rule above: no fragment-assembly at all) → Vocal Comping and Takes — Mix with the Masters, [Behind the Track｜'Elephant' by 070 Shake](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OKBT8-0l9AI)
- 🎬 *From video:* don't stop a singer to chase "the perfect take" — let them sing the same phrase repeatedly (stated as seven times) without commentary, unless there's something genuinely specific to correct. "It becomes a beautiful process if you make it something mechanical, singing that part seven times without needing to correct it, unless you need to tell them something specific." If the singer "has the magic," the right take arrives on its own; repeated generic notes are framed as worse than just letting more passes happen. Named tradeoff: this whole approach takes LONGER overall than recording to a single mixed channel, because of the extra comping pass it creates — worth it for how it treats the singer. → Vocal Comping and Takes — Mix with the Masters (Andrés Torres and Mauricio Rengifo), Vocal production with Andrés Torres and Mauricio Rengifo

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD Console)

Printed on the way in — conservative, because printed is forever.

### 1. UAD Neve 1073 — Unison preamp
- The pop/rock vocal classic — mid-forward weight and silk. Gain into gentle color, level to ~0 VU
- **Alt:** UAD UA 610-B for rounder tube warmth on soft/ballad vocals.

### 2. UAD Tube-Tech CL 1B mkII — Tracking compressor
- Ratio ~2:1–3:1 · attack **fast**, release **slow/auto** (the mkII's fixed-attack/release plus manual mode) · **2–4 dB GR** — a smooth opto *ride*, not a peak grab (Kenny's rule: "never past 7 on the needle, 10 is really pushing it")
- This is an **optical/tube leveler** going in — it rides the whole phrase like a fader and prints tube warmth + silk, where the old 1176 caught fast transients. Let the opto do the gentle glue; the fast peak-precision now lives on Pro-C 2 in Ableton (§4.3).
- mkII extras worth using on the way in: **sidechain HP filter** so low-end doesn't pump the gain, and keep **wet/dry mix ~100%** (parallel is a mix-phase move, not a print move).
- 🎬 *From video:* a concrete recipe for this exact stage from a UAD-interface tracking chain — Release **Medium/Medium-fast**, Attack **Medium/Medium-slow** (song-dependent), **Threshold left alone, level controlled entirely via Input drive**, targeting only slight needle movement: bumps to ~−1 dB, peaks −3 to −7 dB at the very most ("I'm not looking for crazy −10, −20... just a healthy movement"). Monitored live with reverb + a delay on a secondary Aux while tracking, so the take is sung against real space from the first pass. → Latency-Free Tracking, [The Weeknd Vocal Chain](#/chain/the-weeknd-vocal-chain) — Illangelo (Mix with the Masters), Producing The Weeknd's vocals with Illangelo
### 3. UAD Pultec EQP-1A — Broad EQ
- Low ATTEN 1–2 @ 60–100 Hz (rumble) · +1–2 dB @ 12 kHz air, bandwidth broad · print conservatively — tone-shaping happens in Ableton.
- 🎬 *From video:* a contrasting case where the Pultec instead **boosts** ~100 Hz hard rather than attenuating — used to put analog richness back into a voice an earlier in-the-box parallel-double stage had already thinned out, then feeds a fast-attack/fast-release 1176 downstream so the compressor reacts to the boosted bass response too (not just peaks). Only reach for this on a chain that's genuinely thinned the source first — it's compensation, not a default. → UAD UA 1176LN, Compression Staging, BASS Slot — Mix with the Masters (Ben Baptie), Julian Casablancas' vocal sound with Ben Baptie

**While tracking, the Ableton monitor chain is lean:** Gate (−40 to −43 dB, room noise between phrases) → light EQ → nothing latent. The "sound-good-izer" lift stays OFF until the song is done — it adds latency and character artists get used to — Kenny Beats, [Vocal Template](https://youtu.be/X_iDENABLmk).

## Prep — before any plugin (between tracking and mixing)

- **Clip-gain the comp to ~0 VU / −18 dBFS average** — pull the big volume jumps down by hand first; the compressor then works on musical dynamics, and every analog-modeled plugin gets its calibrated level.
- **Chop out ALL dead space between phrases** (keep natural breaths, never clip word edges) — every compressor downstream raises the floor of whatever you leave; uncut room noise across stacked tracks is why "the vocal feels muddy on the beat." **Editing is gain-staging** — Kenny Beats, [Recording Vocals the Right Way](https://youtu.be/3Nw1d37nluo).
- Edit pops, mouth noise, big breaths; nail timing; manual pitch surgery (Melodyne-level) *before* the chain — no plugin fixes a sloppy comp.
- Flip Pro-Q 4 instances from Zero Latency to **Natural Phase** now that tracking is done — Kenny Beats, [Vocal Template](https://youtu.be/X_iDENABLmk).

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

**From the [Vocal Foundation](#/chain/vocal-foundation) →** the lead is the **reference the foundation was carved out of**, so its front is the block *verbatim, at neutral defaults* — §4.1–4.4 (Auto-Tune @ Retune 45–50, corrective Pro-Q, Pro-C 2 leveling, Soothe2) **are** the Vocal Foundation with nothing overridden. Where the other roles bend or decline the block, the lead is the one part that then runs the **full character/tone/air tail**: §4.5 Saturn 2 color → §4.6 Pro-Q 4 tone boosts → §4.7 Pro-DS finishing de-ess → §4.8 Gem Dopamine air. It gets the complete chain because everything else in the stack is built to support it.

### 1. Auto-Tune Pro — Pitch
- Key/scale: match song (④) · **Retune 45** (① — natural pop; ~50 is the proven "invisible" default, 30–35 tighter) · **Humanize 100%** (③) · **Flex-Tune 0** (②) · **input voice type set to the voice** (④)
- The retune map: **~30–40 = invisible support** ("spotting you while you bench") · **~7 = deliberately audible** (Travis/Migos/Greedo bite) · **>10–12 = full T-Pain chip**. Kenny's alternative: Humanize 0, naturalness from low retune + **Legato** style — pick ONE philosophy per song. And set the **input voice type** (Low Male/Alto/Soprano — a range switch) or the tracking misreads everything — [Auto-Tune Process](https://youtu.be/dyr6F9DLG7c)
- Pro move: scale on Chromatic, remove out-of-key notes on the keyboard (advanced view) — per-note control for borrowed notes.
- **Why:** First in chain so everything downstream reacts to corrected pitch.
- 🎬 *From video:* 070 Shake & Dave have pulled Auto-Tune back further than ever for a rawer vocal, pairing minimal correction with almost no other vocal FX ("it's really just how she sounds") → Vocal Tuning — Mix with the Masters, [Behind the Track｜'Elephant' by 070 Shake](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OKBT8-0l9AI)
- 🎬 *From video:* strip tuning off ONE specific section (not the whole vocal) for a raw, spoken quality against a bigger, corrected chorus — "take the tune off of the first verse... it should just feel so raw it sounds like she's just speaking," breaths kept in on purpose → Vocal Tuning — Mix with the Masters (Benny Blanco & Selena Gomez), [Behind the Track｜'Younger And Hotter Than Me' by Selena Gomez & benny blanco](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rkJ-LaoArUY)

### 2. Pro-Q 4 — Corrective EQ
- HPF 24 dB/oct @ 80–100 Hz · cut mud −2 to −4 dB @ 200–400 Hz (narrow-ish) · check 2–5 kHz for harshness/nasality
- **Why:** Cuts before compression so the comp doesn't fight rumble and mud.
- 🎬 *From video:* trim a touch of low end even on a vocal meant to stay rich — "I'm getting a little bit of a low end thing, even though I want his voice to be rich, I'm taking a little bit of that off." Richness and low-end control as two separate axes: keep the body, trim the excess underneath it. *(general starting point — no Hz/dB given)* → EQ (effect), BASS Slot — Chris Lord-Alge (Mix with the Masters), Chris Lord-Alge processing vocals
- 🎬 *From video:* aggressive, repeated narrow-Q ("tight Q's") notching by ear to dig out harsh, ear-piercing resonances — "don't be afraid... go in there and find those frequencies that are harsh and pierce into your ear, find them, and pull them out... I'm not afraid to notch multiple times if I have to, whatever it takes." Framed as a loud-playback-safety move (a spiky frequency "kills" the ear when played loud), not just tone-shaping. One problem zone named but garbled by captions — roughly **~2.2–2.8 kHz**. → EQ (effect), De-essing, Masking and Carving — Mix with the Masters (Stuart White), Mixing vocals in the box with Stuart White

### 3. Pro-C 2 — Leveling compression
- Style: Vocal · attack 10 ms · release auto · **3–5 dB GR** · range slider caps GR at ~5 dB so it can't overreact
- **Why:** Second-stage leveler (the CL 1B at tracking was stage one). The CL 1B is a slow opto that rides the *program*; Pro-C 2 set fast catches the quick transients the opto lets through — two complementary curves, which is exactly why staged compression sounds smoother than one deep comp (Compression Staging).

### 4. Soothe2 — Resonance suppression
- **Soft mode** · default sharpness/selectivity (~3) · raise depth until clearly working, back off slightly · focus 1–6 kHz · delta mode to hear what it's removing
- **Why:** Dynamic harshness control static EQ can't do; before saturation so you're not exciting resonances.

### 5. Saturn 2 — Color
- **Warm Tape or Warm Tube** (③), **single band** (①) · **Drive ~15%** (② — low) · **Mix 30%** (⑤ — 20–40% window)
- **Why:** Density + harmonics so the vocal reads on small speakers. After compression = consistent drive level.
- 🎬 *From video:* a contrasting order worth knowing — an unnamed "warmth" stage run FIRST/early instead, subtle enough that toggling it on/off is the only way to hear it: "it kind of got forward a little bit, and it gave it a little bit of warmth. It's subtle, but it's nice." One stage in a deliberately gradual, many-plugins-each-doing-a-little-thing chain rather than this note's own after-compression placement — no product/settings named. → Saturation and Distortion, Compression Staging — Mix with the Masters (Stuart White), Mixing vocals in the box with Stuart White

### 6. Pro-Q 4 — Tone EQ (additive)
- Presence +1–2 dB @ 3–5 kHz · air shelf +1–2 dB @ 10 kHz+
- 🎬 *Carve, don't just boost:* the original "Help Me Lose My Mind" boosted vocal highs **+12 dB** ("psychopath stuff"). Keep this move **small (+2–3 dB), dynamic mode** so it de-esses as it lifts; lean on subtractive EQ for the rest, and get air from **Gem Dopamine** (adds highs *with* compression/de-ess) rather than a raw shelf — Disclosure, [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU).
- **Why:** Boosts after compression/saturation — shape the finished texture.
- 🎬 *From video:* a simpler, fixed 3-band alternate recipe run identically on every singer — high shelf ~10 kHz for air, small mid bump, small third band, "all I need is just high-end." Deliberately non-diagnostic (same three moves regardless of the voice) — a fallback when there's no time to tailor per-singer. → EQ (effect) — Kuk Harrell, Radio-ready vocal effects with Kuk Harrell

### 7. Pro-DS — De-ess
- **Single Vocal mode** · split-band · sidechain filters framed on the S region (~4–8 kHz) · range 4–6 dB · audition button to hear only what's ducked
- **Why:** Late in chain — comp + saturation both push sibilance up. (Wideband + no lookahead = zero latency, safe while tracking.)
- 🎬 *From video:* "some nice, subtle DS" — a light touch, no product/frequency/amount given, logged only to confirm de-essing has a place even in a genre (rock) where the mix goal is deliberately warm/dark rather than pop-bright. → De-essing — Mix with the Masters (Stuart White), Mixing vocals in the box with Stuart White
- 🎬 *From video:* a tape machine can do this stage's job as a side effect of its own saturation/EQ character, via a named preset, rather than a dedicated de-esser — Studer A800, "Pop" setting, chosen specifically to make a background-role lead vocal thinner while de-essing it at the same time. Owned equivalent: Kramer Tape dialed toward thin/bright. → Kramer Tape, Plugin Wishlist, [Tony Maserati Vocal Chain](#/chain/tony-maserati-vocal-chain) — Tony Maserati (Mix with the Masters), Vocal chain with Tony Maserati
- 🎬 *From video:* a **layered two-de-esser** discipline worth adopting on a busy chain — one plugin does the heavy lifting (an unowned Eiosis E2 Deesser gets the video's single strongest endorsement: "nothing does what this de-esser does... it's my first choice" — see Plugin Wishlist), then a SECOND, lighter de-esser runs later in the chain purely as touch-up, "chipping away at any syllables or sibilances" the first stage missed — explicitly not doing the heavy lifting itself. Maps onto this note's own §7 as: Pro-DS does the primary pass, a second light Pro-DS instance (or a dynamic Pro-Q 4 band) mops up after later chain stages (Saturn 2, tone EQ) have had a chance to reintroduce sibilance. ### 8. Gem Dopamine — Final air (optional)
- **Wet 30–40%** (① — how much Dolby-A-style sheen the encoder adds) · **Compression** engaged (② — the dynamic/de-ess action that keeps the added air off the S's) · **Frequency/Tone** focused on the top octave (③) · **Mix** to taste (④) · **Model** (⑤) — audition both emulated units, they're voiced differently
- **Why:** Dead last so it airs the *finished* texture. Like Fresh Air it's a **dynamic** HF enhancer rather than a static shelf, so the lift tracks the program and reads as sheen instead of harshness. The reason it's here **instead of Fresh Air**: Gem Dopamine has its own compression/de-ess stage built into the air circuit, so the enhancement self-polices sibilance — which matters at the very end of a chain where §3's compression and §4's saturation have already pushed the S's up. Fresh Air has no such stage, so it needed Pro-DS in §7 to have done a perfect job first.
- **Still skip it entirely if the Pro-Q 4 air shelf in §6 already did the job** — two air stages stack into sibilance fast, dynamic or not.
- 🎬 *From video:* independent confirmation this dedicated-air-band slot is worth having — Illangelo runs Utility into an unnamed EQ (name not captured — the source transcript cuts off before he states it) built around a dedicated **"Air band"** control, boosted gently around **20 kHz**, and calls it his favorite plugin overall — "such beautiful high end frequency content in such a way that I haven't found anything else that comes close to it." Compares it directly, unprompted, to **owned Fresh Air**: "I think Slate Digital might have just released something called Fresh Air... it's fire. This one also does a similar thing." Worth auditioning Fresh Air or Gem Dopamine in this exact "final dedicated air stage after everything else" slot as the owned stand-in. → Fresh Air, EQ (effect), [The Weeknd Vocal Chain](#/chain/the-weeknd-vocal-chain) — Illangelo (Mix with the Masters), Producing The Weeknd's vocals with Illangelo

## Variations

- **Hip hop / trap:** Retune 0–20 (hard tune), 1176-style comp harder (4–6 dB GR), drier — slap delay instead of reverb, more Saturn drive.
- **Beatles / vintage:** skip Auto-Tune or Humanize 100%, swap Saturn for Kramer Tape, LALA instead of Pro-C 2, room reverb up.
- **Lo-fi / crushed:** the SM-58→Distressor lane above, or see [Gorillaz Vocal Chain](#/chain/gorillaz-vocal-chain).

- **One combined reverb+delay plugin standing in for two separate sends, plus a low-end trim and a "tense" compression target — a short in-the-room vocal-packaging demo.** Reverb pulled back to ~5% wet, tested against a "zombie vocal" failure mode (audibly-wet = too much); a short delay tap + a quarter-note tap built inside Waves CLA Epic (unowned) rather than routed to two owned sends, specifically to avoid "trying to build something from scratch"; a touch of low end trimmed off the vocal despite wanting it to stay rich; compression dialed until it reads "tense." No hard numbers beyond the ~5% reverb figure — a workflow/discipline lesson more than a settings recipe. → Reverb (effect), Delay (effect), EQ (effect), Compression (effect), [Reverb Send Room](#/chain/reverb-send-room), [Delay Send Other](#/chain/delay-send-other), Plugin Wishlist — Chris Lord-Alge (Mix with the Masters), Chris Lord-Alge processing vocals
- **Build the whole finished-sounding monitor chain live, in the singer's headphones, while they're tracking — a full worked mic-to-doubler recipe, deliberately kept identical singer to singer.** Chain: mic (Sony C800 or Elam 251, picked for warmth) → Renaissance EQ (fixed 3-band high-end boost, all singers) → Renaissance Compressor (light, peaks only) → RVox (push vocal in front of the track) → sends: R-Verb medium hall + H-Delay quarter-note ping-pong + a basic doubler (subtle width). "When I'm cutting this, he's actually singing to this — so what I'm doing is creating it in his headphone to sound like a finished product, like a mix," which "helps me to dictate the right pocket and everything." Session kept to three sends total (reverb/delay/doubler) specifically so the handoff to the mix engineer needs no cleanup — see Mix Handoff. Stated philosophy behind the fixed, repeatable recipe: "I'm not going on tech, I'm going on emotion." → RVox, Pro-Q 4, Pro-C 2, Pro-R 2, H-Delay, Doubler2, Vocal Mic Technique, Mix Handoff, Latency-Free Tracking — Kuk Harrell, Radio-ready vocal effects with Kuk Harrell
- **A full alternate lead-vocal signal path: a parallel "mult" (driven, thinned, hard-limited duplicate blended under the untouched original) feeding a four-stage analog chain — Pultec (boost) → 1176 (fast/fast) → Tube-Tech CL 1B (slow leveler) → line EQ with only its low-pass filter engaged.** Source vocal handed over completely clean; character built entirely in processing. Two parallel channels run into the console: a milder one (iZotope Trash → an unclear-named compressor, "c62" → EQ → 1176, all in the box) and a far more driven one (an unclear-named distortion/phase-utility plugin, "sanzan," + Waves L1 limiting hard) that becomes a stable mid-range "box" for the voice to sit in without losing its own dynamics — see Parallel Processing, Phase Alignment. The combined signal then runs the analog chain above, closing with a single-purpose LPF-only EQ move to de-hi-fi the top end. Song starts bone dry; the only effect ever used is a slap delay, introduced gradually, chosen specifically to syncopate against tightly-picked rhythm guitar — see Delay (effect), Arrangement and Song Form, Rhythm and Groove. → UAD Pultec EQP-1A, UAD UA 1176LN, UAD Tube-Tech CL 1B mkII, Compression Staging, Saturation and Distortion, Plugin Wishlist — Mix with the Masters (Ben Baptie), Julian Casablancas' vocal sound with Ben Baptie
- **Delay printed into the monitor chain BEFORE the vocal is written, not applied after — the singer performs against the audible repeats and the delay does real compositional work on phrasing.** Billie Eilish's "Birds of a Feather": "there's a lot of delay on her vocal. She was able to sing with that while we were writing the song and have the delay to feed off of." Also on this record: Finneas sings the harmony stack's octave-down layer himself rather than pitch-shifting a copy (see Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs), and Billie was deliberately taught to vocal-engineer/comp her own takes, with the producer leaving the room during tracking (see Vocal Comping and Takes). → Delay (effect), Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs, Vocal Comping and Takes — Finneas, Behind the Track - 'BIRDS OF A FEATHER' by Billie Eilish
- **No comping + pulled-back autotune, in service of a "one expression, one flow" raw-vocal philosophy.** 070 Shake & Dave record full continuous takes (no punch-ins, redo the whole take if a line's off), run close to zero vocal FX, and have "kicked back off the autotune more than we ever have" — three pieces of the same underlying choice to let the performance itself be the sound rather than assembling/correcting one after the fact. → Vocal Comping and Takes, Vocal Tuning — Mix with the Masters (070 Shake & Dave), [Behind the Track｜'Elephant' by 070 Shake](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OKBT8-0l9AI)
- **A pitched-up, formant-down "ghost double" built from a pitch-shift plugin at ~50% mix, instead of a real second take.** EQ boost on the high end for presence, then Little AlterBoy pitched all the way up + Formant brought down + Mix pulled back to ~50% — the shifted copy sits BEHIND the untouched lead rather than replacing it, reading as two vocals from one performance. Kept deliberately unreverbed and subtly blended, unlike the accompanying harmony line's full-mix, reverb-finished AlterBoy chain (see [Harmony Vocal Track](#/chain/harmony-vocal-track)). A cheap doubling alternative to Illangelo's automated-doubler entry below when a second AlterBoy instance is faster than a dedicated doubler plugin. → Little AlterBoy, Pitch and Formant, Layering and Stacking — loner, [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo)
- **"Old broken radio" vocal character: CL 1B for initial control → Decapitator Punish mode (Drive 4, mix backed off) → a hardware Distressor pushed hard specifically to pull up room ambience/movement ("brings out all the underneath, him moving around in the room") → dynamic EQ cutting more lows and boosting high-mids for the radio-box tone → de-essing at the very top of the chain.** The Distressor here is a texture/character move, not just distortion — pushed hard enough to reveal room noise a gentler compressor would miss. → De-essing — Disclosure (Sol State), [In The Studio: Disclosure "My High" breakdown [Twitch]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hOJafQO-LyY)

- **Automated doubler-width as a lead-vocal finisher** — Illangelo runs iZotope Vocal Doubler (owned equivalent: Doubler2) directly on the lead, Dry/Wet automated ~50% → ~90% across the song, so the vocal opens up progressively rather than sitting at one fixed width all the way through — a big part of the "3D" sound across *The Weeknd*'s *After Hours* album — Illangelo, [How Illangelo mixes The Weeknd's vocals](https://youtube.com/shorts/fG2s168La_E?is=dN4ixQppvlexuZOz)
- **Tuning and octave-register both treated as per-SECTION arrangement decisions, not one setting for the whole lead vocal.** "Younger and Hotter Than Me": tuning stripped from the first verse only ("take the tune off... it should just feel so raw it sounds like she's just speaking," breaths kept in), then the lead is placed "down the octave in the first verse, up the octave in the second verse" — two independent per-section moves building a raw-to-big arc across the song. A separate bridge-only pass builds deliberate density on a raw/borrowed vocal fragment: distortion (Saturn 2) → delay/reverb (Lair + others) → Vocoder, then everything but the vocal is cut away. → Vocal Tuning, Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs, Saturation and Distortion — Mix with the Masters (Benny Blanco & Selena Gomez), [Behind the Track｜'Younger And Hotter Than Me' by Selena Gomez & benny blanco](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rkJ-LaoArUY)

## Sources
