- 🎬 **Sample one good note and pitch it around** when a synth won't track evenly across the keyboard; add a **rim on top for attack** ("three notes but it gels") — Disclosure, [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU). Go-to synth-bass sounds: Sound Selection Guide.
- 🎬 **Tune the reinforcement devices to the note, not just the patch** — on an Operator/Serum FM/synth bass, two or three Saturator instances each tuned (Color section's Freq) to the note's own fundamental (then an octave up), plus Corpus tuned to the same sub frequency, thickens the fundamental before any EQ/comp stage even runs — a free pre-tuned rack version exists. Full escalation ladder (parallel high-passed harmonic layer, multiband glue, a tuned phase disperser, grit, duplicate) on Bass Design — dnksaus, [Tighten Your Sub Bass with CORPUS (Not Clickbait) \[I Swear\]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=260MHJtu0pc)

- 🎬 **Speed-run alternative to the full sound-design ladder above: one deep-bass one-shot + a simple root-following line, beefed up with just three stock devices.** For a UK garage beat, skip synthesis entirely — pick a "super deep bass" one-shot (Oliver's Power Tools kit), write the line as the chord roots only, then OTT (multiband: Depth down from default, low boosted, high cut, some mids cut) → MicroShift (light, for chorus-like thickening, not width) → EQ Eight (cut at 30 Hz). Three devices instead of the tuned-Saturator/Corpus escalation — reach for this when a fast, simple, garage-appropriate bass is the goal rather than a dense sound-design build. → Bass Design — loner, [i combined r&b melodies with uk garage drums to make an insane beat (crazy bounce!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I4-jcoCVdC0)

## 2 — Programming Best Practice

- **Simpler settings for 808s:** set it to *cut itself* so notes never overlap; glide mode for slides; end patterns with a **velocity-0 note** so the tail doesn't carry into the next section. → Simpler — 808 Sample (Choke + Glide)
- **The bassline does the harmony** — over a static melody collage, the 808/bass line walking different roots *implies* the chord changes (Young Chop blueprint; Disclosure literally "harmonize the bassline"). Root-avoidant lines = instant sophistication (the Latch lesson). → Arrangement and Song Form
- **Multiple bass SECTIONS per song** — a synth-bass "Mike Dean section" vs an 808 section, or live bass answering between 808 hits — Kenny Beats, [Trap Drums More Interesting](https://youtu.be/fo-E8dY81Nw)
- **Layering two basses? One frequency band each** — Minimoog-style low (volume automation only) + a squelchy top layer (OBXD lane); "you want each bass in its own frequency spectrum" — Disclosure, [Prince Edit + Talk VIP](https://youtu.be/hOvLf9nX500) → Masking and Carving
- Mono, center — always.

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD front end)

Same 1-record/2-process discipline as external sources, minus the Unison impedance magic — UAD plugins in Ableton acting as the console input, printed to audio when dialed:

### 1. UAD UA 610-B — Preamp plugin
- Light tube drive · ~0 VU (Gain Staging)

### 2. UAD UA 1176LN — Compressor
- 2–3 dB on peaks, or skip — a good 808 sample is already even

### 3. UAD Pultec EQP-1A — EQ
- The low-end trick (boost + atten @ 60) if the 808 needs weight · print gently
- 🎬 Named directly as a go-to low-end EQ for the "sense of bottom" its emulation brings, close to the hardware — used here right after a distortion pass for grit (see Saturn 2 stage below) — Mix with the Masters (Marcella Araica), Blending melodies with Marcella Araica

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Shape
- HPF 25–30 Hz · boost/cut the fundamental to fit the key · **cut where the kick lives** (kick usually owns 50–60 Hz — same pocket logic as [Electric Bass DI Track](#/chain/electric-bass-di-track) stage 5)
- 🎬 On a high, busy bassline with little natural boom: **boost the sub, cut the boxy low-mids ~150 Hz** — Disclosure, [You've Got To Let Go](https://youtu.be/1iRPvK1gaOI)

### 2. Saturn 2 — Harmonics (the 808 make-or-break)
- **Multiband** (① — crossover ~80–100 Hz): sub band **clean/undriven** (②), drive the band above — **Gentle Transformer** type (③) on 350 Hz–2 kHz + small level boost + **a touch of per-band Dynamics squeeze** (④)
- **Heard vs felt:** the sub is *felt*, the mids are *heard*. Turning up the felt costs ~7 dB of headroom; saturating the heard band costs ~1 dB and reads everywhere. Diagnose which is missing first.
- 🎬 The heard band is where **bass-amp fizz** lives — overdrive + Softube-style saturator on top, "like a real bass amp; you miss it when it's gone" (roll super-lows, boost the ~700 Hz–1.5 kHz click) — Disclosure, [Waterfall](https://youtu.be/sL5CG444qwQ). Sub-only bass vanishing on phones? **Octave-up layer purely for 100–200 Hz warmth** — Disclosure, [NO CAP](https://youtu.be/kz5dmb3QdI8) / [You & Me](https://youtu.be/9zsU5Y8r_Ow)
- **Why:** Distorting the whole 808 turns the sub to mud; driving only the mids gives fundamental *plus* audibility. (Optional soft clip after to claw back the last dB.)
- 🎬 A qualitative confirmation of this stage's own thesis from a working mixer: "add distortion to the 808s... it just brings it a nice grit... little tricks that I use to kind of cut things through" — judged primarily on NS-10-style monitors (see Referencing and Translation), then followed by the Pultec stage above for bottom-end warmth — Mix with the Masters (Marcella Araica), Blending melodies with Marcella Araica

### 3. Pro-C 2 — Control
- 4:1 · fast attack · release timed to the gap between notes · **2–4 dB GR**
- **Why:** Every 808 note the same size — low-end evenness matters more than dynamics down here.
- 🎬 **On a pure sine-wave bass specifically, heavy compression is framed as a correction, not just glue: no distortion/harmonics means "each moment at each frequency generates a different volume level," so compression is what makes the note-to-note loudness even — with a bit of perceived definition as a bonus.** *(qualitative — no ratio/threshold survives the source's garbled machine-translated captions)* → Bass Design, Compression Staging — Mosty (Mix with the Masters), Mosty mixing a reggaeton track

### 4. Kickstart 2 — Kick duck (the EDM/pop school)
- **Sync'd to the kick pattern** (②/④ — or Duck_Buddy / Pro-C 2 external sidechain for real triggering) · depth via the **Mix knob** (③ — back off until the pump stops being audible) · **curve = the groove** (①)
- **Stealth mode:** duck **only the lows** (multiband, or SC filtered <150 Hz) — full mix benefit, zero audible pumping
- 🎬 **A reggaeton fourth data point for the no-sidechain school below: skipped entirely, by choice, on a sine-wave sub bass** — the mixer doesn't recall his exact reason, just that "I felt that I didn't need it," favoring a simple, low-processing-count arrangement instead. → Sidechaining, Bass Design — Mosty (Mix with the Masters), Mosty mixing a reggaeton track
- 🎬 **Disclosure's double-sidechain:** gentle wideband (~3–4 dB) + an aggressive **Pro-MB band on the sub only** (~12 dB) — the SUB Slot fully clears the kick while the BASS Slot detail keeps its level — [Deeper](https://youtu.be/SM0FZ58ckVw). Use a **dedicated sidechain trigger track** if extra syncopated kicks would stutter the pump (Sidechaining).
- **The hip hop counter-school (Mixed by Ali + Kenny):** *don't* sidechain — "it pulls the punch out of the 808" / "sidechain as a band-aid is lame." Fix sample pairing + surgical EQ pockets + gate the kick's tail instead; duck only when you like the sound of ducking. Sparse trap → the Ali way; dense four-on-floor → the duck.
- 🎬 **A third school, between the two above: duplicate the kick (with its full processing chain) as the trigger, hand-draw the duck instead of letting a live compressor react, then let Soothe2 catch whatever still leaks through.** Bring the duplicated, fully-processed kick down to sit right under this bass, manually dip the bass's volume around each kick hit, then add Soothe2 on top — triggered by the duplicated kick — to mop up any transient/resonant bleed the manual dip missed. Genre-agnostic per the source ("works for every genre out there"); only the *depth* of the effect changes by genre. Result on the source mix: no audible bass-dip and 4 dB of headroom recovered. → Soothe2, Sidechaining — Jaycen Joshua (Mix with the Masters), [Mixing Summits with Jaycen Joshua](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L6xx7DWKzng)

### 5. Utility — Mono low
- Bass Mono on, ~100–120 Hz
- **Why:** Stereo low end phase-cancels on clubs/vinyl and collapses on phones — subs live in mono, width lives above.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- **EchoBoy motion delay on a driven bass** — keeps a heavily saturated bass from feeling static without softening the distortion (the Monark→Distressor-on-full-red "My Hi" chain; owned drive lane: FETish/Devil-Loc Deluxe pushed hard) — Disclosure, [First Twitch Stream](https://youtu.be/IObzp3OugtY)
- **Chorus-Ensemble only above 200 Hz** (synthwave/pop lane) — keep the sub mono-clean.

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Digital Bass → [Bass Group](#/chain/bass-group) → [Bass Bus](#/chain/bass-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)**.

- Low end gets **no reverb, no width** ([FX Chain System](#/chains/system) rules) · [Saturation Send](#/chain/saturation-send) for parallel dirt if stage 2 isn't enough.

## Variations

- **Long sliding 808s (trap):** Limiter at the end to pin sustain · glide on the instrument, not the chain.
- **Synthwave/pop synth bass:** open the LPF, chorus above 200 Hz, less duck.

## From videos

- **Heavy compression as a loudness-evenness fix on a sine-wave sub bass, plus a data point for skipping the kick sidechain entirely** — see the inline 🎬 notes in §3 (Pro-C 2) and §4 (Kickstart 2) above. → Bass Design, Compression Staging, Sidechaining — Mosty (Mix with the Masters), Mosty mixing a reggaeton track
- **Mix 808 low-end decisions primarily on NS-10-style monitors, add distortion purely for grit/cut-through, then finish with the Pultec for bottom-end warmth** — see the inline 🎬 notes in §4 (Saturn 2) and §3 (Pultec) above. → Saturation and Distortion, UAD Pultec EQP-1A, Referencing and Translation, SUB Slot — Mix with the Masters (Marcella Araica), Blending melodies with Marcella Araica
- **A CS80 one-shot bass, pitched up, pulsed with a ShaperBox volume preset, built around a found a cappella** — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above. → Shaper, Sound Selection Guide, Plugin Wishlist — loner, [we made a crazy r&b trapsoul song!? (making a beat from scratch around an acapella)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=39aHjEJ5-FU)
- **A minimal-effort UK garage bass chain: one deep-bass one-shot, root-following line, then OTT → MicroShift → EQ** — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above. → OTT, MicroShift, EQ Eight, Bass Design — loner, [i combined r&b melodies with uk garage drums to make an insane beat (crazy bounce!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I4-jcoCVdC0)
- **Root-following bassline + pitch-shift-the-whole-take-down fix on Kontakt Scarbee Rickenbacker** — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above. → Kontakt 7, Bassline Writing — loner, [making a soulful afrobeats beat for rema & wizkid from scratch (use voice notes to start ideas!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e-KvnLXHAy4)
- **A "make the run stand out" finishing move: light Decapitator drive + EQ applied ONLY to a pitched-down accent run, not the whole bassline** — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above for the full two-part bass system this belongs to. → Decapitator, EQ — loner, [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo)
- **Root-following Juno-emulation bass + extra bounce notes, written early in the build, plus Decapitator crunch** — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above. → Decapitator, Bass Design, Synthwave — loner, [how to make an 80's synthwave/pop beat for the weeknd.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dWhh27UFWhY)
- **A full "chain it over and over" dubstep bass sound-design pass, built entirely on stock tools:** start from a plain sine wave → drive it through distortion (Saturator/Overdrive) until the waveform's character comes entirely from the processing → a 3-band Multiband Dynamics preset ("Smasher": heavy ratios on low/mid/high) as a faux-OTT stage → automate an EQ band directly for a moving notch/wah character → **bounce/resample the result and keep layering more processing on the printed audio** rather than endlessly tweaking one live chain. Worth knowing: resampling then pitching the bounced tone pitches every baked-in effect (phaser, chorus, distortion) along with the note, not just the pitch — a genuinely different texture than pitching a live synth voice. Build **3 separate layers** for one composite bass (long fuzzy sustained tone / short plucky hit / high screechy top) rather than one patch doing everything; **layer an octave-up duplicate** when the sub feels harmonically thin, and **crank distortion (not EQ) to generate missing harmonics** on a thin sub. → Saturation and Distortion, EQ, EDM Subgenres (Dubstep) — Max Konyi, [How to Make Dubstep in Studio One with Stock Instruments | Weekly Challenge #10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sD3mE-siI5M)
- **Tuned dual/triple Saturator + Corpus for a "thick bass" front end** — the full recipe: two or three Saturator instances each tuned to the played note (fundamental, then an octave up), plus Corpus tuned to the same sub frequency for physically-modeled reinforcement, before any of the usual EQ/comp/duck stages below run. Escalation from there: resample + a parallel high-passed (~150–300 Hz) Saturator layer, Multiband Dynamics + notch EQ, a harmonically-tuned phase disperser + grit, then a Limiter before anything wilder. Full writeup: Bass Design. — dnksaus, [Tighten Your Sub Bass with CORPUS (Not Clickbait) \[I Swear\]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=260MHJtu0pc)
- **808 tuning + slides workflow** — tune the 808 UP an octave+ to hear the note center, then drop it back (never guess at sub pitch); slides on audio 808s: pitch to the note with warp OFF, then warp mode **Tones** + clip transposition envelope and draw the slides — Lophiile, [All About Basslines stream](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tnruvmw_OWc)
## Sources

Disclosure — [Deeper](https://youtu.be/SM0FZ58ckVw) · [Waterfall](https://youtu.be/sL5CG444qwQ) · [NO CAP](https://youtu.be/kz5dmb3QdI8) · [First Twitch Stream](https://youtu.be/IObzp3OugtY) · [Prince Edit + Talk VIP](https://youtu.be/hOvLf9nX500) · Kenny Beats — [808 & Kick + Subtractive EQ](https://youtu.be/4iAKvWWlCvY) · [Beat Mix & Creation](https://youtu.be/FC__hbvnETY) · George T Music (Mixed by Ali) — link in [FX Chain System](#/chains/system)

chains.title: Electric Bass DI Track
chains.routing: Electric Bass DI → Bass Group → Bass Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** DI'd Hofner B-Bass H-Series — the low-end foundation. Current working chain, kept as the default with starting points.

**Chain philosophy:** cut-EQ → compress → tube color → broad tone → carve-EQ. **EQ on both sides of the dynamics/color block** — cut *before* so the comp doesn't chase rumble, carve *after* so the kick relationship is set on the finished tone.

## 1 — Recording Setup

- **Bass: Hofner B-Bass H-Series**, DI into the Universal Audio Apollo Twin MkII Hi-Z — no amp needed. **With flatwounds this IS the Dahi lane:** "flatwounds just got a tone — sounds old school but got pocket," tracked straight in with nothing on it. Trust the dry take — [SZA "Used" breakdown](https://youtu.be/SPyDimvPNb0).
- **Playing technique is the tone:**
  - **Modern hip hop thick bass:** bass pickup solo'd, play *lightly with the thumb* above the neck pickup — the Hofner goes lower/thicker than a Fender; a legit 808-alternative.
  - **Beatles palm-mute:** the classic "Hofner sound" is really *palm muting* — short thumpy notes, tone rolled down.
  - 🎬 *From video:* the same "technique over gear" diagnosis from the tracking-engineer side of the glass: a boomy bass sound is almost always the bass/player's tone, not a mic-placement or processing problem — "most good bass players get a good tight sound," and a boomy one doesn't get fixed by leaning on a compressor ("the Summit doesn't help that much in controlling it"). Applies just as much to a DI signal as a mic'd one: if the DI reads boomy, check the instrument/technique before reaching for more EQ/comp. → Sound Selection Guide — Al Schmitt (Mix with the Masters), Recording techniques with Al Schmitt
  - 🎬 *From video:* a blind-test teardown of the full bass tone chain rated **fingers/plucking-hand technique as the single most important link — ahead of every piece of gear**, including strings, pickups, and amp: push with the pad of the finger (not near the nail) for a strong tone, dig in for growl vs. wispy/light plucking for a weak thin tone, and always fix technique first when a tone problem shows up before reaching for gear. Full ranked chain: Bass Tone Chain Priority. → BassBuzz, [How to Fix Your Sh*tty Bass Tone](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7b0ShkSBtcU)
- Levels: peaks −12 dBFS, ~−18 average — bass has the widest level swings of any DI source (Gain Staging).

## 2 — Tracking Best Practice

- **Mono, single take, dead center** — bass is never double-tracked for width; the low end lives in mono (Width and Stereo). For vintage lanes, force it: **stereo width to zero** (Kenny keeps his bass dead mono for anything 60s/70s — "makes everything really easy to pan and figure out").
- **One bass, multiple SECTIONS** — the bass doesn't have to be one thing per song: a synth-bass section vs an 808 section vs live bass answering between 808 hits (Arrangement and Song Form) — Kenny Beats, [Trap Drums More Interesting](https://youtu.be/fo-E8dY81Nw).
- **Write on the instrument** — Howard wrote Watch Your Step's bassline on a bass guitar while waiting for the session; a busy bassline can imply the whole harmony over one chord ("root-avoidant basslines = instant sophistication," the Latch lesson).
- Comp per phrase; the groove pocket matters more than note perfection.

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD Console)

### 1. UAD UA 610-B — Unison preamp
- The classic DI bass front end; a little tube gain is most of a "bass tone." (Alt: UAD Neve 1073 for more forward, modern punch.)

### 2. UAD UA 1176LN — Compressor
- 4:1 · fast-ish attack, fast release · **2–4 dB GR** grabbing the pluck peaks
- **Why on the way in:** catching peaks at tracking means the Ableton chain gets an even signal.

### 3. UAD Pultec EQP-1A — EQ
- The famous **low-end trick: boost AND atten @ 60 Hz simultaneously** (lows up while the shifted dip keeps 200 Hz mud out) · print gently (1–2).

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Corrective (pre)
- HPF 35–40 Hz (sub rumble) · LPF 8–9 kHz (string clank) · wide cut ~300 Hz if boomy, slight wide cut ~100 Hz if overwhelming
- Starting point: the **dynamic "Bass Guitar Brighten" factory preset**, then edit (highs back down, peaks tamed) — dynamic presets evolve with the signal — Kenny Beats, [Bass Mix & Effects Chain](https://youtu.be/ivvV0iiiCxQ)
- **Bass EQ rule: wide moves only** — narrow cuts notch *individual notes* out of the line.
- 🎬 *From video:* the wide ~300 Hz boomy-cut and HPF above are "Tubby" (~80 Hz rumble) and "Muddy" (~250 Hz mush) territory in the Bass EQ Frequency Zones — The Five Dwarves framework — Tubby fixes stage-shaking rumble/kick masking, Muddy fixes notes mushing together into indistinct mud; both are two-way controls (Muddy can be added back in if the tone reads thin, not just cut). → BassBuzz, How to Get the PERFECT Bass Tone
- **Why:** Cuts before compression — low junk dominates the comp's detector and makes it pump.

### 2. Ghz Vulf Compressor 3 — Character compression
- **Compression for ~5 dB GR** (① — 4–6 dB range) · **medium Attack** (②) · **timed Release** (③ — grooves with the part) · **Drop off** (④) · **Dust off** (⑤ — clean on a mix bass) · **Mix 100%** (⑥)
- Brand-agnostic per Kenny: "you just need some kind of compression — the EQ part is probably more important."
- **Why:** On bass, colored consistency IS the sound; the low end must be *steady* for the mix to feel solid.

### 3. Ghz Tupe 3 — Tube harmonics
- Low-medium drive
- **Why:** Harmonics at 2×/3× the fundamental let the line read on phones that can't reproduce 60 Hz.

### 4. Ghz Tone Control 3 — Broad seat
- **Darker (Bass +1.5 dB ①, Treble −1 dB ③)** for Motown-y support; **brighter (Treble +1.5 dB ③, or Tilt bright ⑤)** for melodic/McCartney lines.

### 5. Pro-Q 4 — Carve vs kick (post)
- Decide who owns what: typically kick 50–60 Hz, bass 80–120 Hz (or flipped — per song)
- Dynamic node: dip the bass −2 to −3 dB @ the kick's zone, **sidechained from the kick track**
- **+1–2 dB wide boost somewhere in 700 Hz–1 kHz** — the single best "hear the bass on any speaker" move
- 🎬 *From video:* this 700 Hz–1 kHz presence boost sits right at the top of "Honky" (~500 Hz) running into "Bitey" (~1.5 kHz) in the Bass EQ Frequency Zones — The Five Dwarves framework — a nasal (Honky) or overly harsh (Bitey) DI can fight this exact boost; check those zones aren't already overcooked before adding more here. → BassBuzz, How to Get the PERFECT Bass Tone
- **Sub addition when the vintage bass can't ring it off:** R-Bass-style ~69 Hz generation, low amount (owned lane: Saturn 2 low band or Bloom Bass Impulse) — the Hofner has the same sub gap as Kenny's '69 Fender — [Bass Mix & Effects Chain](https://youtu.be/ivvV0iiiCxQ)
- **Layering another bass?** One frequency band each ("you want each bass in its own frequency spectrum" — Disclosure's Minimoog-low + OBXD-top split) — [Prince Edit + Talk VIP](https://youtu.be/hOvLf9nX500)
- **Why:** The kick/bass pocket is the most important low-end decision in the mix; set it *after* the color stages so it holds.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- **Envelope filter, used subtle** — the Mu-Tron lane: "just about the best on bass," run *way less drastic* than the funk quack. Owned: Envelope Follower → Auto Filter cutoff, low amount — [Guitar Recording Process](https://youtu.be/VruZ-A0_aZk)
- **Parallel dirty bass:** duplicate to an amp-sim channel, drive hard, **bandpass 160 Hz–1.2 kHz**, blend under the clean DI — bass audible everywhere without more level. (Or the [Saturation Send](#/chain/saturation-send).)
- 🎬 *From video:* a real-world sighting of exactly this parallel-blend move, done as a deliberate remix upgrade over the original mix rather than a from-scratch default. Tom Lord-Alge blended a clean bass DI with an amp-sim run through a personal saved distortion preset (starting point, then dialed in further) for a "nasty and gritty" tone — "when you play the two sounds together, it's just nasty and gritty." Explicitly not on his original mix of the same song; a case for revisiting an old mix with a fresh creative move rather than only correcting it. → Saturation and Distortion, Parallel Processing, Plugin Wishlist — Mix with the Masters (Tom Lord-Alge), Bass and Guitar sound with Tom Lord-Alge
- 🎬 *From video:* **verse/chorus tonal shift via deliberate re-phasing, not EQ** — if the bass is tracked with a second close mic alongside the DI (not just DI alone), split that close mic to its own channel engaged only on choruses, and nudge a sample-accurate phase/time adjuster (Align Delay) to change the phase relationship between the close mic and the DI — the resulting tonal difference is real and section-specific, with no EQ move at all. Only works because a second source exists to re-phase against — a single DI or single mic gives no second phase relationship to manipulate. → Phase Alignment — Mix with the Masters (Nick Launay), Parallel distortion by Nick Launay

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Electric Bass DI → [Bass Group](#/chain/bass-group) → [Bass Bus](#/chain/bass-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)**.

- Low end gets **no reverb, no width** ([FX Chain System](#/chains/system) rules); [Saturation Send](#/chain/saturation-send) is the only send that regularly earns its place.
- The bass ducks to the kick via the dynamic node in §4 (or a dedicated sidechain trigger — see Sidechaining).

## The "heard vs felt" model

Bass splits into two jobs: **felt** = sub/low warmth (big speakers, chest) · **heard** = ~350 Hz–2 kHz grit and note detail (phones). If the bass is "missing," diagnose *which one*: turning up the felt costs huge headroom for little audibility; saturating/boosting the heard band costs ~1 dB and makes the line audible everywhere. Tupe 3 + the mid boost are the heard tools; the fader is the felt tool.

## Variations

- **Beatles/Sgt Pepper lane:** DI + amp **blended** (the Abbey Road invention), amp mic 5–8 ft back, compress the blend (LALA standing in for the RS124), tone rolled off, palm-muted. (Most of Sgt Pepper is the Rickenbacker — the "Hofner sound" people mean is the muting.)
- **Modern pop:** Saturn 2 multiband — drive mids only, keep sub clean.
- **Vintage 60s/70s:** flats, dry, dead mono, Pro-Q 4 mid/side with width 0 below ~200 Hz.
  - 🎬 *From video:* validated on the same Hofner B-Bass H-Series class of instrument through an analog mixer's channel strip — bass EQ has no universal curve, it's entirely mix-dependent (scoop mids for a mid-dense mix, more/less low end for others); build a "fundamental" tone/EQ pass on the mixer first, then refine further in the DAW once there's an actual mix to fit, rather than doing 100% of the EQ work on either side alone. Compression kept light (~5 dB GR at most) and treated as a later, song-specific decision, not a blind default. Driving the mixer's channel strip harder simultaneously distorts the bass AND limits its dynamic range — a combined saturation+dynamics move, not just tone shaping. → Saturation and Distortion — Zach Scholz, [How To Record 70's Style Bass Tones](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c4EPtO-Jgj0)
  - 🎬 *From video:* the same mixer's overdriven channel fuzz on bass was rated above every fuzz pedal tried on bass — "the best and cleanest sounding fuzz" — a real, repeatable analog-mixer-as-fuzz-pedal move if an analog mixer/console is ever added to this chain (not owned today, so this stays a reference point rather than an owned-gear step). → BASS Slot — Zach Scholz, [How To Record 70's Style Bass Tones](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c4EPtO-Jgj0)

## From videos

- **A slightly hollow bass DI fixed with a small top-end shelf, A/B'd bypassed vs. engaged to confirm it was doing real work — then, separately, that same DI blended with amp-sim distortion for a deliberately "nasty and gritty" remix move (see the inline 🎬 note in §5 Track FX above for the full distortion-blend detail).** Also: a fast visual habit for navigating a session with parallel DI/amp bass tracks — a DI region reads visually "pointier" than a mic'd amp region on the same instrument, before even soloing either. → EQ, Saturation and Distortion, BASS Slot — Mix with the Masters (Tom Lord-Alge), Bass and Guitar sound with Tom Lord-Alge
- **"Blend first" philosophy for a bass delivered from a strong producer — add EQ/compression only if the source genuinely needs it, not by default — plus a light character/distortion stage and a kick sidechain reserved specifically for the drop.** "Again, when you're getting tracks from a really good producer, usually the sounds that are coming in are top-notch. The first thing I do is I blend, and then I, you know, design with the EQ and compression if need be, but the only thing I really did on this guy was throw some Trash on there, a little Clip Control." Trash + Clip Control (iZotope, unowned — see Plugin Wishlist) supplied light distortion character, credited to a named colleague as the source of that move ("Seth Hunter put me on to that"). A saturation/character plugin ("Dark Essence") was flagged as good for both bass AND vocals — also unowned. Sidechain compression off the kick, specifically for the drop section only: **2.5 dB GR**. → Sidechaining, Sound Selection Guide, Plugin Wishlist, Saturation and Distortion — Mix with the Masters (Josh Gudwin), Mixing Dua Lipa's vocals with Josh Gudwin
- **A five-zone bass EQ frequency map — Tubby ~80 Hz, Muddy ~250 Hz, Honky ~500 Hz, Bitey ~1.5 kHz, Edgy ~3–5 kHz+ — each a cut-to-fix-a-symptom / boost-to-chase-a-tone pair, useful as a naming system for exactly what this chain's Pro-Q 4 stages are already doing.** Full per-zone breakdown, fixes, and five artist recipes (Jamerson, McVie, Steve Harris, Geddy Lee, Tim Commerford) on Bass EQ Frequency Zones — The Five Dwarves; inline notes added at the corrective (pre) and carve (post) Pro-Q 4 stages above. Also reinforces this chain's "playing technique is the tone" framing directly: tone is a chain (fingers → strings → pickups → amp → EQ) and EQ's power comes from being last — a great chain up to that point can still be ruined by bad EQ at the end, and the reverse also holds. → EQ, BASS Slot, BED Slot, MIDS Slot, LEAD Slot, Bass Tone Chain Priority — BassBuzz, How to Get the PERFECT Bass Tone
- **String type (round wound vs. flat wound) is a real, deliberate tonal choice worth making on purpose — but pickup upgrades, electronics/wiring swaps, tone wood, and cable all tested as marginal-to-placebo in a blind test when the existing gear is functional.** Full ranked chain and troubleshooting priority order: Bass Tone Chain Priority. → BassBuzz, [How to Fix Your Sh*tty Bass Tone](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7b0ShkSBtcU)
- **Bass EQ is entirely mix-dependent — there is no default curve, only what a given mix calls for** — demonstrated by applying several different EQ curves to the same take specifically because there was no target song to judge against; the takeaway is the discipline (audition against context, don't reach for a preset), not any one curve. → [Bass Bus](#/chain/bass-bus) — Zach Scholz, [How To Record 70's Style Bass Tones](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c4EPtO-Jgj0)
- **Split workflow: a "fundamental" tone pass on hardware/console first, refined further in the DAW once there's a real mix to fit** — deliberately not doing all the tonal work on either side alone. — Zach Scholz, [How To Record 70's Style Bass Tones](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c4EPtO-Jgj0)

## Sources

Andrew Lepard, Make Believe Studios (Hofner hip hop), Boulevard Recording (Beatles bass) — links in [FX Chain System](#/chains/system) · Kenny Beats — [Bass Mix & Effects Chain](https://youtu.be/ivvV0iiiCxQ) · [Guitar Recording Process](https://youtu.be/VruZ-A0_aZk) · Dahi — [SZA "Used"](https://youtu.be/SPyDimvPNb0) · Disclosure — [Prince Edit + Talk VIP](https://youtu.be/hOvLf9nX500) · Zach Scholz — [How To Record 70's Style Bass Tones](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c4EPtO-Jgj0)

chains.title: Bass Group
chains.routing: [Electric Bass DI, Digital Bass] → Bass Group → Bass Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** All bass sources summed. Usually only one bass plays at a time, so this group is mostly about a consistent low-end lane regardless of which source is active.

## Chain

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Lane consistency
- Match the electric and digital bass into the same spectral footprint (their track chains differ; the *mix* shouldn't notice a handoff between them)
- The kick-pocket dip lives on the tracks — only repeat it here if both basses layer simultaneously.

### 2. LALA — Level ride
- **Peak Reduction for ~1.5 dB GR** (① — slow) · **Comp mode** (③) · **HPF engaged** (④ — so the sub doesn't pump it) · **Gain to unity** (②)
- **Why:** An opto leveler smooths section-to-section bass level (verse fingerstyle vs chorus 808) so the low-end energy of the song stays constant — the thing listeners feel as "solid."

## Variations
- 🎬 *From video:* found bass presence in the 700 Hz–1 kHz tone/string-noise range rather than adding low end that was already excessive. Andrew Scheps: "there's more than enough low-end, but a lot of these sort of tone and string noise will be down in this 700 to 1k range, so I'm gonna try adding a little bit of this — just sounds a little more present." → EQ, Masking and Carving — Andrew Scheps (Mix with the Masters), Mixing Guitars & Bass - Andrew Scheps
- **Live bass + 808 layered (pop-trap hybrid):** split duties with EQ — 808 owns below ~120 Hz, Hofner owns 120 Hz+ (HPF the Hofner hard) — two basses only work when they don't share an octave.

chains.title: Bass Bus
chains.routing: Bass Group → Bass Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Final pass on the low-end lane. Light — most bass work already happened at track/group.

## Chain

### 1. Ghz Tupe 3 — Warmth
- **Tube 15%** (① — very low drive) · **Tilt neutral** (②) · **Mix 100%** (④) · **Output** matched (⑤)
- **Why:** one more coat of harmonics helps the whole low end translate; the bus is the right place because it catches whichever bass source is active.

### 2. Glue Compressor — Glue
- **Ratio 2:1** (②) · **Attack 30 ms** (③ — lets the note attack/pluck through before clamping) · **Release 0.2 s** (④ — or Auto) · **Threshold for ~1.5 dB GR** (①) · **Range 6 dB** (⑥) · **Makeup** to unity (⑤) · **Dry/Wet 100%** (⑦)
- **Why:** Gentle 2:1 with a slow attack fuses whichever bass source is active without squashing the sub or dulling the transient — the bus glues, it doesn't level.

### 3. Utility — Mono guarantee
- Bass Mono ~100 Hz — the final insurance under everything (harmless if the tracks already did it).
- 🎬 *From video:* when a synth bass has lots of built-in chorus/sides, a touch of **OTT** before this (upward, "a push not a squash") **tightens the mono low end** so the SUB Slot reads punchy — Disclosure, [Deeper](https://youtu.be/SM0FZ58ckVw).

## Variations
- **If the bass lane feels over-compressed:** bypass Glue here — three comps (track, group, bus) can be one too many; the track comp is the load-bearing one.

## From videos
General tips pulled from production breakdowns (via `/music-enrich`), newest-first.

- **OTT to tighten a wide bass's mono center** — upward, subtle, so the sub reads punchy under all the chorus/sides — Disclosure, [Deeper](https://youtu.be/SM0FZ58ckVw)
- **Most bass moves are track-level** (double-sidechain, bass-amp fizz, octave-up for phones, sample-one-note) — see [Digital Bass Track](#/chain/digital-bass-track) / [Electric Bass DI Track](#/chain/electric-bass-di-track) for those; the bus stays light — Disclosure, various

chains.title: Acoustic Piano Track
chains.routing: Acoustic Piano → Inst-Synth Group → Inst-Synth Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Piano VST — usually a supporting harmonic instrument that must *not* fight the vocal (piano covers the entire spectrum, so it's the #1 masking offender).

**Chain philosophy:** carve → even → sweeten → width check.

## 1 — Sound Selection

- **Keyscape — the default.** *LA Custom C7* flagship grand (pop/ballad centerpiece), *Wing Upright*/*Wing Tack* for character/vintage, duo patches for hybrid color. In-patch: internal reverb OFF (space comes from sends), velocity curve to taste. → Keyscape — LA Custom C7 Grand / Keyscape — Wing Upright & Tack Piano
- **Kontakt 7** libraries for felt/intimate or cinematic flavors.
- **Nexus** for instant pop "stacked piano" (already produced — bypass most of the chain below). → Nexus — Stacked Pop Piano
- **Rule: choose the patch that already IS the sound** — patch-switching beats EQ-rescuing. 🎬 Pre-highlight favorites *before* a writing session (Disclosure star their D-50 patches ahead of time — "less messing about") — [Making Beats + Talk](https://youtu.be/1GhqAf9lc3A) → Sound Palette.

## 2 — Programming Best Practice

- **Play at performance energy, commit to audio when dialed** ([FX Chain System](#/chains/system) bounce-in-place — Disclosure record synths/keys in as audio: "the MIDI isn't the sound").
- **Cut the low junk from the part itself:** if the left hand doubles the bassline's register, thin the voicing — arrangement beats EQ (Masking and Carving).
- **HPF discipline applies to keys too** — sub-100 Hz belongs to kick/808; the piano's low octave stays only when piano is the star — Kenny Beats, [808 & Kick](https://youtu.be/4iAKvWWlCvY).

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD front end)

The "recorded through a console" pass that keeps software instruments on the same footing as recorded ones — printed when dialed:

### 1. UAD Neve 1073 — Preamp plugin — barely driven, ~0 VU
### 2. UAD Teletronix LA-2A (Silver) — 1–2 dB gentle leveling
### 3. UAD Pultec EQP-1A — +1 @ 12 kHz air max

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Carve
- HPF 60–100 Hz (give the low octave to bass/kick unless piano is solo) · low shelf −1 to −3 dB @ 150–200 Hz in dense mixes (boost instead when it's the sparse centerpiece)
- **Mid/side mud trick:** cut 250–300 Hz on the **mid channel only** (−6 to −9 dB is fine) — clears the center for snare/bass/vocal while the sides keep the body; *widens* the piano for free
- **Dynamic dip 2–3 kHz sidechained from the lead vocal**, −2 to −4 dB
- Magic frequencies (sound honky soloed, correct in the mix): **1–2 kHz = background→priority** (and earbud/car translation) · **5 kHz shelf = presence** (automate up in choruses) · 10–12 kHz = airy-but-distant
- **Why:** The vocal-sidechained dip is the modern answer to piano/vocal masking — full piano alone, automatic space when the singer's in.

### 2. Pro-C 2 — Even out
- 3:1 · attack 30–40 ms (hammer transient passes) · **2–4 dB GR** — slightly more than feels natural, so it never jumps over the vocal.

### 3. Kramer Tape — Sweeten
- **15 ips** (④) · **Flux low** (①) · **a touch of Wow & Flutter** (⑥) · **Playback to unity** (③)
- **Why:** VST pianos are too perfect; tape wobble/harmonics add the "recorded in a room" quality.
- 🎬 **J37 tape → Abbey Road Chambers reverb, "to make it sound like it's in a room."** A bridge/breakdown piano (built by copying chords + vocals in from the main pad, then manually "strummed") runs this device (the owned J37 stand-in) directly into a reverb standing in for Abbey Road Chambers — owned equivalent ValhallaVintageVerb (1970s Color, chamber-family mode). Same J37→Kramer Tape mapping already confirmed on a separate electric-piano video. → ValhallaVintageVerb, Reverb, Plugin Wishlist — loner, [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo)

### 4. Utility — Width check
- VST pianos come huge-stereo; narrow to ~70–85% so it doesn't smear over the panned guitars.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- **RC-20 Retro Color** for the lo-fi bed lane (use it as an effects box, not a crusher). A filtered/reversed copy of the piano makes a free intro (Arrangement and Song Form's filtered-intro trick).

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Acoustic Piano → [Inst-Synth Group](#/chain/inst-synth-group) → [Inst-Synth Bus](#/chain/inst-synth-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)**.

- **[Reverb Send Room](#/chain/reverb-send-room)** modest · **[Reverb Send Long](#/chain/reverb-send-long)** generous only on featured/ballad parts · sidechain-duck under the vocal when it's a bed.
- 🎬 *From video:* a second, CHORUS-ONLY high-piano layer running alongside the main piano, with **Ghz DC19 3's Spring reverb as the entire distinguishing move** — reserve the spring for a section-exclusive layer (route only the chorus-only piano to it, or automate the send in specifically at the chorus) rather than a constant texture, so the spring's entrance itself reads as the arrival cue. A/B dry vs. wet before committing — the effect is meant to be obvious ("another dimension"), not subtle glue. → Ghz DC19 3, Arrangement and Song Form — Mix with the Masters (Tom Elmhirst), Tom Elmhirst breaks down his mix of 'Rolling in the Deep' by Adele

## Variations

- **Featured/ballad:** skip the vocal dip, HPF down to 40 Hz, long verb generous.
- **Pop stab piano:** more comp (4–6 dB), Transient-style attack, mono it and pan like a rhythm guitar.

## From videos

- **A pair of small-diaphragm condensers ("K86s") strapped directly to the piano's soundboard and left in place permanently, for a live-tracked piano.** Paul Epworth: "we've been recording pianos with a couple of K86s strapped to the soundboard of the piano, which is something we discovered that Abbey Road like to do" — praised specifically for **flexibility**: mounted on the soundboard rather than floating over open strings, the lid can be opened or closed at will (open for isolation/character, closed to track another instrument in the room at the same time) without re-rigging the mics. A hedged, unconfirmed mention of a hardware stereo bus compressor on the same piano signal path ("probably the best stereo compressor available... may well have been a 1178 or something") — best-match owned equivalent logged on UAD UA 1176LN, flagged speculative there (no settings given). → UAD UA 1176LN, Vintage Gear Worklist — Mix with the Masters (Paul Epworth), Paul Epworth opens up the session for Adele's "Rolling In The Deep"
- **A two-piano arrangement: a low piano runs the entire song as the harmonic "peg," a high piano is reserved for the chorus only, and spring reverb is the high piano's sole distinguishing move — see the inline 🎬 note in §6 above for the full recipe and owned-plugin mapping.** → Ghz DC19 3, Arrangement and Song Form — Mix with the Masters (Tom Elmhirst), Tom Elmhirst breaks down his mix of 'Rolling in the Deep' by Adele
- **Build a bridge/breakdown piano part by copying existing chord MIDI + vocal audio into a new section, then manually "strumming" the copied chords for a played feel** — see the inline 🎬 J37/Abbey Road Chambers note in §4.3 above for the finishing processing. → Arrangement and Song Form, Kramer Tape, Plugin Wishlist — loner, [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo)

## Sources

Hardcore Music Studio (piano frequencies), Better Mixes (mid/side), Help Me Devvon (collision detection) — links in [FX Chain System](#/chains/system) · Disclosure — [Making Beats + Talk](https://youtu.be/1GhqAf9lc3A) · Kenny Beats — [808 & Kick](https://youtu.be/4iAKvWWlCvY) · loner — [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo)

chains.title: Electric Piano Track
chains.routing: Electric Piano → Inst-Synth Group → Inst-Synth Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Rhodes/Wurli VST — the warm harmonic bed of the neo-soul/hip hop lane. The classic EP sound *is* its signal chain: keys → tube preamp → chorus/tremolo.

**Chain philosophy:** clean → level → tube bark → motion → (tremolo).

## 1 — Sound Selection

- **Keyscape — the definitive EP box:**
  - *Rhodes — LA Custom E* / *Classic Mark I*: THE neo-soul/hip hop Rhodes. In-patch: a little tube drive for bark; tremolo OFF if using PanMan downstream (don't double-tremolo) → Keyscape — Rhodes LA Custom E & Mark I
  - *Wurlitzer 140B* (tube, warmer) or *200A* (the Supertramp/Queen pop-rock Wurli) → Keyscape — Wurlitzer 140B & 200A
  - *Clavinet C* for funk comping · *Pianet* for the "I Am the Walrus" tine sound → Keyscape — Clavinet C / Keyscape — Pianet
- **Operator** for DX7-style FM e-piano (80s glass; modern trap loves it pitched dark). → Operator — DX7 FM E-Piano
- **Nexus** EP patches when it needs to be produced-and-done in 10 seconds.
- 🎬 **A vintage/ambient Rhodes chain built around a found a cappella, plus a doubling piano layer for body.** Rhodes chords (freestyled in C minor, the personal home key, then transposed back to the source's pitch when done) → **J37 tape** ("my favorite preset," a "metallic drum loop" character) → **ShaperBox filter preset** (rolls off the highs, turns the part into more of a pad) → **spring reverb**, "to give it more of a vintage sound." A doubling piano (Teletone Audio "Postcard Piano," unowned — third confirmed use, see Plugin Wishlist) copies the exact same chords for body, then gets its own **"Reels" "Excited Tape" preset** (harshness + flutter both up) + a few original licks/riffs + a **Portal** instance for extra character. Owned-lane mapping: J37 → Kramer Tape; ShaperBox filter → Shaper; spring reverb → Ghz DC19 3. → Kramer Tape, Shaper, Ghz DC19 3, Portal, Plugin Wishlist, Melody Writing — loner, [we made a crazy r&b trapsoul song!? (making a beat from scratch around an acapella)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=39aHjEJ5-FU)
- 🎬 **Voice-memo-to-DAW chord workflow + a named go-to Wurlitzer patch.** Chord progressions found away from the studio get voice-memo'd on the phone first "so I could remember it," then rebuilt in the DAW; the default go-to electric-piano sound named explicitly is Arturia Wurli V's "Plain Roads" preset (owned lane: Keyscape Wurlitzer 140B/200A above) — chords played in freely to match the voice-memo idea, then quantized. Processing: Kramer Tape (J37 best-match) → a very subtle reverb (size/decay/wet all pulled down) → a dotted delay preset with wow/flutter-style character reduced → a closing EQ low-cut. → Kramer Tape, Reverb, Delay, EQ Eight, Plugin Wishlist — loner, [making a soulful afrobeats beat for rema & wizkid from scratch (use voice notes to start ideas!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e-KvnLXHAy4)
- 🎬 **West Coast "Mustard" bounce — layer TWO piano parts together, both in a major scale, for the bouncy melodic-chord identity.** Doubled piano + major scale specifically is what gives the chords their bounce — called out as ingrained DNA for the style, not a one-off preset choice. Rhodes/Roads + guitar accents get layered on top afterward as further texture. → Melody Writing, Layering and Stacking, Genre Drum Patterns — loner, [the secrets behind DJ Mustard's ICONIC beats!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bID1-whdYB0)

## 2 — Programming Best Practice

- **The behind-the-beat feel can be printed, not quantized** — 🎬 Kenny runs the Rhodes through a Strymon Deco "for some lag": tape-slew as a feel artifact. Owned lane: Cassette or EchoBoy tape mode (single subtle repeat), or a small positive track delay — [R&B Vibes Beat](https://youtu.be/XJEEE7q2oEA).
- **Ninth chords nearly always** (Howard Lawrence's default color) — EPs love extensions; voice them mid-register so the mud zone stays clear.
- Commit to audio when the patch is dialed ([FX Chain System](#/chains/system) bounce-in-place).

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD front end)

### 1. UAD UA 610-B — Preamp plugin — driven slightly harder than piano (EPs love tube input) · ~0 VU
### 2. UAD Teletronix LA-2A — 1–2 dB
### 3. UAD Pultec EQP-1A — low ATTEN @ 100 Hz if woolly

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Clean
- HPF 60–80 Hz · tame the honky 400–800 Hz zone if muddy · bell +2–4 kHz for tine definition on melodic parts.

### 2. LALA — Leveling
- **Peak Reduction for ~2.5 dB GR** (①) · **Comp mode** (③) · **Mix 100%** (⑤) · **Gain to unity** (②)
- **Why:** opto compression is historically what Rhodes ran into (an LA-2A in every 70s studio) — smooth sustain without killing the bark.

### 3. Ghz Tupe 3 — Tube drive
- **Tube 30%** (① — low-medium; push to **50%** for bark on funky parts) · **Tilt slightly bright** (②) · **Mix 100%** (④)
- **Why:** A Rhodes' character comes from overdriving its amp; clean EP VSTs are missing the point.

### 4. Chorus-Ensemble — Motion
- **Mode Ensemble** (①) · **Rate 0.4 Hz** (② — slow drift) · **Amount 20%** (③ — low depth) · **Width 100%** (⑥) · **Dry/Wet 30%** (⑧) — the Dyno-My-Piano shimmer
- Pensado's "silky bed" recipe: micro pitch-shift (Little MicroShift) + **multiband saturation** (Saturn 2 — warm the mids, leave the top clean) + Dimension-D-style chorus — judge by *feel*, not solo sound.

### 5. PanMan — Tremolo/auto-pan (optional)
- Slow sine, subtle — the suitcase-Rhodes stereo tremolo.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- **RC-20 Retro Color** instead of Tupe for the lo-fi trap/ambient loop flavor.
- 🎬 A **velocity→filter mapping** (Poly6-style: velocity drives cutoff) makes comping expressive without automation — Disclosure, [Howard Is Here](https://youtu.be/gCfU5Cq9WU4).

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Electric Piano → [Inst-Synth Group](#/chain/inst-synth-group) → [Inst-Synth Bus](#/chain/inst-synth-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)**.

- **[Reverb Send Long](#/chain/reverb-send-long)** heavy on ambient EP beds · [Delay Send Slap](#/chain/delay-send-slap) (Howard's one-slap) for the small-club feel · sidechain-duck vs kick with Kickstart 2 on trap lanes.

## Variations

- **Trap/ambient EP loops:** RC-20, heavy long verb, kick duck.
- **Dry funk:** skip chorus + tremolo, more Tupe bark, mono, panned.

## From videos

- **Deliberately minor, sub-2 dB piano processing on an already-good mix stem: mid/side narrowing on the sides, a light kick-sidechain to pull certain frequencies more mono during kick hits, and an overall light EQ pass purely for thickness.** "This is all minor stuff, right? Taking out some sides, doing some really soft moves on here, a little bit of mid/side work on this piano, hitting it with a little bit of side chain off the kick, making it a little more mono in certain frequencies, and then doing some overall light EQ. Nothing over... nothing over 2 dB. For me it just kind of thickened him up a little bit." A useful reminder that a piano's stereo width can be narrowed dynamically (via sidechain) rather than only with a static M/S EQ move. → Width and Stereo, Sidechaining, EQ, [Dua Lipa Vocal Chain](#/chain/dua-lipa-vocal-chain) — Mix with the Masters (Josh Gudwin), Mixing Dua Lipa's vocals with Josh Gudwin
- **A vintage/ambient Rhodes chain (J37 tape → ShaperBox filter/pad → spring reverb) plus a doubling Teletone Audio "Postcard Piano" layer (Reels "Excited Tape" preset → licks/riffs → Portal), built around a found a cappella** — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above. → Kramer Tape, Shaper, Ghz DC19 3, Portal, Plugin Wishlist, Melody Writing — loner, [we made a crazy r&b trapsoul song!? (making a beat from scratch around an acapella)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=39aHjEJ5-FU)
- **Voice-memo-to-DAW chord capture + Arturia Wurli V "Plain Roads" as the named go-to sound, with a tape → subtle reverb → dotted delay → EQ low-cut processing chain** — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above. → Kramer Tape, Reverb, Delay, EQ Eight, Plugin Wishlist — loner, [making a soulful afrobeats beat for rema & wizkid from scratch (use voice notes to start ideas!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e-KvnLXHAy4)
- **Two bouncy pianos layered together, both in a major scale, for the West Coast "Mustard bounce" chord identity, plus Rhodes/Roads + guitar accents layered on top as texture** — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above. → Melody Writing, Layering and Stacking — loner, [the secrets behind DJ Mustard's ICONIC beats!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bID1-whdYB0)

## Sources

Pensado's Place (Rhodes recipe) — link in [FX Chain System](#/chains/system) · Kenny Beats — [R&B Vibes Beat](https://youtu.be/XJEEE7q2oEA) · Disclosure — [Howard Is Here](https://youtu.be/gCfU5Cq9WU4) · [Making Beats + Talk](https://youtu.be/1GhqAf9lc3A) · loner — [the secrets behind DJ Mustard's ICONIC beats!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bID1-whdYB0)

chains.title: Synth Bed Track
chains.routing: Synth Bed → Inst-Synth Group → Inst-Synth Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Pads, beds, atmosphere — the glue layer the listener feels but never notices. The whole chain is about *making room*: a pad fills space until something more important needs it.

**Chain philosophy:** aggressive framing → even the wash → width/level → duck.

## 1 — Sound Selection

- 🎬 **Genre-match a preset first, revoice the chord tops by hand after, then swap the preset mid-build if it isn't landing.** Building an airy Post Malone-style pad (Arturia Analog Lab's "Layers Volume 2" bank): picked "Burning Desire" for its melodic character, wrote the progression, hand-nudged individual chord-TOP notes into a similar register for a different feeling without touching the harmony — then swapped the whole instrument to "Night Sky" mid-build once it read "a bit more Post Malone-ish." Same slot, same voicing work, different patch. → Melody Writing, Plugin Wishlist — loner, [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo)
- **Omnisphere** — THE pad instrument; **layer two patches (one dark + one airy)** and balance instead of hunting one perfect patch. → Omnisphere — Layered Dark+Airy Bed
- 🎬 **Mike Dean's CS-80 + Jupiter-8 pad** — a two-oscillator raw patch (sawtooth + rectangle wave, Fine Tune pulled up for a wide detune, light chorus + reverb + overdrive, chorus and cutoff modulated together) layered with a factory strings preset from a second synth entirely, built starting from a default patch rather than a preset. Nearest owned build path: DUNE 3/Serum 2 for the raw detuned-oscillator layer + Model 84 Polyphonic Synthesizer or Omnisphere strings for the second layer. → Sound Selection Guide, Layering and Stacking, Roland Jupiter-8 — loner, [mike dean's secret 'astroworld' synth techniques!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2bJGXDlSFdY)
- **Model 84 Polyphonic Synthesizer** — the Juno pad lane: saw + sub, chorus II, slow filter — the 80s/indie warm bed in 30 seconds. 🎬 Era-match the processing: "it's got to be 80s for all the reverbs — it's definitely an 80s Juno" — Disclosure, [Making Beats + Talk](https://youtu.be/1GhqAf9lc3A).
- 🎬 **One Juno-emulation instrument carrying FIVE roles in a single 80s synthwave/pop beat (main pad, bass, a second "chorus-lift" pad, a pluck texture, a bell counter-melody), each with a small dedicated chain.** Main pad: attack/envelope down → chorus (before the arpeggiator) → Cassette → heavy reverb → EQ (cut lows) → delay (a tried half-time stage got cut for being unused). Second pad, added because the chorus needed to sound bigger: same dry-start move → EQ (lows + mids) → delay → reverb. Full per-layer breakdown (pluck, bell) on Model 84 Polyphonic Synthesizer and Synthwave. → Cassette, TAL-Chorus-LX, Model 84 Polyphonic Synthesizer, Synthwave, Layering and Stacking — loner, [how to make an 80's synthwave/pop beat for the weeknd.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dWhh27UFWhY)
- **Wavetable / Drift** — evolving/motion pads (position-LFO movement that OTT loves). · **Nexus** — instant produced pads.
- 🎬 **80s synth-pop pad recipe (Weeknd *Dawn FM*): saw + square blended ~70/30, one oscillator tuned a major-key interval above the other (interval, not unison-detune, gives the "big" size), then Chorus → Reverb → Overdrive in that exact order, then two LFOs on two different cycle modes — LFO→filter cutoff synced to quarter notes in Single mode (per-note sweep), LFO→reverb dry/wet in Cycle mode (continuous, fills the space between chord hits).** Full recipe on DUNE 3's Techniques section. — loner, [the production secrets behind the weeknd's evolving sound!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GMeZtNImaT0) → Modulation, Reverb
- Universal pad rules: **attack 0.5–2 s, release 1–3 s**, unison detune wide, slow filter motion, velocity → nothing, no sub octave (the chain HPFs it anyway).
- 🎬 **A one-shot with portamento/glide turned up, used purely as a dedicated section-transition marker** — one specific patch reused every time a "switch" into a new section is needed, rather than writing new transitional material each time (the "Ballin'" glide sound). → Arrangement and Song Form — loner, [the secrets behind DJ Mustard's ICONIC beats!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bID1-whdYB0)

## 2 — Programming Best Practice

- 🎬 **A three-part layering recipe to make ONE synth read as a whole band: a ghost note of the chord just before/after the main hit, one short percussive impact, then a reverb-tail return.** "Every time there's a chord playing you're going to have like a ghost note of the chord just before or after, or you're going to have one impact of the chord that's going to be short, and then you're going to have the reverb coming back... so it gives like a movement of a whole band playing together just with one instrument." Three distinct roles from ONE source rather than three instruments: quiet pre/post-echo ghost hit → short punchy transient impact on the downbeat → longer reverb-tail return filling the space after. → Layering and Stacking, Reverb — Justice x Kevin Parker (Mix with the Masters), [Behind the Track｜'Neverender' by Justice & Tame Impala](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=emP9EWcqss4)
- 🎬 **Morph a pad into an arp of the SAME patch via automation, instead of writing a new part for a new section** — automate the arpeggiator's on/off state together with **attack** and **filter cutoff frequency**, so the existing pad reshapes into an up-arp'd version of itself when a new section (e.g. a choir entering a bar early) needs a lift — reusing one sound in a new form reads as more cohesive than introducing a competing new sound at the same moment. → Automation — loner, [James Blake's production tricks are GAMECHANGING!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9FX7p23hSlc)
- 🎬 **Keep the bed thin and mono when it's meant to leave room for a vocal, not just "wide and lush" by default** — a deliberately thin, mono foundation (paired with the lead/bass synths, not just this bed) frees frequency and stereo headroom for the voice; width gets introduced later and on purpose, staggered a bar ahead of the section that needs it. → Width and Stereo, [1 Synth Lead Track](#/chain/synth-lead-track) — loner, [James Blake's production tricks are GAMECHANGING!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9FX7p23hSlc)
- 🎬 **The melody collage** — a bed doesn't need one great part: stack ~3 unremarkable airy melodies in one key (high octave / low octave / bell), filter/texture/reverse into a drone, and let the **bassline imply the changes** — Kenny Beats, [Beat Mix & Creation](https://youtu.be/FC__hbvnETY) → Arrangement and Song Form, BED Slot.
- **Voice above the mud zone** — the chain cuts 200–300 Hz anyway; don't write the pad's weight there.
- Commit to audio when dialed; a filtered/reversed copy = free intro (Arrangement and Song Form).

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD front end)

Optional — beds get framed so hard in §4 that the front end matters least here:

### 1. UAD UA 610-B — barely on · ~0 VU
### 2. UAD Teletronix LA-2A — 1 dB
### 3. UAD Pultec EQP-1A — bypass

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Aggressive framing
- **HPF 150–300 Hz** (pads NEVER need real low end — fastest mud-killer in a dense mix) · LPF 8–12 kHz (leave the air to vocals/hats) · dynamic dip in the vocal band keyed from the vocal
- **Mid/side upgrade:** make the 200–300 Hz cut **mid-channel only**, deep — the pad vacates the center (snare/bass/vocal) but keeps body on the sides, getting *wider* as a side effect. The single best pad-in-a-dense-mix move.
- 🎬 A small low-mid carve where the synth clashes with the vocal is often all a chord bed needs — Disclosure, [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU).

### 2. OTT — Even the wash
- **Depth 10–20%** (①) — no note swells over the mix · **Time moderate** (② — avoid pumping) · **In/Out to unity** (③/④)

- 🎬 **Low-cut EQ → heavy reverb → cassette/tape stage, that exact order, for an ambient "vintage-but-airy" pad.** After Pro-Q 4's low-cut in this stage, a deliberately heavy reverb goes on for the "super ambient" target, then a clean-tape/cassette pass strictly for vintage color — the tape stage comes LAST, after the pad's already wet, not as a dry-signal color pass before space is added. Owned lane: Cassette. → Cassette, Reverb — loner, [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo)

### 3. Utility — Width + level
- Wide is fine here (pads are where width belongs), check mono · sit the level lower than feels right — **if you clearly hear the pad, it's too loud.**

### 4. Kickstart 2 — Duck
- **Gentle curve** (① — rhythmic breathing vs. the kick) — or **keyed from the *vocal*** (④) for auto-space in ballads · **Mix to taste** (③)
- 🎬 Disclosure key the bed's compressor **off the vocal via a muted empty bus**, slow release so it flows (fast release = "radio compression, always full"); Soothe2/Trackspacer do the frequency-domain version — [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU) → Sidechaining.
- **Why:** A pad that ducks is a pad that never has to be turned down.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- **RC-20 Retro Color** texture on dark trap pads · ValhallaShimmer insert (low mix) on exposed ambient sections · granular smears (Portal-style — wishlist) behind a printed part.
- 🎬 **Textured pulsating one-shot pad: Reverb → guitar amp → shaper box → EQ — the guitar-amp stage is what makes it read as "textured" instead of clean.** Reused twice with different attack/shaper settings for two Mustard beats (a dark two-note power-chord pad, and a glossier more-attack pad). Owned amp-sim lane: Morgan Amps Suite; the shaper-box stage is the already-tracked Plugin Wishlist gap (Cableguys ShaperBox). → Saturation and Distortion, EQ — loner, [the secrets behind DJ Mustard's ICONIC beats!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bID1-whdYB0)

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Synth Bed → [Inst-Synth Group](#/chain/inst-synth-group) → [Inst-Synth Bus](#/chain/inst-synth-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)**.

- Beds mostly carry their own space (patch reverb/motion); [Reverb Send Long](#/chain/reverb-send-long) only when the bed doubles as the song's atmosphere.

## Variations

- **Ambient intros/outros (pad exposed):** open the filters, automate width, Shimmer insert.
- **Trap bed:** LPF down to 5–6 kHz, RC-20 texture, very low in the mix.

## From videos

- **The ghost-note + impact + reverb-tail band-in-a-box recipe, sourced end to end** — see the inline 🎬 note in §2 above. → Layering and Stacking, Reverb — Justice x Kevin Parker (Mix with the Masters), [Behind the Track｜'Neverender' by Justice & Tame Impala](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=emP9EWcqss4)
- **The full Post Malone-style pad build, sourced end to end** — see the two inline 🎬 notes in §1/§4 above (preset choice + swap, then low-cut → heavy reverb → cassette-tape finishing order). → Cassette, Reverb, Plugin Wishlist — loner, [making a billboard number 1 pop beat for post malone's next album from scratch!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX_IB6K-xIo)
- **A portamento one-shot as a section-transition marker, plus a textured pulsating pad chain (Reverb → guitar amp → shaper box → EQ) built twice with different attack/shaper settings** — see the two inline 🎬 notes in §1/§5 above. → Arrangement and Song Form, Saturation and Distortion, Plugin Wishlist — loner, [the secrets behind DJ Mustard's ICONIC beats!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bID1-whdYB0)
- **Pad-to-arp morph via automating arp on/off + attack + filter cutoff together, plus a thin/mono foundation to leave room for a vocal** — see the two inline 🎬 notes in §2 above. → Automation, Width and Stereo — loner, [James Blake's production tricks are GAMECHANGING!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9FX7p23hSlc)
- **The full Dawn FM synth-pop pad build, sourced end to end** — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above; full step-by-step (waveform blend, tuning interval, effects order, dual-LFO cycle-mode routing) lives on DUNE 3's Techniques section. → DUNE 3, Modulation — loner, [the production secrets behind the weeknd's evolving sound!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GMeZtNImaT0)
- **One Juno-emulation instrument run across five pad/texture roles in one build (main pad, second "chorus-lift" pad, plus a pluck and a bell logged on other chains) — see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above.** Full per-layer chains on Model 84 Polyphonic Synthesizer and the Synthwave genre page's third worked-breakdown section. → Cassette, TAL-Chorus-LX, EchoBoy, Synthwave — loner, [how to make an 80's synthwave/pop beat for the weeknd.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dWhh27UFWhY)

## Sources

Disclosure — [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU) · [Making Beats + Talk](https://youtu.be/1GhqAf9lc3A) · Kenny Beats — [Beat Mix & Creation](https://youtu.be/FC__hbvnETY) · loner — [the production secrets behind the weeknd's evolving sound!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GMeZtNImaT0) · Justice x Kevin Parker (Mix with the Masters) — [Behind the Track｜'Neverender' by Justice & Tame Impala](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=emP9EWcqss4)

chains.title: Synth Lead Track
chains.routing: Synth Lead → Inst-Synth Group → Inst-Synth Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Melodic synth lines — the "second vocal." Gets vocal-style treatment: present, controlled, carved against the actual vocal.

**Chain philosophy:** carve → multiband control → edge → width → seat.

## 1 — Sound Selection

- **Serum 2** — the modern default (pop/trap/EDM). Patch recipe: 1–2 osc, unison 3–7, detune 0.10–0.20, LPF 24 dB with a touch of envelope, **mono + legato + glide 40–80 ms** for expressive lines. → Serum 2 — Modern Lead
- **DUNE 3** — festival supersaws (the unison engine is the point, 8–16 voices). → DUNE 3 — Festival Supersaw Lead
- **Massive** — growly 2010s character. · **Drift / Model 84 Polyphonic Synthesizer** — warm analog mono (synthwave/indie; Model 84 chorus = instant vintage width). · **Omnisphere** — hybrid/organic texture leads.
- Universal patch rules: vibrato via mod-wheel LFO (not baked in), attack 0–10 ms, release short enough not to smear, **kill sub content below ~100 Hz at the patch**.
- 🎬 **No VST for the target hardware? Substitute a one-shot sample kit and keep it unquantized** — Mike Dean's Moog Matriarch leads (no VST exists) sourced from a producer one-shot kit instead, played back completely off the grid on purpose. → Sound Selection Guide, Sampling and Sound Selection, Rhythm and Groove — loner, [mike dean's secret 'astroworld' synth techniques!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2bJGXDlSFdY)
- 🎬 **Pick oscillators whose harmonic content fits the key** — a major-harmonic voice sits where a clashing square wouldn't — Disclosure, [Higher Than Ever Before](https://youtu.be/9XkHSronZck). Pre-highlight favorite patches before the session (Sound Palette).

## 2 — Programming Best Practice

- 🎬 **Keep the foundation thin and mono, on purpose, to leave room for the vocal** — where "typically people use big, rich sounds," a deliberately thin, simple, **mono** patch (bass + lead synth both in mono) leaves more frequency and stereo headroom for the voice to sit in; a new synth entering later gets staggered a bar early and hard-panned to introduce width — see Width and Stereo for the pan-timing half of the move. → Width and Stereo — loner, [James Blake's production tricks are GAMECHANGING!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9FX7p23hSlc)
- 🎬 **Two-synth morph** — layer a **smooth synth + a raspy one on the same MIDI** and fade the filter so one *becomes* the other across the phrase (clean Diva/Juno → filter-distorted MS-20) — Disclosure, [NO CAP](https://youtu.be/kz5dmb3QdI8).
- 🎬 **Velocity → filter, not volume** — expression via cutoff mapping (the Poly6 move) — Disclosure, [Howard Is Here](https://youtu.be/gCfU5Cq9WU4).
- 🎬 **~10 automation lanes on one synth** (release, EQ builds, verb/delay builds) bring a line to life; in dense sections layer several synths each panned/automated *slightly* differently so nothing loops identically — Disclosure, [Howard Is Here](https://youtu.be/gCfU5Cq9WU4) → Automation.
- Commit to audio when dialed ([FX Chain System](#/chains/system) bounce-in-place).

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD front end)

Light-touch — the patch is the tone; this is the analog handshake:

### 1. UAD Neve 1073 — Preamp plugin, light · ~0 VU
### 2. UAD UA 1176LN — 1–2 dB fast (tames patch level jumps)
### 3. UAD Pultec EQP-1A — bypass or air only

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Carve
- HPF 100–200 Hz · if it shares register with the vocal, dynamic-dip 2–4 kHz keyed from the vocal (the lead synth defers to the lead singer).

### 2. OTT — Multiband control
- **Depth 15–30%** (① — never the default 100%; that's sound design, not mixing) · **Time up** (② — relax pumping on slower material) · **In/Out to unity** (③/④)
- What it is: 3-band up+down compression — highs near-limited, mids breathing, output hyped — "bright, dense, modern" in one knob; works best on sounds that already *move*.

### 3. Saturn 2 — Edge
- Tube/tape, drive to taste — leads can take real drive; harmonics = cut-through
- 🎬 Hero raspy lead: **Decapitator "Punish"** near 9–10 for one moment; **acid**: hot resonant filter (~+20 dB) sweeping INTO the distortion so the resonance peak drives it (MS-20 → 303) — Disclosure, [NO CAP](https://youtu.be/kz5dmb3QdI8) / [Deeper](https://youtu.be/SM0FZ58ckVw).

### 4. Wider — Width
- Subtle, mono-compatible — big without leaving the center.

### 5. Utility — Final gain/pan seat.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- 🎬 **Frequency Shifter on a sawtooth** — the Ring Shifter move, "the key to our sound": movement + stereo width + phase — Disclosure, [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU) / [You & Me](https://youtu.be/9zsU5Y8r_Ow) → Modulation.
- **Bit-crusher for "silk"/character** on a beep/lead — Disclosure, [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU).

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Synth Lead → [Inst-Synth Group](#/chain/inst-synth-group) → [Inst-Synth Bus](#/chain/inst-synth-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)**.

- **[Delay Send Other](#/chain/delay-send-other) is the lead synth's reverb** — synced repeats keep energy; wash reverb blurs it. [Delay Send Slap](#/chain/delay-send-slap) for the small-club one-slap.

## Variations

- **Supersaw EDM:** skip Wider (already huge), mono below 150 Hz, sidechain-duck vs kick.
- **Analog mono lead:** skip OTT, add RC-20 Retro Color wobble + slap delay — the synthwave lane.

## From videos

- **A thin, mono foundation (bass + lead synth both in mono) is used specifically to leave room for the vocal, with new elements staggered a bar early and panned to build width once room is needed** — see the inline 🎬 note in §2 above. → Width and Stereo — loner, [James Blake's production tricks are GAMECHANGING!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9FX7p23hSlc)

## Sources

Disclosure — [NO CAP](https://youtu.be/kz5dmb3QdI8) · [Deeper](https://youtu.be/SM0FZ58ckVw) · [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU) · [Higher Than Ever Before](https://youtu.be/9XkHSronZck) · [Howard Is Here](https://youtu.be/gCfU5Cq9WU4) · EDMProd (OTT) — link in [FX Chain System](#/chains/system)

chains.title: Inst-Synth Group
chains.routing: [Acoustic Piano, Electric Piano, Synth Lead, Synth Bed] → Inst-Synth Group → Inst-Synth Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** All keys + synths summed — the harmonic middle of the record. This group's enemy is *cumulative low-mid buildup*: every keyboard part adds 200–500 Hz, and together they swamp a mix that soloed fine.

## Chain

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Sum carve
- Cut the summed low-mids 200–400 Hz −1 to −3 dB (the buildup only exists on the sum — this can't be done on tracks)
- **Collision-detection workflow (Pro-Q's killer diagnostic):** put a Pro-Q on the vocal bus, another here; on this one, set the analyzer's sidechain to the vocal-bus instance — the display **highlights the exact colliding frequencies in red** while both play. Cut the red zones *here* (music yields to vocal), by ear, until the vocal opens up. No more guessing where the masking is.
- Broad dip in the vocal presence zone if the section still masks the singer
- **Alt (often better):** Soothe2 sidechained from the lead vocal (soft mode, mid-channel, pre-emphasis in the vocal's range) — clears the vocal's lane dynamically and *exactly*, the modern unmasking move for dense synth beds vs vocals
- 🎬 *From video:* a more surgical alternative to the Soothe2 route above — build multiple bands on this group centered on the exact frequencies colliding with the vocal, set each **Dynamic**, and point each band's **external sidechain** at the vocal so the threshold measures the vocal's level instead of this group's own; only those targeted frequencies duck, and only while the vocal is actually singing. Push further with per-band **Stereo Placement** — one dynamic band ducking the mid image, another the side image — combining the frequency-specific duck with a stereo-imaging decision in the same move — Sage Audio, [EQ Masterclass](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iPBnL6mx9c0)
- **Why:** Step 4 of your process at its purest — EQ decisions that only make sense against the *other* groups.

### 2. Glue Compressor — Section glue
- **Ratio 2:1** (②) · **Attack 30 ms** (③) · **Release Auto** (④) · **Threshold for ~1.5 dB GR** (①) · **Makeup** to unity (⑤) · **Dry/Wet 100%** (⑦) — the section moves as one.
- **Why:** Same gentle section glue as the other groups — enough to fuse keys + pads + synths into one layer, light enough that no single part's dynamics get flattened.

## Variations
- **Synth-heavy EDM drop:** sidechain the whole group from the kick (Glue Comp external sidechain or Kickstart 2) — pumping the harmonic layer as a unit is the genre's engine.
- **Lo-fi/gentle cohesion duck (not a pump you're meant to hear):** same routing idea, much lighter touch — kick's compressor send set to **External/pre-fader ("preader")** mode so the duck amount stays constant even if the kick's own fader moves later, sidechaining the group's own Glue Compressor. Sidechain-duty settings: **knee 0, high ratio, attack instant, release ~300 ms**, threshold dialed by ear (dip extreme first to hear it, e.g. ~26 dB GR, then back off) to land **6–9 dB GR** — deliberately below the threshold of being noticed as "a sidechain happening," just felt as glue between the group and the drums. 🎬 *From video:* Max Konyi, [Final Mix & Master | Studio One LoFi Tutorial | Part 9](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-OKUCuyLBSg)

## From videos

- **Advanced mid-side EQ: dynamically duck this group's specific frequencies off an external vocal sidechain, with per-band mid/side placement** — build multiple Pro-Q 4 bands on this group centered on the exact frequencies that clash with the vocal, set each **Dynamic**, then point each band's **external sidechain** at the vocal so the threshold measures the vocal's level instead of this group's own — only those targeted frequencies duck, and only while the vocal is actually singing. Taken further: assign **Stereo Placement per band** (one dynamic band ducking the mid image, another the side image) to combine the frequency-specific duck with a stereo-imaging decision in the same move — a more surgical, per-band alternative to the Soothe2 sidechain already used on this group's sum-carve stage. → EQ, Sidechaining, Masking and Carving, Width and Stereo — Sage Audio, [EQ Masterclass](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iPBnL6mx9c0)
- **Pre-wire this group's sidechain compressor disabled, in a session template, with the kick's send already built** — as a template habit rather than a per-song setup step: park a dedicated compressor on this group specifically for sidechain duty, disabled, with the kick track's compressor-send already routed to its external sidechain input and set to pre-fader/"preader" mode ahead of time — so activating the felt-not-heard kick duck documented above (or any future song's version of it) is a single power-button click instead of rebuilding the routing from scratch. → Session Templates — Max Konyi, [The Ultimate Template Creation Guide for Studio One (or any other DAW)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eFMfip3CQcI)
- **Route the reverb sends into the same sidechain-ducked group as the instruments, not just the dry signals** — when building the felt-not-heard lo-fi duck above, every reverb feeding this group (except the one on the drums) gets summed into the group *before* the sidechain compressor, so wet tails duck along with their dry sources instead of smearing through the kick untouched — Max Konyi, [Final Mix & Master | Studio One LoFi Tutorial | Part 9](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-OKUCuyLBSg)

chains.title: Inst-Synth Bus
chains.routing: Inst-Synth Group → Inst-Synth Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Finish coat on the harmonic section. Lightest bus in the template — keys/synths arrive already polished (VSTs are pre-produced sounds).

## Chain

### 1. Sie-Q — Musical tilt
- A dB brighter or darker to seat the whole section behind the vocal.

### 2. Kramer Tape — Analog unify
- **15 ips** (④) · **Flux low** (①) · **Record low** (②) · **Playback to unity** (③)
- **Why:** running every digital instrument through the same tape stage gives sample-based and synthesized parts one shared "recorded" texture — the cheapest cohesion available.

### 3. Bus glue for presence, not squash — a UA 33609 alternative
- 🎬 *From video:* Marcella Araica adds a **UA 33609** here (an "All Music" bus carrying samples, transitional risers, AND guitars together) deliberately light: "I don't want it compressing too much, I want it to breathe. It's not about really over-compressing it, just allowing it to give it more presence without it feeling like it's being [squashed]." Rode the gain by ear against the mix and pulled the guitars down slightly in the same pass — a light-glue-for-presence move, not a leveling/control move. Unowned — see Plugin Wishlist; owned stand-in for the same light-touch role is this chain's own Sie-Q/Kramer Tape pairing, or Solid Bus Comp barely engaged. Contrast with the SAME plugin dialed much harder on the drum bus in the same session — see [Drums Bus](#/chain/drums-bus) and Compression Staging. → Committing and Printing, Compression Staging, [Drums Bus](#/chain/drums-bus), [Guitar Bus](#/chain/guitar-bus) — Mix with the Masters (Marcella Araica), Printing stems through analog equipment with Marcella Araica

### 4. Duck the section off the vocal (add when there's a lead)
- 🎬 *From video:* Disclosure make room for a soft lead by **ducking the whole synth section off the vocal** — a compressor keyed off the vocal (via a muted empty bus), or **Soothe2 / Pro-MB in dynamic/sidechain mode** so the synths give up *exactly* the frequencies the vocal occupies (sharper than a wideband ducker like Trackspacer). **Slow release** so it flows. → Sidechaining, LEAD Slot — Disclosure, [Looking For Love](https://youtu.be/NlJt0pCptGk) / [Higher Than Ever Before](https://youtu.be/9XkHSronZck) / [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU).

## Variations
- **If this bus feels redundant:** it often is for sparse arrangements — bypass and let the group feed the master. Buses earn their place in *dense* mixes.

chains.title: 2000s R&B Piano Sample Chain
chains.routing: Piano + Analog Lab counter-melody + Splice string loop + SRX Orchestra strings + lead/harmony vocal → [[2 Inst-Synth Group|Inst-Synth Group]] / [[2 Main Vocal Group|Main Vocal Group]] → [[3 Inst-Synth Bus|Inst-Synth Bus]] / [[3 Vocal Bus|Vocal Bus]] → Master
chains.reference: 2000s R&B era (Ne-Yo "So Sick," T-Pain/Chris Brown "Best Love Song") — a from-scratch sample built, then flipped into a Tory Lanez/Bryson Tiller-style modern trap beat
plugins: Compressor → small room plate → Pro-Q 4/3 make-dynamic carve)
Analog Lab "softy lead" counter-melody (EQ → Cassette Crushed → light reverb)
lead vocal (octave-up → AlterBoy → Pro-Q 4/3 → Decapitator-if-needed → Intensity reverb → light delay)
flip stage (EQ band → short low-cut reverb → stretch/tempo-drop to ~145 BPM)
flip drums (snap → rim shot → hi-hat roll → second stabby bass)
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a from-scratch sample deliberately styled on the **2000s R&B era** — reference tracks named on-screen are Ne-Yo's "So Sick" and T-Pain/Chris Brown's "Best Love Song" — then flipped into a modern-day R&B trap beat aimed at a Tory Lanez/Bryson Tiller lane.
