Reverse-engineered from a loner (YouTube) breakdown, [how to make a 2000's r&b sample & flip it into a beat for tory lanez/bryson tiller](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPqBmZLaDM4). Distinct from [Tory Lanez Underwater Synth Chain](#/chain/tory-lanez-underwater-synth-chain) (a minimal two-melodic-element build) and [Kendrick Lamar Soul Sample Chain](#/chain/kendrick-lamar-soul-sample-chain) (heavily vintage/worn processing) — this chain's defining move is **restraint**: because the 2000s reference material "isn't too vintage," no tape/wear stage is added anywhere, keeping the piano and vocal comparatively clean while still reading as period-appropriate.

## Chain overview

Four melodic sources stack around a piano bed (piano, counter-melody, chopped string loop, second string layer for a vocal-free section), plus a full lead-and-harmony vocal — then the whole finished sample gets a 3-stage lo-fi push (EQ → reverb → stretch/tempo-drop) before a compact drum pattern (snap, rim shot, hi-hat roll, switch-up bass) turns it into a beat. The reusable core idea: **genre-appropriate restraint is itself a production decision** — skip the default aging/vintage stage when the reference material doesn't call for it — paired with a simple, repeatable "flip a finished sample" recipe (EQ → reverb → stretch) that works on the whole sample rather than per-layer.

## 1. Piano — Kontakt "Gentleman"

- **Instrument:** Kontakt's "Gentleman" patch — "super clean, super simple." → Kontakt 7
- **Chords:** built entirely from the **A minor scale (all white keys)** — "a great way to instantly get a more melodic sound" without hunting for voicings by ear. → Melody Writing, Chord Progressions
- **Voicing detail:** top-line notes double as both the part's bounce AND its melody.
- **Chain:** Compressor ("tighten the sound up, make it super together") → **small room plate reverb** (Little Plate) → Pro-Q 3 (low-end cut + a **Make Dynamic** threshold-gated carve — "almost like compression").
- **Deliberately no tape/vintage stage** — "these types of songs often have really clean sounds... not too vintage." → Sampling and Sound Selection
- 🎬 *From video:* try a single diatonic scale (all-white-keys) as a shortcut to guaranteed-melodic chords before reaching for more complex voicings. → Melody Writing

## 2. Counter-melody — Analog Lab "softy lead"

- **Source:** Arturia Analog Lab, "softy lead" preset (Layers bank) — a super simple melody. → Plugin Wishlist
- **Chain:** EQ (low-end cut) → Cassette "Crushed" preset → a pretty light reverb.
- 🎬 *From video:* keep a counter-melody deliberately plain/simple so the crush stage does the character work, rather than writing a busy line. → Melody Writing

## 3. Strings — Splice loop + SRX Orchestra

- **Layer 1 (main strings):** no VST string sound "sounded really good," so a **Splice string loop** was chopped up and layered directly on top of the piano. → Splice Sounds, Sampling and Sound Selection
- **Layer 2 (vocal-free section):** **SRX Orchestra** (unowned — see Plugin Wishlist), a simple counter-melody, used specifically to fill the space of a section with no vocals. → Arrangement and Song Form

## 4. Lead vocal + harmonies

1. **Pitch up an octave.** → Pitch and Formant
2. **Little AlterBoy** — no specific preset named.
3. **Pro-Q 3** — cut highs AND lows.
4. **Decapitator** — reached for ONLY when the vocal isn't cutting through / lacks grit. Preset: **"mild tube vox."**
5. **Reverb** — unconfirmed "Intensity" reverb, **"vocal distance sci-fi"** preset, almost all the way wet (third confirmed sighting of this named tool — see Plugin Wishlist).
6. **A super light delay** (owned-lane Echo/Delay).
- **Harmonies:** underneath the lead, hit only at the end of each 4 bars, run "pretty much exactly the same" chain. → Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs
- 🎬 *From video:* a vocal saturation/grit stage doesn't have to be a default chain step — reach for it conditionally, only when the vocal audibly needs it. → Saturation and Distortion

## 5. The flip — sample-to-beat processing

1. **EQ** — a restrained band cut (some highs, some lows, "not go too crazy"), pushing the whole finished sample toward lo-fi/distant/airy.
2. **Reverb** — kept fairly short, low end cut from the return, Size reduced.
3. **Time-stretch + tempo drop** — stretch the sample and bring the tempo down to roughly **145 BPM**.
- 🎬 *From video:* EQ → reverb → stretch/tempo-drop, applied to the WHOLE finished sample (not per-layer), is a compact 3-stage recipe for distancing an already-complete sample before drums go under it. → Sampling and Sound Selection

## 6. Flip drums

- **Snap:** the starting element, trimmed to hit only twice.
- **Rim shot:** placed in between the two snap hits.
- **Hi-hat:** one small roll, "nothing crazy."
- **Second bass (switch-up layer):** a **short and stabby** bass, layered in purely so the pattern "switches up." → Bass Design
- 🎬 *From video:* build a flip's drum pattern starting from the snap/rim-shot pair rather than the kick — a lighter, sample-forward alternative to a kick-first drum build. → Genre Drum Patterns

## Arrangement

**Two moves here, both explicitly structural:**

- **The second string layer exists to fill a vocal-free section.** SRX Orchestra plays a simple counter-melody *only* where there's no vocal — the arrangement writes the part, not the other way round.
- **The second bass is a switch-up device.** A short, stabby bass layered in purely so the pattern changes. It has no tonal job.

| Section | What carries it |
|---|---|
| With vocal | piano · counter-melody · chopped strings · lead + harmonies |
| Vocal-free | piano · **SRX counter-melody** filling the gap |
| Switch-up | + the stabby second bass |

**The move — write parts for gaps.** Both additions above are answers to "what's missing in this section," which is the opposite of writing a part and then finding somewhere to put it.

**Drums start from the snap/rim pair, not the kick** — a lighter, sample-forward build order. → Genre Drum Patterns

## Variations

- **Any clean-era reference (2000s–2010s) where the usual tape/vintage default would read wrong** — the reusable lesson is checking the reference era BEFORE reaching for the aging stage, not skipping it universally.
- **The flip recipe (EQ → reverb → stretch/tempo-drop) generalizes to any finished sample**, independent of the specific piano/vocal/string sources used here.

## Notes

- No exact EQ frequencies, reverb decay/size values, or Compressor ratio/threshold were given on screen beyond the qualitative descriptions above — treat every device's setting as a starting point to dial in by ear.
- **SRX Orchestra** is the only fully unowned instrument source in this build (Splice covers the main string layer) — see Plugin Wishlist for the current gap; every processing stage after the instrument sources is fully owned-tool coverable.
- Sibling videos in the same 2000s/trapsoul lane: [Tory Lanez Underwater Synth Chain](#/chain/tory-lanez-underwater-synth-chain) (minimal 2-element underwater synth+vocal build) and the [Bryson Tiller Vocal Chain](#/chain/bryson-tiller-vocal-chain) / the secrets behind bryson tiller's 'trapsoul' sound!? breakdown (Bryson Tiller-specific vocal treatment).

**Sources:** loner — [how to make a 2000's r&b sample & flip it into a beat for tory lanez/bryson tiller](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPqBmZLaDM4) (00:09:24, 2022-01-16) · full note: how to make a 2000's r&b sample & flip it into a beat for tory lanez-bryson tiller

chains.title: 90s R&B Sample Chain
chains.routing: Piano (9ths) + second layered keys part + 3-take vocal stack (bounced to one stem) + Battery 4 texture layer → [[2 Inst-Synth Group|Inst-Synth Group]] / [[2 Main Vocal Group|Main Vocal Group]] → [[3 Inst-Synth Bus|Inst-Synth Bus]] / [[3 Vocal Bus|Vocal Bus]] → Master
chains.reference: 90s R&B — a compact from-scratch sample built entirely with VSTs + self-recorded vocals, with a 3-take vocal stack bounced thin, a Battery 4 texture layer, and a whole-sample pitch-down/reverse finish
plugins: Piano 9th chords (EQ → Little Plate → clean chorus → layered "warm keys" pad)
main vocal (EQ → AlterBoy same-pitch/Formant -5 → reverb + slight delay)
high vocal (EQ → AlterBoy pitch-up/Formant down a little → heavy reverb)
low vocal (EQ → AlterBoy pitch-up/Formant down a lot → average reverb → Fruity Delay)
3-vocal bounce → stem EQ (lows+highs) → reverb → Arturia high-pass sweep filter
second keys layer (EQ → reverb → Fruity Delay → Cassette fuzzy-box detune)
Battery 4 texture layer (pitch down → filter highs+lows → buried low in mix)
final polish (pitch whole sample down 7 semitones → EQ cut lows → reverse a section → crossfade de-click)
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a compact, from-scratch '90s R&B sample — no real sample source, built entirely from a VST chord bed and self-recorded vocals. Reverse-engineered from an early (2020) loner breakdown, [how to make your own 90's rnb samples](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PQjIBDgJehQ), whose per-take-processing and bounce-then-thin-out logic reappear across most of this channel's later, more elaborate R&B builds already logged in this vault. Distinct from [2000s R&B Piano Sample Chain](#/chain/2000s-r-b-piano-sample-chain) (a cleaner, "not too vintage" era with restrained processing and a 4-melodic-source stack) and [Bryson Tiller Fake-Sample Chord Bed Chain](#/chain/bryson-tiller-fake-sample-chord-bed-chain) (no vocal stack at all) — this chain's defining move is **thinning the vocal stack on purpose so a future flip has room to sing over it**, not just processing three takes differently.

## Chain overview

A 9th-chord piano bed gets a short 4-stage color chain, then a completely separate second keys layer doubles the same chords with heavier processing. Three vocal takes (main/high/low), recorded with zero effects first, each get a genuinely different Little AlterBoy pitch/formant setting, then get bounced to one stem and deliberately filtered thin — the reasoning stated on-screen is that three full vocal layers would leave no room for an artist to rap or sing on the eventual flip. A pitched-down, filtered Battery 4 drum pass sits underneath purely for background nostalgia, not as a real drum part. The whole thing closes with a single pitch-down-and-reverse pass across the fully bounced sample, cleaned up with a crossfade de-click at the edit points.

## 1. Piano — 9th-chord bed

- **Chords:** four chords, "lots of ninths... that's how you get like an R&B sound" — extend every chord to a 9th rather than picking selectively. → Chord Progressions
- **Chain:** EQ (cut lows + some mids) → **plate reverb** (Little Plate) → **"clean chorus"** preset (Arturia-sourced on-screen; owned-lane Chorus-Ensemble) → a separately-layered **"warm keys"** preset (Arturia Analog Lab — unowned, see Plugin Wishlist) stacked on top "just to give it a bit more depth."
- 🎬 *From video:* stacking 9ths across a whole progression (not just the melody note) is a one-sentence, reliable shortcut to an R&B chord read. → Chord Progressions

## 2. Second keys layer — doubled chords, heavier processing

- **Source:** the same chord progression copied over, with a few extra notes added.
- **Chain:** EQ (cut lows) → reverb → **Fruity Delay** (owned-lane Delay) → **Cassette** "fuzzy box" — reached for specifically to detune the layer for "a very old-school feeling," not as a chain-ending crunch stage.

## 3. Vocals — 3-take stack, each earning a different AlterBoy setting

1. **Record raw first, zero effects, all three takes** — main, low harmonies, high notes — explicitly to prove "you don't have to be able to sing to do this." → Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs
2. **Main:** EQ (cut lows) → Little AlterBoy at the SAME pitch, Formant down 5 → reverb + a very slight delay.
3. **High:** EQ (cut lows) → AlterBoy pitched all the way up, Formant down only a little → noticeably heavier reverb than the main take, "because I want this to be more in the [mix]."
4. **Low:** EQ (cut some lows) → AlterBoy also pitched all the way up, Formant down "quite a lot" (more than the high take) → average reverb → Fruity Delay (Delay).
- 🎬 *From video:* give each take in a small vocal stack a genuinely different AlterBoy pitch/formant setting rather than one shared preset — the same lesson this channel repeats for years afterward, here in its earliest documented form. → Little AlterBoy, Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs

## 4. Bounce + thin the vocal stack

1. Mute the piano, arm disc-recording on the master channel, Alt+R to render the 3-take stack to one stem.
2. **Stem chain:** EQ (cut lows + highs) → reverb → an **Arturia high-pass sweep filter** (owned-lane Auto Filter).
- 🎬 *From video:* bounce a multi-layer vocal stack down and deliberately filter it thin — "if you were having that in a sample normally, it'd be hard for the artist to find room to hop on it." A mixing-for-flippability move, not a tone choice. → Sampling and Sound Selection, Auto Filter

## 5. Texture — Battery 4 drum pass

- A very basic pattern in **Battery 4** (unowned — see Plugin Wishlist), bounced to audio, pitched down, filtered (highs and lows cut), and buried low in the mix — "just so you can have this extra level of texture and nostalgic feeling," not a functioning drum part. → Sound Selection Guide

## 6. Final polish

1. **Pitch the whole finished sample down 7 semitones** as the literal last step across every already-balanced layer. → Pitch and Formant
2. **EQ cut the lows** the pitch-down made muddier.
3. **Reverse a section** for variation.
4. **Crossfade de-click** at every reverse/edit transition point so the cuts don't pop — owned-lane equivalent: a short fade/crossfade at the clip boundary in Ableton's clip editor. → Sampling and Sound Selection

## Arrangement

**Reverse a section for variation** — Stage 6's finishing move, and the only sectional device this build uses. The whole sample gets a pitch-down and a reversed passage rather than a second written section.

| Section | Source |
|---|---|
| Main | 9th-chord piano bed + doubled keys + 3-take vocal stack |
| Variation | a reversed section of the same material |

**The move — crossfade every reverse point.** A short fade at each clip boundary so the cuts don't pop. Unglamorous, and it's the difference between "vintage" and "edited."

**Density: 5–6, flat.** Like most sample builds here, the arrangement lives downstream in the flip — see Hip Hop - Trap § Arrangement.

## Variations

- **The "thin the stack on purpose" lesson generalizes past vocals** — any layered element meant to leave room for a later collaborator (a melodic stack, a chord bed) benefits from the same bounce-then-filter pass.
- **The whole-sample pitch-down-as-last-step move recurs across this channel's catalog** (see Pitch and Formant, [Afro Sample Chain](#/chain/afro-sample-chain)) — the semitone amount varies by build, not the position in the chain.

## Notes

- No exact EQ frequencies, reverb decay/mix values, or delay times were given on-screen beyond the qualitative descriptions above — treat every device's setting as a starting point to dial in by ear, per the video's own auto-caption-only transcript.
- **Battery 4** and the **Arturia "warm keys" Analog Lab preset** are the two unowned sources in this build — see Plugin Wishlist; every processing stage after the source instruments is fully owned-tool coverable.
- Compact/early sibling of the same channel's later, more elaborate R&B chord-bed builds: [2000s R&B Piano Sample Chain](#/chain/2000s-r-b-piano-sample-chain), [Bryson Tiller Fake-Sample Chord Bed Chain](#/chain/bryson-tiller-fake-sample-chord-bed-chain), [Soulful Sample Stacking Chain](#/chain/soulful-sample-stacking-chain).

**Sources:** loner — [how to make your own 90's rnb samples](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PQjIBDgJehQ) (00:09:01, 2020-08-24) · full note: how to make your own 90's rnb samples

chains.routing: 2x Lounge Lizard keys/pad layers + 1x Kontakt guitar counter-melody → [[2 Inst-Synth Group|Inst-Synth Group]] / [[2 Guitar Group|Guitar Group]] → [[3 Inst-Synth Bus|Inst-Synth Bus]] → Master
chains.reference: loner's own million-stream-placement sample — a 3-element afro-sample flip, reverse-engineered from his own breakdown
plugins: Lounge Lizard "blues comp" chord bed (EQ + light spring reverb)
Lounge Lizard "broken" preset → reverb + EQ + chorus + ValhallaDelay → bounce/chop → Kickstart half-time pulse + second reverb + EQ
Kontakt "Evolution Strawberry" wire-preset guitar → Bias FX amp + EQ + double chorus + ping-pong delay + room reverb
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** the exact 3-element sample loner built and sent out that ended up placed on an unnamed song with over a million streams — reverse-engineered from his own breakdown, [how i made the sample that got a 1 million stream placement (it's easier than you think!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=atjGOpxBzag). Unlike most other chains on this page (a specific artist's record being copied), this one is loner's own confirmed working sample, built specifically as an "afro sample" for another producer to develop. The processing across all three elements is deliberately plain (EQ, reverb, chorus, delay — nothing exotic); the real lesson of this chain is what got LEFT OUT (a perc loop and a horn layer, both built then cut) so the sample stayed open for a collaborator to build on. See Sampling and Sound Selection and Arrangement and Song Form for the restraint argument in full.

## Chain overview

Two AAS Lounge Lizard EP-3 layers (a dry chord bed and a heavily-processed pad built from the same chord progression) plus one Kontakt "Evolution Strawberry" guitar counter-melody. A perc loop and a horn layer were built and then deliberately removed before the sample was sent out. The whole finished mix gets pitched down 2 semitones on the master as the last step.

## 1. Chord bed — Lounge Lizard "blues comp" preset

- **Instrument:** AAS Lounge Lizard EP-3, "blues comp" preset. No owned electric-piano VST equivalent tracked — see Plugin Wishlist.
- **Chords:** F major → G major (C passing note) → A minor → D passing note → E minor (pitched up an octave to match the preceding chord). Two majors then two minors, a deliberate melodic→emotional arc. → Melody Writing
- **Feel:** strummed (not block-triggered) for a natural feel, with deliberate gaps left between chord hits — the simplicity is what makes the gaps stand out, giving the part "bounce" before drums are even added. → Rhythm and Groove, Pocket and Microtiming
- **FX:** EQ Eight cutting low end + some mid-range, then a light spring reverb (owned lane: ValhallaVintageVerb spring-modeled algorithm, or UAD RealVerb-Pro). *(general starting point — no specific frequencies given)* → EQ, Reverb

## 2. Pad — Lounge Lizard "broken" preset, manipulated

- **Instrument:** same plugin, "broken" preset — "I use this all the time," per loner — copying the Step 1 chord progression but placed slightly differently rhythmically.
- **Pre-bounce chain:** reverb (preset named "clean chorus," mix ~50%) → EQ Eight cut low → Chorus-Ensemble for width → ValhallaDelay for texture.
- **Bounce + rechop:** bounce the processed layer to audio, then chop it up and re-place the pieces slightly differently — a second manipulation pass distinct from the FX chain, and the step that actually turns a keys sound into a pad.
- **Post-bounce chain:** Kickstart 2 set to pulse at half time → a SECOND, different-type reverb → a final EQ cutting both low AND high end (narrowing it into a supporting textural layer). → Sampling and Sound Selection
- 🎬 *From video:* bounce-then-chop is the actual pad-making move here — the pre-bounce FX chain alone (reverb/EQ/chorus/delay) wouldn't have gotten there on its own.

## 3. Guitar counter-melody — Kontakt "Evolution Strawberry," wire preset

- **Instrument:** Kontakt 7, "Evolution Strawberry" bank, "wire" preset. Played dry first to establish tone. → Kontakt 7
- **FX chain:** Bias FX guitar-amp plugin ("between us" preset, unowned — see Plugin Wishlist) → EQ Eight cutting low + mid-range → Chorus-Ensemble with BOTH factory chorus presets stacked ("to make it super wide") → light ping-pong-mode delay (width tool, not an audible echo) → room reverb closing the chain. → Saturation and Distortion, Delay, Width and Stereo

## 4. What got cut (the headline lesson)

- **A percussion loop** — built, then removed specifically because keeping it would pre-commit the eventual collaborator's own drum programming; loner wanted the other producer to have full creative control over the drums.
- **A horn layer** — built, then muted/cut after loner caught himself adding it "just to flex my muscles as a producer" rather than because the sample needed it — a named trap of getting caught up in what other producers' samples sound like.
- Both cuts are framed as directly responsible for the placement: keeping either would have left no room for the eventual producer ("a producer tempo," per the captions) to add the melodic elements and transitions that filled out the finished song. → Sampling and Sound Selection, Arrangement and Song Form, Ear Candy and Hiding Synths

## 5. Finishing move

- **Pitch the ENTIRE finished sample down 2 semitones on the master**, using a "sound shifter"-type plugin (near-certainly Waves SoundShifter, already tracked on Plugin Wishlist), as the literal last step before sending it out. Owned lane: Ableton Shifter in Pitch mode. → Pitch and Formant

## Arrangement

**This sample is arranged by what got cut** — Stage 4 is the arrangement lesson, and it's the inverse of every other chain here. Two finished layers were deleted specifically so the eventual producer had room to add melodic elements and transitions. Keeping either would have pre-committed a collaborator's choices and, per the source, cost the placement.

**The move — leave slots empty on purpose.** A sample built for someone else to develop should fill BED and MIDS and stop. Filling LEAD and AIR too means there's nothing left to write.

**Density: 3 elements. That's the finished state, not a draft.**

Generalizes past afro flips to anything you're sending out — see Sampling and Sound Selection and Sound Palette's "empty slots are a choice, not a gap."

## Variations

- The two-Lounge-Lizard-layer trick (one dry chord bed, one heavily processed into a pad from the SAME progression) is reusable on any two-VST-instance keys build — cheaper than sourcing two different instruments for a "keys + pad" combo.
- The restraint discipline (build extra layers, then cut anything that pre-commits a collaborator's choices) generalizes to any sample built for someone else to develop, not just afro-genre flips — see Sampling and Sound Selection.

## Source

- loner, [how i made the sample that got a 1 million stream placement (it's easier than you think!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=atjGOpxBzag) — full breakdown: YouTube note

chains.title: Arca Piano
chains.routing: Upright Piano (Instrument Rack) → [[2 Inst-Synth Group|Inst-Synth Group]] → [[3 Inst-Synth Bus|Inst-Synth Bus]] → Master
chains.reference: Arca (sound-design study, not a specific released track), asd (YouTube breakdown channel)
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** the distressed, granular-feeling piano texture found across Arca's work — not a clean acoustic-piano chain like [Acoustic Piano Track](#/chain/acoustic-piano-track), but a deliberately degraded, constantly-moving sound-design patch built as an Instrument Rack with macros. The through-line is **stacking several independent LFO/envelope-driven movements at once** (pitch drift, chorus feedback, filter cutoff, brightness) rather than any single dramatic effect — that stacking habit is the actual "Arca sound," more than any one device setting.

**Signal source:** built entirely from Ableton stock devices (Upright Piano instrument, Glue Compressor, Chorus-Ensemble ×2, Auto Filter, Expression Control, Multiband Dynamics) — nothing here needs an unowned plugin, see Plugin Wishlist (nothing added from this video).

## Chain (signal order, top to bottom)

### 1. Upright Piano — instrument
Ableton's stock upright piano instrument as the seed sound, dropped into an Instrument Rack. First macro, named **"Intimate,"** initialized here (its own target/range wasn't specified in the source — treat as a placeholder macro to wire up later, e.g. to velocity response or mic-position character).

### 2. Reverb (Ableton) — spacious, placed BEFORE the compressor
🎬 *From video:* a spacious reverb send/insert, deliberately placed **ahead of** the Glue Compressor in the chain rather than after it (see stage 3's *Why*) — a macro maps the reverb's **Dry/Wet** for to-taste adjustment.

### 3. Glue Compressor — flatten, don't glue
🎬 *From video:* **Threshold pulled all the way down + Makeup gain cranked up** — the opposite of the gentle 1–3 dB bus-glue setting this device normally runs (compare Glue Compressor's "Used in my chains" section). Flattening the dynamic range this hard accentuates the piano's mechanical pedal/hammer noise, giving the sound a **stuffy, congested quality** — the compression itself becomes a texture generator, not a leveling tool.
- **Why reverb sits before it, not after:** because the compressor is driven this hard, it constantly "resets" between hits — and every reset **pushes the reverb's wet signal to the forefront** once the loud dry transient is clamped down. Bypassing the compressor to A/B makes this obvious: with it engaged, the reverb tail seems to **float free of the dry source**, reading as a mirage/apparition of the original piano rather than a normal room tail sitting under it. A concrete, non-mastering-context example of the same "compression exposes a quiet reverb tail" mechanism Reverb and Compression already document for mastering — here it's used deliberately as a sound-design effect, not something to avoid. → Reverb, Compression, Depth and Space

### 4. Chorus-Ensemble — instance 1, pitch drift
🎬 *From video:* set to what the source calls **"VA mode"** (the transcript's exact wording — the device's real mode options are Chorus/Ensemble/Vibrato per this note's own Key Parameters table, and the described behavior — pure pitch movement rather than delay-time chorusing — matches **Vibrato mode** most closely; flagged as a transcription-garble, not a confirmed mode name), slow LFO **Rate**, for subtle **pitch drift**. **Amount** mapped to a macro to dial the depth of pitch modulation to taste.

### 5. Chorus-Ensemble — instance 2, Classic mode
🎬 *From video:* a second, separate instance kept in **Classic** mode, **Dry/Wet at 100% (fully wet)**, **high-pass filter engaged** on the wet path so the signal's low end stays tight and undisturbed by the chorusing, slow LFO **Rate** again, but **Chorusing Amount maximized** this time (opposite of instance 1's subtle depth). **Feedback** mapped to a new macro to push the effect's intensity further. Meticulous, stacked chorus use like this (two instances, two different jobs) is called out as another Arca staple.

### 6. Auto Filter + Expression Control — velocity-linked cutoff
🎬 *From video:* Expression Control (MIDI effect) links **incoming MIDI note velocity to the Auto Filter's cutoff frequency** — higher-velocity notes open the filter, lower-velocity notes close it, so filter brightness tracks how hard each note is played. Two more macros: one for the filter's **minimum cutoff frequency**, one for the **glide time between cutoff values** via Auto Filter's **Rise and Fall** parameters (how quickly the filter slides to its new velocity-driven target rather than snapping).

### 7. Multiband Dynamics — brightness/final stage
🎬 *From video:* start from the stock **multiband compression preset**, then raise the **output level of each band** for a brighter overall tone, and shorten the **Time Scaling** parameter so all bands' attack/release envelopes are faster — squashing and brightening the signal further. **Amount** mapped to the rack's final macro slot as an overall **brightness control** for the whole patch.

## Macro rack summary

| Macro | Target | Job |
|---|---|---|
| Intimate | (unspecified in source) | placeholder — initialized first, target not detailed |
| Pitch Drift Amount | Chorus-Ensemble #1 Amount | pitch-drift depth |
| Chorus Feedback | Chorus-Ensemble #2 Feedback | chorus intensity |
| Filter Min Cutoff | Auto Filter cutoff floor | how closed the filter gets at low velocity |
| Filter Glide | Auto Filter Rise/Fall | how fast cutoff slides to its velocity target |
| Reverb Mix | Reverb Dry/Wet | space amount |
| Brightness | Multiband Dynamics Amount | overall top-end/squash |

## Arrangement

**Where it sits:** **MIDS + TEXTURE** at once — it's a degraded, constantly-moving sound-design patch, not a piano part. Treat it as a texture occupant when you decide what else can play.

**When it plays:** the macros are the arrangement. Because the rack is macro-driven, a section changes by moving one knob across it rather than by muting or adding parts — closest in kind to Psych-Pop (Tame Impala)'s global-effect-pass method.

**Watch the flattened dynamics.** Threshold down, makeup up (see the chain above) means this thing has no natural swells to shape a section with. Any dynamic contrast has to be written into the macro automation deliberately.

## Variations

- **Any acoustic/EP source, not just piano** — the reusable idea is the rack shape (compressor-driven texture → stacked chorus movement → velocity-linked filter → reverb-before-compressor mirage → multiband brightness), not the specific Upright Piano patch. Try it on [Electric Piano Track](#/chain/electric-piano-track) or a Rhodes/EP source for a similar "haunted" character.
- **Dial back for a usable mix element** — as built, this is an extreme sound-design patch (heavily flattened dynamics, maxed chorus). For something mix-ready, start from lighter Glue Compressor settings and a single chorus instance before adding the reverb-before-comp trick.

## Notes

- Not a recreation of a specific released Arca track — the source frames this as a general study of Arca's sound-design habits (stacked LFO/envelope movement as a "world-building tool"), with an explicit caution at the end against copying an artist's whole identity rather than learning from technique. That caution is captured on the video page, not repeated here.
- All-stock-plugin build — nothing to add to Plugin Wishlist from this video.

**Sources:** asd, [ableton sound design | DECONSTRUCTION STUDY [ver. 1] Arca Inspired Piano](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=equNWJvGVio) — video-derived, 2026-08-11.

chains.title: Brent Faiyaz Ambient Synth Chain
chains.routing: Chord synth + Aperture pluck-double + Aperture perc texture + 5ive&XYZ bass/fill/melody + Layers vocal chop → [[2 Inst-Synth Group|Inst-Synth Group]] / [[2 Bass Group|Bass Group]] → [[3 Inst-Synth Bus|Inst-Synth Bus]] / [[3 Bass Bus|Bass Bus]] → Master
chains.reference: A dark/moody minimal ambient R&B beat styled after Brent Faiyaz's "Mercedes" — a from-scratch build
plugins: Analog Lab Aperture "Pluck Heaven" strummed double (EQ low-cut)
5ive & XYZ kit bass one-shot (pitch slides drawn in
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a dark, moody, deliberately minimal ambient R&B beat built to sound like Brent Faiyaz's *Mercedes* — reverse-engineered from loner's breakdown, [how to make ambient synth beats for brent faiyaz (r&b music theory trick!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ugup5iVzGYY). Same restraint-first ethos as [Frank Ocean Chill Ambient Chain](#/chain/frank-ocean-chill-ambient-chain) — most individual FX chains here are 2–3 stages, and the density comes from stacking many small layers rather than heavily processing any single one. The headline move is compositional, not processing: a bare two-chord loop (see Chord Progressions) carries almost the whole harmonic weight of the beat.

## Chain overview

A two-chord harmonic bed, doubled and textured with progressively more layers, over a drum kit built around velocity-varied hi-hats and a deliberately sparse, layered snare. The reusable core idea: **keep the harmony as simple as possible (two chords, close voice-leading for tension), then build density entirely through arrangement — doubling the chords with a different-character preset, adding texture layers one at a time, and reserving processing complexity for compositional/performance details (slides, velocity, panning) rather than deep FX chains.**

## 1. Chords — vi→v natural-minor loop

- **Progression:** F♯maj7 (vi) → Fm (v) in A♯ natural minor — both diatonic, no borrowed/modal-interchange chords. Full derivation and theory reasoning → Chord Progressions.
- **Melody:** a few top-line passing notes added over the held chords, not a separate melodic layer. → Melody Writing
- **Chain:** spring reverb (heavy, kept short) → EQ (cut lows, cut some highs).
- 🎬 *From video:* "a big key to Brent's sound is simplicity" — two close-voiced chords with a major→minor quality shift generate real tension with zero functional dominant. → Chord Progressions, Reverb, EQ

## 2. Chord double — Analog Lab Aperture "Pluck Heaven"

- **Source:** Arturia Analog Lab (unowned, see Plugin Wishlist), Aperture preset bank, "Pluck Heaven" preset — "a mix of a pluck and a pad."
- **Performance:** same chords as Stage 1, played strummed rather than block-triggered.
- **Chain:** EQ, low-cut only.
- 🎬 *From video:* a doubling layer gets its own identity from preset choice + performance (strumming), not new harmony. → Plugin Wishlist, Sound Selection Guide

## 3. Texture — Aperture perc loop

- **Source:** the same Aperture bank, an unnamed perc loop, added purely for texture.
- 🎬 *From video:* one small texture layer per pass, added and left alone rather than processed further. → Ambient Texture and Field Recording

## 4. Bass — 5ive & XYZ kit one-shot

- **Source:** a "technical bass" one-shot from the 5ive & XYZ kit (vendor unconfirmed, recurring unnamed-kit source already tracked on Sound Selection Guide).
- **Why a one-shot, not a Kontakt bank:** lets pitch **slides** be drawn into the MIDI (not possible on a multisampled bank) for realism; velocity is also easy to vary.
- 🎬 *From video:* motivated directly by "a lot of Brent songs have real basses" — one-shot slides as the cheap stand-in for a real bass performance. → Bass Design, Sound Selection Guide

## 5. Drum fill — 5ive & XYZ kit, chopped perc loop

- **Source:** a perc loop from the same kit, chopped into a fill.
- **Chain:** auto-pan (slow), so it sweeps side to side.
- 🎬 *From video:* stereo width added via one moving element rather than a wide processing chain. → Width and Stereo, Modulation

## 6. Melody — 5ive & XYZ kit synth

- **Source:** a synth patch from the same kit, a simple melody placed toward the end of the 4-bar loop.
- **Chain:** Portal "Echoes" preset → half-time (1-bar setting).
- 🎬 *From video:* the Echoes preset delays the signal so the melody plays later than triggered — a reversed/echoey feel that reads almost like an accent on beat one rather than a normal phrase. → Portal

## 7. Hook vocal chop — Layers "Talk to Me"

- **Source:** the Layers kit ("my bundle," already tracked on Sound Selection Guide), a loop called "Talk to Me," picked for a close tempo match.
- **Processing:** time-stretched, then pitch-fit into the song's key.
- 🎬 *From video:* a texture layer, not a lead vocal — chosen and conformed rather than written. → Sound Selection Guide

## 8. Transition — unnamed "fill impact" texture

- A short, unnamed impact/fill sound used purely to smooth the transition into the drums/drop. No further detail given.

## 9. Drums — velocity-varied hats, spaced/layered snare

- **Hi-hats:** two layers — hat 1 straight, with velocity changed on every OTHER note for realism/bounce; hat 2 staggered, a few sparse notes underneath. → Rhythm and Groove
- **Snare:** spaced to once per bar (modeled on Brent Faiyaz's own "kind of weird" snare spacing) for rhythmic contrast against the fast hats, layered with a separate ambient percussive hit (its own reverb) to help it sit in the mix. → Snare Design
- **Rest of kit:** perc → rim shot → open hat → another perc → kick → sub bass (sub explicitly designed off a Brent Faiyaz reference sound, no further detail given).
- 🎬 *From video:* "I'd really recommend layering your snares like this especially if you're finding it hard to get the snare to sit in the mix nicely." → Snare Design, Rhythm and Groove

## Arrangement

**Two chords, and density does everything else.** Stated in the chain overview and it's the headline: keep the harmony as simple as possible (a vi→v loop with close voice-leading), then build every bit of sectional movement through *arrangement* rather than through new chords.

| Section | Layers |
|---|---|
| Intro | chord bed alone |
| Verse | + pluck double · texture · bass |
| Hook | + melody · vocal chop |
| Transition | the "fill impact" texture, then a drop back |

**The move — add one layer per section over a harmony that never changes.** The nine stages above are effectively nine arrangement slots, and the build order *is* the running order.

**Density: 1 → 7 over a two-chord loop.** The widest density swing in this folder sitting on the narrowest harmony — that contrast is the genre.

## Variations

- **The vi→v natural-minor two-chord device generalizes past this specific key** — any natural-minor scale's vi and v chords sit a semitone apart at the root with close inner voices; transpose the same relationship into any key for the same close-voice-leading tension. → Chord Progressions
- **The live-bass-one-shot-for-slides trick (Stage 4) applies to any bass patch where a Kontakt-style articulation bank would otherwise block pitch slides.**
- **The once-per-bar snare + ambient-perc layer (Stage 9) is a reusable mix-placement fix any time a snare "won't sit," independent of this beat's specific spacing choice.**

## Notes

- Several sample-kit names are auto-caption garbles carried over from other Sound Selection Guide entries ("5ive and XYZ kit," heard variously as "five and xyz kit" / "x y and five's kit") — vendor unconfirmed, treat as the same recurring unnamed kit.
- No exact numeric settings (reverb decay, EQ frequencies, auto-pan rate, half-time parameters) were given on screen beyond qualitative descriptions — treat every device's setting as a starting point to dial in by ear.

**Sources:** loner — [how to make ambient synth beats for brent faiyaz (r&b music theory trick!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ugup5iVzGYY) (00:08:10, 2021-12-05) · full note: how to make ambient synth beats for brent faiyaz (r&b music theory trick!?)

chains.reference: a '90s-R&B-style chord bed built entirely from layered VST electric pianos and processed to sound genuinely sampled — reference track Bryson Tiller's "Always Forever"
plugins: Layer 1 Rhodes (Cassette → chorus → heavy reverb → heavy delay → EQ cut lows/mids → Juno emulation heavy)
Layer 3 second Rhodes (EQ → mid-sides for width)

Analog Lab triangle lead with cutoff pulled down
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a from-scratch chord bed deliberately built to sound like a **genuine '90s R&B sample** — reference track named on-screen is Bryson Tiller's "Always Forever" — without sampling anything real. Reverse-engineered from a loner (YouTube) breakdown, [how to make smooth rnb beats for bryson tiller from scratch (no samples)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZMB_sqF_Y3Q). Distinct from [2000s R&B Piano Sample Chain](#/chain/2000s-r-b-piano-sample-chain) (a real sample-flip built from one instrument per layer, comparatively CLEAN processing appropriate to a 2000s-era reference) and [Bryson Tiller Vocal Chain](#/chain/bryson-tiller-vocal-chain) (Bryson Tiller's own lead-vocal processing style) — this chain's defining move is **fabricating the "sampled" character from scratch**: three separate electric-piano layers, each independently processed, plus a heavy dual-end EQ + reverb + tremolo pass explicitly reasoned as "if you're sampling a '90s R&B record, you're going to have to cut loads of the highs and lows" — the processing recipe IS the era simulation, not a light touch held back because the reference "isn't too vintage" (the opposite judgment call from the 2000s chain).

## Chain overview

Three electric-piano/synth layers stack into one chord bed (two separate Lounge Lizard Rhodes instances plus a Wurlitzer V2, each with its own processing recipe), a wordless 4-bar vocal chop plus a harmony chop sit on top, everything gets bounced down to two stems for easier manipulation, then the vocal stem gets a deliberate "sampled from a record" EQ/reverb/tremolo pass. The whole bed is written at a slow 80 BPM and Warp-stretched up to the final 135 BPM once the arrangement is locked. Drums are simple but bounce-focused: a shortened/pitched-down/timing-shifted hi-hat, four stacked percussion layers doing most of the actual bounce work, a deliberately spaced-out kick, and an 808 that follows the chord roots with ghost notes layered in so it never locks 1:1 with the kick.

## 1. Chord bed — three layers

1. **Layer 1 — Lounge Lizard Rhodes, basic 4-chord progression, the heaviest-processed layer.** Chain: Cassette (tape/lo-fi) → **chorus** (TAL-Chorus-LX) → heavy reverb → heavy delay → EQ (cut lows + some mids) → a **Juno emulation run "quite heavy"** — named on-screen as a free plugin (unowned; owned stand-in Model 84 Polyphonic Synthesizer, see Plugin Wishlist). → BED Slot
2. **Layer 2 — Wurlitzer V2 (Arturia Wurli V), already "watery"/washed-out, kept as background texture.** Lighter chain since the source is already soft: reverb → delay → EQ. → Plugin Wishlist, BED Slot
3. **Layer 3 — a second Lounge Lizard instance, "for more depth," same chord pattern transposed to each key of the progression.** Chain: EQ → **mid-sides** (Ghz Midside 3) for width. → Width and Stereo
- 🎬 *From video:* stack multiple instances of the SAME source instrument, each with its own distinct chain and register, rather than one layer trying to do everything — three "Rhodes" instances read as one wide, lush bed. → Layering and Stacking

## 2. Vocal chop + harmony

1. **Main chop:** a 4-bar wordless vocal run (deliberate nonsense lyrics — texture, not a topline) → Little AlterBoy (pitch all the way up, Formant down a little) → EQ (cut lows AND highs) → reverb "to drown it out, space it out." → Pitch and Formant
2. **Harmony chop:** a second layer of vocal chops behind the main run, same chain (AlterBoy → reverb → delay). → Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs
- 🎬 *From video:* AlterBoy's pitch-up/formant-down move works as well on a texture/sample-style vocal chop as it does on a lead vocal — same recipe, different musical role.

## 3. Consolidation + vocal-bus finishing

1. **Bounce down:** 2 vocal stems → 1 stem; 3 keys layers → 1 stem — explicitly to make reversing/chopping/stretching easier downstream. → Layering and Stacking
2. **Vocal bus:** new mixer channel → heavy EQ cut (a lot of both highs AND lows) → reverb → **tremolo panning side to side** (Ghz Trem Control 3).
- 🎬 *From video:* "if you're sampling a '90s R&B record, you're going to have to cut loads of the highs out and loads of the lows out" — the explicit reasoning behind the vocal bus's heavy dual-end EQ cut. → EQ, Sampling and Sound Selection

## 4. Tempo — write slow, stretch up

- Written and arranged at **80 BPM** (near the felt tempo of the "Always Forever" reference), then both keys and vocal clips switched to **Stretch/Warp mode** and the project tempo bumped to **135 BPM** once the arrangement was locked. Stated payoff: makes it easier to get a good drum bounce once the bed is already living in the faster pocket. → Rhythm and Groove

## 5. Drums

- **Hi-hat:** shorten the tail/decay drastically → pitch down → nudge timing off-grid (~half the shift range) for bounce. → Pocket and Microtiming, Genre Drum Patterns
- **Percussion:** 4 stacked layers — "where I'm getting most of the bounce from." → Layering and Stacking
- **Kick:** deliberately spaced out — the hats/perc already carry the bounce/energy.
- **808:** follows the chord progression's bass notes, plus short ghost notes between the main hits so it never locks 1:1 with the kick. → Bass Design, SUB Slot
- **Lead:** Analog Lab triangle-wave patch, cutoff pulled down (raw patch too bright) — "a very classic R&B" lead tone. → LEAD Slot
- **Riser:** a perc one-shot pitched all the way down, time-shifted, reversed — bridge-to-hook riser. → TEXTURE Slot

## 6. Arrangement

- **Intro:** reverse keys + bass + lead.
- **Verse:** sparse start (keys only, no bass) → builds to full (vocals, reverse keys, lead, bass, riser) by verse-end.
- **Hook:** vocals OUT, 808 back IN, and the key sample itself bounced to audio and **pitched all the way up** to stand in for the vocal as the hook's melodic variation. → Arrangement and Song Form

## Variations

- **The multi-instance-of-one-source layering move (three separate Lounge Lizard/Wurlitzer loads, each independently processed) generalizes to any electric-piano/pad source** — the reusable lesson is differentiated processing per instance, not the specific plugins.
- **The "cut both ends hard + reverb + tremolo = sampled from a record" vocal-bus recipe** is a reusable era-simulation move for any from-scratch part that needs to read as genuinely sampled rather than merely vintage-flavored.
- **Write-slow-then-Warp-stretch-up** generalizes to any beat where the target tempo makes the chord/vocal writing stage feel rushed — write at a comfortable slower tempo, stretch the finished bed up afterward.

## Notes

- No exact EQ frequencies, reverb decay/mix values, or delay time/feedback settings were given on screen beyond the qualitative descriptions above ("heavy," "cut the lows and some of the mids") — treat every device's setting as a starting point to dial in by ear.
- The named **free Juno emulation** plugin is unconfirmed by exact product (likely TAL-U-NO-62 given the free/Juno-60-style description) — flagged on Plugin Wishlist for identification; Model 84 Polyphonic Synthesizer is the owned Juno-106 stand-in in the meantime.
- Sibling chain in the same R&B-sample lane, same reference artist: [Bryson Tiller Vocal Chain](#/chain/bryson-tiller-vocal-chain) (his own lead-vocal treatment, a separate breakdown) and [2000s R&B Piano Sample Chain](#/chain/2000s-r-b-piano-sample-chain) (the real-sample-flip, restrained-processing counterpart to this chain's fabricate-it-from-scratch, heavy-processing approach).

**Sources:** loner — [how to make smooth rnb beats for bryson tiller from scratch (no samples)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZMB_sqF_Y3Q) (00:11:34, 2020-10-02) · full note: how to make smooth rnb beats for bryson tiller from scratch (no samples)

chains.reference: Finneas — one song's drum-and-sample build, from a solo drum-programming session outward (strings, 808, kit)
plugins: Battery drum layer (auditioned by ear) → PanMan (always-on hard-bounce auto-pan)
primary kick (sound-first selection) + a "1-and-3" second kick

chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a from-Finneas-himself breakdown of one song's build, reverse-engineered from [Creative drum sampling with Finneas](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CPROY0-0T2U) (Mix with the Masters, 2021). Unlike the fuller multi-take vocal-chain breakdowns elsewhere in this vault, this one is short and the value is concentrated in **process and philosophy** rather than exact numeric settings: a solo drum-programming session as the song's literal starting point, a stated belief that any raw sound is only a starting place ("dress it up until it's kind of unrecognizable"), and a direct compositional lesson pulled from writing "bad guy" (make the bass line itself singable). Treat every device setting below as qualitative — the video shows the signal path and reasoning, not exact parameter values.

## Chain overview

Two chain-shaped elements plus a build-order lesson: (1) a drum kit built from sound-first layering (Battery → PanMan on one layer, a two-kick pattern, and a chorus-gated character tom), and (2) a five-effect "dress it up until unrecognizable" processing stack turning a plain Output Analog Strings patch into cinematic, aged-sounding strings. A separate 808 Studio bass stage rounds out the low end. The reusable core idea: **a raw starting sound (sampled, patched, or purchased) is a beginning, not a ceiling — the payoff is in how far you're willing to process it, and a drum kit's real job is how it locks with the bassline's pocket, not how it sounds solo.**

## 1. Drum foundation — the song's actual starting point

- **Source:** the very first piece of the song, written alone, became "the main percussion element" before anything else existed.
- **Kit build:** primary kick chosen for its own sound first, then how it layers with the rest — a sparse "one and one" (downbeat-only) kick plus a second kick pattern hitting 1-and-3. Claps layered directly onto the 2-and-4 backbeat snare as one composite hit; a second snare doubled with a deliberately "crappy"-toned tom, reserved for a specific section (named as chorus) — described as reading like "20th Century Fox or something."
- 🎬 *From video:* a stated minimalism preference governs the whole kit — "I love minimalism, I love simplicity, anything that's just a wonderful foundation for other things to develop is really exciting to me." → Layering and Stacking, Kick Design, Snare Design, Arrangement and Song Form

## 2. A picked drum layer — Battery → PanMan

- **Source:** Battery (Native Instruments), his primary sampler at the time this song was written — since replaced by Logic Pro's Drum Machine Designer + Quick Sampler as his main engine. Workflow was pure auditioning: browse the library, stop on whatever "felt really interesting."
- **Chain:** PanMan, set to a continuously-active "hard bounce MIDI" pattern (not a one-off pan move) — "just takes things out of mono mania... added a real sort of depth."
- 🎬 *From video:* an instrument-engine choice can migrate over a producer's career without the earlier tool being wrong — Battery is still "adored," just superseded by a newer in-DAW option. → Plugin Wishlist, Sampling and Sound Selection, Drum Rack, Simpler

## 3. Strings — Output Analog Strings, dressed up until unrecognizable

- **Source:** Output's Analog Strings, praised specifically for its own onboard Dirt/Delay/Pitch faders ("so satisfying, and they add such a good image to the whole thing") before any outboard FX are even added.
- **Chain:** sample delay → clip distortion → ValhallaRoom → a channel EQ → Little AlterBoy (last stage, on a non-vocal source).
- **Result:** "crazy kind of messed up old sounding strings," compared directly to "some Hans Zimmer type things."
- 🎬 *From video:* the whole point is stated on camera — a plain starting patch "doesn't mean that you can't sort of change it into something kind of unrecognizable... when you dress it up, it takes on so much character and totally changes the way it actually is." → ValhallaRoom, Little AlterBoy, Sampling and Sound Selection, Sound Selection Guide, Plugin Wishlist

## 4. Bass / 808 — 808 Studio, deep envelope tweaking

- **Source:** 808 Studio (started this song before 808 Studio 2 released), reached for specifically over "finding an 808 sample and throwing it on the keyboard."
- **Processing:** "tweaked all the envelopes on this, the sub box" — a synthesis-level approach rather than a sample-plus-pitch shortcut.
- 🎬 *From video:* the pocket comes from the bass sitting on the eighth note, locked with an eighth-note hi-hat pattern (his on-screen name: "zipper") — and the bass line itself should be genuinely singable, a lesson credited directly to writing "bad guy": "you can sort of sing it in your own right, as opposed to only thinking of the vocal line as the thing that you'd sing along to." → Roland TR-808, Bass Design, Bassline Writing, Pocket and Microtiming, Plugin Wishlist

## Arrangement

**Reach for a layer only in the section that needs it.** The chorus-gated character tom in Stage 1 exists for one section and is absent everywhere else — the same principle as Sound Selection Guide's Tom Elmhirst chorus-only reinforcement entry.

| Section | Kit |
|---|---|
| Verse | sparse downbeat-only kick + composite clap/snare on 2 and 4 |
| Chorus | + the second kick pattern (1-and-3), + the character tom |

**The move — minimalism as a foundation, not an endpoint.** Finneas: *"anything that's just a wonderful foundation for other things to develop."* The kit is deliberately under-built so the arrangement has somewhere to go.

**Density: 3 → 5 drum elements.** Note how small that swing is — the drums aren't carrying the section contrast, they're leaving room for it.

## Variations

- **A hand-programmed, non-sampled "cowbell-type" clacky percussive layer, rhythmically keyed to the kick rather than pulled from a cowbell sample.** A second Finneas source (a Billie Eilish vocal-production breakdown, not this video) describes a percussion layer explicitly NOT built from a cowbell sample — "not that complicated," but functioning rhythmically the way a cowbell would relative to the kick drum, adding what he calls "a little bit more neck." Thin on synthesis/programming specifics, logged qualitatively as a second confirmed instance of Finneas building small non-sampled percussive texture layers rather than always reaching for a sample. → Layering and Stacking, Kick Design — Mix with the Masters (Finneas), Vocal production for Billie Eilish by Finneas
- **The "dress it up until unrecognizable" philosophy (Stage 3) generalizes past strings** — any plain patch/sample/keyboard recording is a candidate for a multi-effect transformation pass, not just an instrument that already sounds "cinematic."
- **The chorus-gated character-tom move (Stage 1) is the same principle as Sound Selection Guide's Tom Elmhirst "chorus-only reinforcement" entry** — reach for an extra layer only in the section that needs it, not throughout.
- **The "singable bass line" rule (Stage 4) applies to any instrumental hook-writing situation**, not just 808 bass — write the part so someone could hum it back, not just the vocal melody.

## Notes

- No exact numeric settings (Decay/Mix on ValhallaRoom, Pitch/Formant/Drive on AlterBoy, envelope times on 808 Studio, PanMan's Offset/Width/Rate) were given on screen — every device setting above is a starting point to dial in by ear.
- A few product/song names are auto-caption-garbled: "little altar boy" (a confident homophone match for Little AlterBoy), "channel eq" (left generic — no vendor named on-screen), and a song title captioned "Various Friend" (unresolved).

**Sources:** Mix with the Masters (Finneas) — [Creative drum sampling with Finneas](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CPROY0-0T2U) (6:55, 2021-08-19) · full note: Creative drum sampling with Finneas

chains.title: Frank Ocean Chill Ambient Chain
chains.routing: Lounge Lizard chords + Kontakt flute + bell one-shot + Pianobook violin + texture perc/water SFX + MODO Bass/AmpliTube + Postcard Piano lead → [[2 Inst-Synth Group|Inst-Synth Group]] / [[2 Bass Group|Bass Group]] → [[3 Inst-Synth Bus|Inst-Synth Bus]] / [[3 Bass Bus|Bass Bus]] → Master
chains.reference: A minimal, "could be on Blonde" chill/ambient R&B beat for Frank Ocean — a from-scratch build
plugins: Kontakt Ventus Ethnic Winds flute (Reversed Rhythm reverb
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a minimal, restrained chill/ambient R&B beat built to sound like it "could be on *Blonde*" — reverse-engineered from an early (2022) loner breakdown, [how to make chill ambient beats for frank ocean (sad/melodic chord technique)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=whI75NJcom8). Unlike the richer, more heavily-processed builds in [Tory Lanez Underwater Synth Chain](#/chain/tory-lanez-underwater-synth-chain) or [Kendrick Lamar Soul Sample Chain](#/chain/kendrick-lamar-soul-sample-chain), this chain's whole ethos is stated directly on camera: **"that's the key to Frank Ocean's beats — they're all very simple, some of them are literally just one instrument and him singing over the top."** Every individual FX chain here is short (2–5 stages); the density comes from stacking many *quiet*, restrained layers rather than processing any one of them hard.

## Chain overview

Eight melodic/textural layers plus a three-piece drum kit, each kept deliberately short and simple. The reusable core idea: **write the counter-melody first (even if most of it gets cut later), keep the harmony plain (three major triads, sad only because the progression descends), then build outward with one real or organic-feeling instrument per layer, each given a short, distinct FX chain and its own space in the mix (mono+pan, EQ carving) rather than competing for the same register.**

## 1. Chords — Lounge Lizard, unedited first preset

- **Source:** AAS Lounge Lizard's very first factory preset, completely unedited.
- **Progression:** A♯ major → F major → C major — three plain major triads (3-note voicings), reading as "sad and mellow" purely because the progression descends, not because of minor harmony.
- **Processing:** a single low-end EQ cut. Nothing else.
- 🎬 *From video:* three major chords + a descending line is enough for a "sad" read on its own — don't reach for minor harmony by default. → Chord Progressions, EQ

## 2. Flute — Kontakt Ventus Ethnic Winds (ocarina)

- **Source:** the video's stated compositional order — this flute originally carried the FULL counter-melody the chords were written under; most of it got cut once the progression was locked in, leaving one short closing run.
- **Chain:** Reversed Rhythm reverb (textured) → medium ValhallaVintageVerb → half-time Cassette "Crushed" preset → EQ (low + some mids cut) → Portal "Dreamy Music Box" preset, dry/wet ~50%.
- 🎬 *From video:* a soft flute + Cassette's Crushed preset is a repeat go-to combination — "when you have a soft sound and you add this to it, it gives a nice little bit of crunch to it without doing too much and sounding too weird." → Kontakt 7, ValhallaVintageVerb, Cassette, Portal, EQ, Melody Writing

## 3. Bell synth — one-shot kit

- **Source:** an unnamed one-shot kit (auto-captioned "5 and xyz one shot kit," vendor unconfirmed).
- **Chain:** pretty heavy ValhallaDelay → medium-sized spring reverb.
- 🎬 *From video:* combine real/organic instruments with one synthy one-shot element per beat, rather than an all-organic or all-synth palette. → ValhallaDelay, Sound Selection Guide

## 4. Violin — free Pianobook Kontakt bank

- **Source:** a free violin Kontakt bank from pianobook.co.uk.
- **Chain:** EQ cut ("good hurts low high" in auto-captions, product unresolved) to darken/drown the tone → very heavy ValhallaVintageVerb → forced almost fully mono, panned hard right.
- **Why mono+pan:** "I found when it was stereo it was filling too much space, and I wanted to have its own little pocket."
- 🎬 *From video:* when a wide sampled instrument is fighting other layers for room, collapse it to mono and hard-pan it rather than EQ-carving alone. → Kontakt 7, ValhallaVintageVerb, EQ, Width and Stereo

## 5. Texture layers — perc loop + water-stream SFX

- **Perc loop:** from "one of Only Ones' kits" (a third confirmed use of the Only Ones pack on this vault), chopped for rhythmic gaps → bandpass EQ → medium reverb, kept deliberately subtle.
- **Water-stream SFX:** volume pulled way down, low end cut ("pointless having it in there" at full range).
- 🎬 *From video:* the video's explicit thesis — restraint, not more layers, is what makes texture read as "Frank Ocean." → Ambient Texture and Field Recording, EQ

## 6. Bass — MODO Bass + AmpliTube underwater preset

- **Source:** MODO Bass ("Moto Bass"), a muted, finger-plucked patch.
- **Chain:** AmpliTube's "underwater" amp-sim preset (supplies tone AND reverb character in one device) → EQ cut for muddiness.
- 🎬 *From video:* "you can hear how much of a difference that reverb on the bass adds, it gives it a super unique sound" — a one-preset amp-sim shortcut rather than a multi-device bass chain. → Bass Design, EQ, Reverb

## 7. Piano — Postcard Piano (Teletone Audio)

- **Source:** Postcard Piano, discovered via an Instagram ad.
- **Chain:** EQ (cut low AND high, specifically to separate it register-wise from the Lounge Lizard/Rhodes chord bed) → valve compressor (UAD Tube-Tech CL 1B mkII best-match) → ValhallaVintageVerb → ValhallaDelay.
- 🎬 *From video:* "I wanted to separate it from the Roads, so I added this EQ cutting the low end and cut some high end as well" — a register-carving EQ move as the FIRST stage when two harmonic layers share a beat. → EQ, UAD Tube-Tech CL 1B mkII, ValhallaVintageVerb, ValhallaDelay, Layering and Stacking

## 8. Drums — minimalistic and textural

- **Rim shot:** pitched down two semitones → a delay tuned to sound bit-crushed (wet/level down, low-pass with cutoff brought down, two further degrade-style knobs pulled down).
- **Stick:** layered under the snare, barely audible — presence, not a heard element.
- **Kicks:** two, the second deliberately lighter/more textural than the first.
- **Hi-hat:** very light, with an end-of-pattern roll set to 1/3-step subdivisions for an off-grid feel, finished with a fruity phaser (Phaser-Flanger best-match).
- 🎬 *From video:* build the whole kit around restraint — no element is a full sound-design pass, each is one or two small moves. → Delay, Saturation and Distortion, Kick Design, Snare Design, Rhythm and Groove, Phaser-Flanger

## Arrangement

**Restraint first — eight melodic sources, almost none playing at once.** The *Blonde* quality comes from how few of these are audible in any given bar, not from the count.

| Section | What's playing |
|---|---|
| Intro | chords alone, unedited |
| Verse | chords · flute · minimal textural drums |
| Lift | + bell · violin (forced mono, hard-panned) |
| Ambient bed | perc loop + water SFX, running under everything |

**The move — hard-pan a single mono element instead of widening it.** The violin is forced to mono and thrown to one side. Placement does the work width tools would do, and it keeps the center clear for the voice — the same logic as Stereo Field's MIDS opposing-pairs rule.

**Density: 2 → 5, and the drums stay textural throughout.** Same restraint-first ethos as [Brent Faiyaz Ambient Synth Chain](#/chain/brent-faiyaz-ambient-synth-chain); both are density genres running at a low ceiling.

## Variations

- **The "counter-melody first, trim it down to almost nothing" writing method generalizes beyond this beat** — a scaffold melody doesn't need to survive into the final mix to have done its compositional job.
- **The mono+hard-pan move for a wide sampled instrument (Stage 4) is reusable any time a real-instrument layer is fighting a dense mix for stereo room.**
- **The register-separation EQ move (Stage 7: cut low AND high to clear space from a co-occupying chord bed) generalizes to any two harmonic layers sharing a beat.**

## Notes

- Several plugin/sample-source names are ambiguous in the auto-captions and flagged rather than guessed: the violin's EQ ("good hurts low high"), the one-shot kit ("5 and xyz"), and the exact device/parameters behind the rim shot's bit-crushed delay repeats.
- No exact numeric settings (reverb decay/wet%, delay time/feedback, EQ frequencies, compressor ratio/threshold) were given on screen beyond the qualitative descriptions above — treat every device's setting as a starting point to dial in by ear.

**Sources:** loner — [how to make chill ambient beats for frank ocean (sad/melodic chord technique)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=whI75NJcom8) (00:08:31, 2022-02-20) · full note: how to make chill ambient beats for frank ocean (sad-melodic chord technique)

chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a from-scratch "vintage sample" built to sound like a genuinely old chopped record, then flipped into a hard, dark trap beat for Future. Reverse-engineered from a loner (YouTube) breakdown, [this is how frank dukes & cubeatz make vintage samples in 2022!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nak-TAIPQ-c) — despite the title, this is loner's own build, not an actual Frank Dukes/CUBEATZ session. Nine layered elements stack into one sample before the whole thing is bounced and chopped. Unlike [Kendrick Lamar Soul Sample Chain](#/chain/kendrick-lamar-soul-sample-chain) (piano-centric, 3-part vocal harmony stack), this build's centerpiece ideas are **semitone-close chord voicing for tension**, **room-preset reverb on real-instrument samples**, and **giving each vocal layer in a stack its own distinct processing chain** rather than one copied chain. See Plugin Wishlist for every unresolved instrument/plugin name in this chain.

## Chain overview

Nine elements — a Rhodes-style chord bed, a doubled vintage-upright piano, a bass, an accent hit, a violin melody, a texture layer, two perc loops, two differently-processed vocal loops, and a reversed/chopped guitar — are built up individually, then the whole mix is bounced into a beat-slicer, pitched down 9 semitones, and chopped by ear into a beat, finished with a simple programmed drum layer. The two biggest reusable ideas: **voice a repeating chord shape so only the top note moves, always by a semitone**, and **treat "give every vocal/instrument layer its own distinguishing chain" as a rule, not an accident** — no two layers in this build share an identical processing chain.

## 1. Chords — Arturia Wurli V2 ("funky cat" preset)

- **Instrument:** Arturia Wurli V2, "funky cat" preset (heard/captioned "Whirly V2" — see Plugin Wishlist).
- **Voicing:** all three chords are the same D♯m shape (the last a G♯m), only the top note changes each time — bar 1–4 the top line walks up, bar 5–8 it walks back down. Every top-line move lands a semitone from an adjacent chord tone, which is where the "creepy, eerie, mysterious" tension comes from. → Chord Inversions
- 🎬 *From video:* "these two notes are only a semitone apart... it's just creating real tension and mystery" — a reusable voicing principle independent of the specific chord.

## 2. Chords FX chain

- A tape-cassette color stage FIRST, noise turned off — see Cassette.
- **Room-preset reverb** (small/reflective, small decay, high wet) — NOT hall/plate. "Use room presets when you're picking a reverb, especially if you're using a sample with real instruments like a piano or Rhodes." → ValhallaVintageVerb, Reverb
- **EQ** (cut low end) → **dynamic EQ** (knocks down two identified resonant peaks) → **valve compressor** (mix pulled back so it doesn't over-tighten). → EQ, Compression
- 🎬 *From video:* static EQ handles broad shaping; the dynamic-EQ stage right after mops up specific problem peaks a static cut can't reach cleanly.

## 3. Doubled piano — "SSS Vintage Upright"

- **Instrument:** "SSS Vintage Upright" (see Plugin Wishlist — second confirmed use of this exact name), copying the same chords an octave up, chosen for its deliberately imperfect/old character.
- **Processing:** velocities pulled down significantly → pushed toward mono (not fully) → panned right → ValhallaVintageVerb (ambient room preset, short, high mix) → AudioThing Speakers (radio/mic/bathroom-style emulation, see Plugin Wishlist) → AudioThing Reels ("Excited Tape" preset, wow/flutter pushed up for detune) → Pro-Q 4 (high-cut) → delay.
- 🎬 *From video:* automate the reverb's wet/dry mix UP under the last four bars, where only one chord is hitting — the space should track arrangement density, not stay static. → Automation, Depth and Space

## 4. Bass — Scarbee Rickenbacker

- **Instrument:** NI Scarbee Rickenbacker (in owned Kontakt 7) — second confirmed use, see Sound Selection Guide.
- 🎬 *From video:* a walk-down fill + a short connective phrase sell the part as "realistic," more than tone choice alone. → Bassline Writing
- 🎬 *From video:* track in a HIGHER-than-usual octave, then pitch the whole part down afterward — the register move itself (not just the final pitch) is what produces the texture. → Bass Design, Pitch and Formant

## 5. Accent — "Layers Volume 2" one-shot

- A single one-shot hit landed on the bass note's downbeat, then half-timed to sit lower/less busy. → Rhythm and Groove, Plugin Wishlist

## 6. Violin — Embertone Joshua Bell

- **Instrument:** Embertone Joshua Bell violin, **harmonic** articulation preset — reads closer to a flute than a violin (soft, airy, minimal attack). A very simple melody, short reverb to close. No owned equivalent — see Plugin Wishlist. → Melody Writing

## 7. Texture layer

- A subtle texture bed added purely for depth. → Ambient Texture and Field Recording

## 8. Perc loops — Splice

- Two Splice perc loops (a simple drum bounce + a small transitional fill), both filtered to sit under the main elements. → Sampling and Sound Selection

## 9. Vocals — 2 Splice loops, 2 DIFFERENT chains

Both loops first run through the **double-time stretch trick** (credited to Hicks): stretch a vocal loop to double its length in a beat-slicer for an instant warped/vintage read. Owned-lane mechanism: Ableton clip Warp mode (Complex/Complex Pro), drag the clip's right edge to double its length. → Sampling and Sound Selection

- **Loop 1:** short-but-heavy delay → ValhallaDelay "reverse pitch" 4-bar reverse-loop preset (mix pulled well down, since the repeats land off-time) → EQ (cut a little low, a little high).
- **Loop 2 (underneath):** a DIFFERENT chain — plate reverb (ValhallaPlate) → a heavier/longer delay than loop 1's → more filtering, with more high end taken away.
- 🎬 *From video:* credited to Corbinian's Nami/CUBEATZ sample-style breakdowns — "different vocals have different effects, some have lots of delay, some don't." Give every vocal layer in a stack its own distinguishing chain rather than copying one chain across all of them. → Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs

## 10. Guitar — reversed granular chop

- **Trick (credited to Simbo, Split Mind):** reverse the guitar → random-chop it into many small pieces → select all → nudge the whole selection back "maybe two little clicks" → set to Generic mode for a click-free crossfade. A granular-blur effect distinct from a plain reverse. Owned-lane equivalent: Ableton clip Warp mode set to Beats, slice heavily, select-all + nudge, Complex/Complex Pro for the crossfade behavior. → Sampling and Sound Selection
- **Finishing:** Shaper (ShaperBox-style pulse) → reverb (full mix, but short) → tremolo panning side to side as the final stage. → Reverb, Modulation, Width and Stereo

## 11. Finishing chop + drums

1. Bounce the full 9-element sample.
2. Load into a beat-slicer (Fruity Slicer, beat-slicing mode for even chops — owned-lane Simpler Slice Playback Mode or Ableton's Slice to New MIDI Track).
3. Pitch down 9 semitones; raise attack and decay slightly.
4. **Chop by ear on a keyboard** "trying to find a bounce" — first half of the resulting beat left sparser, second half repeats the same chop pattern with more elements layered back in.
5. **Drums:** clap → hi-hats → clap layered with a snare (for grip) → a second snare → 808 → kick → an open hat as a one-off switch-up. → Genre Drum Patterns

## Arrangement

**Space tracks density, not the other way round.** The reusable arrangement move from Stage 3: automate the reverb's wet/dry **up** under the last four bars, where only one chord is hitting. A sparse passage needs more space, not the same amount — static reverb across a whole loop is what makes thin sections sound thin.

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Build | nine elements written and processed individually |
| Bounce | the whole mix printed to one stem |
| Flip | pitched down **9 semitones**, sliced, re-chopped as the beat |

**The move — the arrangement happens after the bounce.** Everything up to the flip is sound design. Section structure is decided by *which slices go where*, which is why the sample only needs to be four or eight bars long.

**Density: 9 elements collapsing to 1 stem, then chopped.** See Hip Hop - Trap § Arrangement for what happens to it downstream.

## Variations

- **The semitone-top-line chord-voicing trick generalizes past D♯m/G♯m** — any minor-key vintage chord bed can borrow the "only the top note moves, always by a semitone" shape for the same tension.
- **Cross-reference: the near-identical D♯m → G♯m(iv) chord shape recurs in a separate loner video** ([how southside makes dark synth trap beats for future from scratch (dark melody music theory)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TVjyuF5-xUo)) — same two chord tones a semitone apart, same iv-chord resolution — almost certainly loner's recurring "Southside dark trap" teaching example rather than a coincidence. That video's build is a straight synth-pad trap instrumental (not a sample-flip-then-chop), documented separately as [Southside Dark Synth Trap Chain](#/chain/southside-dark-synth-trap-chain); full worked chord example on Chord Progressions.
- **The per-layer-distinct-chain rule** (vocals here, but also true of the piano/doubled-piano pair and the two perc loops) is the single most reusable idea in this build — reach for it on any multi-layer stack, not just vocals.

## Notes

- No exact EQ frequencies, compressor ratios, reverb decay/mix percentages, or delay time/feedback values were given on screen beyond the qualitative descriptions above — treat every device's setting as a starting point to dial in by ear.
- All-unowned instrument sources (Arturia Wurli V, "SSS Vintage Upright," Embertone Joshua Bell, AudioThing Speakers/Reels, "Layers Volume 2") — see Plugin Wishlist for the current gaps; the processing stages around them (EQ, delay, reverb, compression, tremolo) are fully owned-tool coverable.

**Sources:** loner — [this is how frank dukes & cubeatz make vintage samples in 2022!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nak-TAIPQ-c) (00:11:50, 2022-05-01) · full note: loner - this is how frank dukes & cubeatz make vintage samples in 2022!?

chains.title: Jetsonmade Bouncy Melodic Sample Chain
chains.routing: Mallet + bell + percussion + Analog Lab texture + sub-fill + vocal chop → [[2 Inst-Synth Group|Inst-Synth Group]] / [[2 Main Vocal Group|Main Vocal Group]] / [[2 Drums Group|Drums Group]] → [[3 Inst-Synth Bus|Inst-Synth Bus]] → [[Master Chain|Master]]
chains.reference: bouncy, melodic Playboi Carti/Lil Keed-style trap beat, built from scratch
plugins: drum-kit perk one-shot + EQ hi/lo-cut + heavy reverb
embedded 808 extracted from the finished bounce
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a from-scratch, "oozy," bouncy melodic trap beat built in the style of jetsonmade's work for Playboi Carti and Lil Keed. Reverse-engineered from a loner (YouTube) breakdown, [how jetsonmade makes bouncy/melodic beats for playboi carti & lil keed (from scratch)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OQZbvASWIQE) — a loner build in jetsonmade's style, not an actual jetsonmade session. Unlike the vintage/soul-sample chains elsewhere in this folder (which build toward an old-record character), this build's centerpiece ideas are **structuring a sample-for-flip like an actual song** (hook + verse, signaled purely by reverse/pitch-down processing rather than new material), and a genuinely counterintuitive drum decision: **skip the kick entirely and extract the bassline from the sample's own bounce** rather than programming a fresh 808.

## Chain overview

Five melodic/textural layers (mallet, bell, two percussion layers, a felt-not-heard sub-fill) stack around a self-recorded, heavily processed vocal chop to form the sample; the whole thing is then bounced, and a reversed/pitched-down-an-octave "verse" version is built from the same material. Drums, added afterward in a fresh project, stay deliberately minimal — the sample already carries the bounce, and the beat's bass comes from the sample itself rather than a new 808.

## 1. Mallet lead — Kontakt

- **Instrument:** Kontakt, unnamed mallet patch. → Kontakt 7, Sound Selection Guide
- **FX:** EQ, lows cut. → EQ
- 🎬 *From video:* already bounced to audio by the time of the walkthrough — its live chain isn't shown beyond the stated low-cut move.

## 2. Percussion layer 1 — drum-kit "perk"

- A percussion one-shot from a drum-kit pack, EQ'd with both highs AND lows cut, then a lot of reverb added — pure texture, not rhythmic weight. → EQ, Reverb (effect), Sound Selection Guide

## 3. Percussion layer 2 — Analog Lab shaker + bowl

- **Instrument:** Arturia Analog Lab, a combined shaker + bowl preset, found by clicking through presets until one had "a really cool cool sound, a cool texture." → Sound Selection Guide, Plugin Wishlist

## 4. Sub-fill layer (felt, not heard)

- An element added underneath the mallet purely to fill the low and low-mid frequencies — "you can hardly even hear it but it just fills up the lower frequencies and the mid frequencies." → Layering and Stacking, SUB Slot, BASS Slot

## 5. Bell accent

- A second, higher-frequency element with more attack/harshness than the mallet, added purely for extra bite. → Layering and Stacking, Sound Selection Guide

## 6. Stab bass

- A frequently-reused preset (auto-captioned "knits her base"/"knitter bass," exact source unconfirmed), release brought down for a short, stabby character. *(low confidence on the preset name)* → Bass Design, Sound Selection Guide

## 7. Vocal chop — two self-recorded takes

- **Take 1 & 2 shared base chain:** Little AlterBoy → heavy EQ ("trying to drown out... because obviously I can't sing, so it's drowning out the bad frequencies") → heavy reverb. → EQ, Reverb (effect)
- **Take 2's distinguishing move:** a tremolo control panning the vocal side-to-side, plus a bit of delay. → Ghz Trem Control 3, Modulation, Delay (effect)
- 🎬 *From video:* bounce both takes to one audio stem, double-time it (stretch to 2x speed), chop to fit the other elements, then reverse just the last two small chopped parts for a late variation. → Sampling and Sound Selection, Vocal Stacks and Ad-libs

## 8. Verse version — reverse + octave-down

- Reverse and re-chop the main mallet part to match its original rhythmic pattern, then pitch the WHOLE thing down one octave — used specifically to signal the verse section, not as a tone choice.
- Vocals pitched down to match at the same point, so hook and verse share sonic identity but read as clearly different energy.
- A declick/degrade pass removes pops introduced by the heavy chopping. *(specific tool name garbled in auto-captions — general lesson only)*
- → Pitch and Formant, Arrangement and Song Form, Sampling and Sound Selection

## 9. Structuring for handoff

- The whole sample is built like an actual song (hook + verse) specifically so a producer flipping/buying it already knows how to build on it — "it gives the producer who's flipping it, they know how to structure it, it's already done for them." → Arrangement and Song Form, Sampling and Sound Selection

## 10. Drums — deliberately minimal

- **Build:** clap + a basic hi-hat with a few rolls, velocity varied, plus some low notes following the chords' root notes/bounce.
- **No extra percussion** — "Uzi's beats are normally very open."
- **No kick at all** — the embedded 808/bass already has a heavy attack; "finding a kick that matches over the top of that is quite difficult," so it's left out entirely and the 808 alone "already hits."
- **Bassline:** rather than programming a new 808, the bass baked into the finished bounced sample is isolated (right-click → extract) and dragged across the arrangement as the beat's own bassline.
- → Genre Drum Patterns, Bass Design, Kick Design

## Arrangement
