- 🎬 *From video:* a fifth confirmation of restraint as the default, with one named exception spelled out in full — on an analog-recorded band track, "there's no gouging of EQ," most guitar layers get only a top-end touch or nothing at all. The one deliberate EQ move given: main guitars get a **tight, narrow +6 dB bump around 700 Hz** specifically to make the tone "bark," plus HPF and a little top end — "a very tight curve, because I want it to kind of bark." A bridge-guitar layer on the same session got literally zero EQ ("this guitar just sounds great, so I didn't need to do anything to it other than gain it"). → EQ, [Guitar Group](#/chain/guitar-group) — Mix with the Masters (Tom Lord-Alge), Bass and Guitar sound with Tom Lord-Alge

### 4. Ghz Tupe 3 — Tube color
- **Tube 30%** (① — low–medium) · **Tilt neutral** (②) · **Output matched to input** (⑤) · **Mix 100%** (④)
- **Why:** Restores the "pushed amp" harmonics after corrective cleanup; before the comp so the 1176 glues the colored tone.

### 5. Ghz Tone Control 3 — Broad tone
- **Tilt slightly dark** (⑤) / **Treble −1.5 dB** (③) to seat it against the vocal — guitars usually give up 2–5 kHz where the vocal lives (Masking and Carving).

### 6. UAD UA 1176LN — Compression
- 4:1 · attack slow (counter-clockwise — knobs run backwards) · release fast · **2–4 dB GR** · no threshold — work input/output toward each other; sidechain filter ON if palm-muted lows pump it
- **Why:** Slow attack lets the pick through, fast release adds sustain and attitude — the classic 1176-on-guitar move. Last in chain to even out the tone stages.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- Most amp takes want nothing — the character was printed at the amp/pedals.
- 🎬 *From video:* a third confirmation of this rule — "no EQ, no compression, no plugins on the guitar tracks themselves; all the character is printed at the amp/pedal stage." — Jack Ruch, [My Home Recording Setup for Guitar](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KYTGFneEJ2A)
- **RC-20 Retro Color** for a lo-fi layer under a produced track: Wobble 10–15%, MIX ~30%.
- Cut the ~**15 kHz** super-highs when stacking multiple guitar layers — stacked top-octave junk becomes "white-noise ringing" (handled at [Guitar Group](#/chain/guitar-group) if not here) — [How to Make a Guitar Sample](https://youtu.be/i86bG2OsOSQ).

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Electric Guitar → [Guitar Group](#/chain/guitar-group) → [Guitar Bus](#/chain/guitar-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)** — section carve at the group, tape/glue at the bus.

- **[Reverb Send Room](#/chain/reverb-send-room)** to place it · **[Delay Send Other](#/chain/delay-send-other)** for leads · **[Width Send](#/chain/width-send)** on singles that need to feel doubled (a real double from §2 always wins).
- 🎬 *From video:* a guitar-solo "arrival" recipe — dual synced delay (eighth-note + a longer, roughly-quarter-note repeat) run together with a touch of reverb underneath, plus [Width Send](#/chain/width-send) for a micro-pitch widener — see EchoBoy and MicroShift for the full owned-lane recipe — Mix with the Masters (Chris Lord-Alge), Mixing Muse Guitars - Chris Lord-Alge.
- 🎬 *From video:* for a Mk.gee-style "controlled chaos" alternative send — a distorted reverb that only fires on the loudest notes, gated first in the send chain — see [Mk.gee Baritone Guitar Chain](#/chain/mk-gee-baritone-guitar-chain).

## Variations

- **Beatles lane:** SM57 only, Kramer Tape instead of Tupe 3, compress harder (LALA after the 1176) for that squashed AM sweetness.
- **Funk/tight:** faster 1176 attack (5–6) to clip the pick attack down, HPF up to 120 Hz.

## From videos

- **A "one guitar sound" built from several simultaneous tracked layers — multiple room mics on the amp plus a separate DI fuzz track — needs its own phase check once the DI layer is added, distinct from a plain two-mic blend.** Chris Lord-Alge's six-track guitar sound: three room mics in one blend plus a fourth DI fuzz layer (pedal/source unclear), phase-checked and flipped against the mic'd signal (see the inline 🎬 note in §1 above) before the DI layer's "heat" could be trusted in the mix. → Phase Alignment, Layering and Stacking — Mix with the Masters (Chris Lord-Alge), Mixing Muse Guitars - Chris Lord-Alge
- **"Know when to EQ and when to leave it alone" — the organizing principle for a full analog-recorded band's guitar pass, with a deliberately thinned intro guitar as the one section that gets real, arrangement-motivated processing.** Because the source is an analog recording, "there's no gouging of EQ" — most tracks get a top-end touch or nothing. The intro guitar is the exception: HPF + a boost around 6–7 kHz to make it thinner than its natural tone, justified by A/B'ing against the original mix ("I did reference the original mix... I felt it was just a little too chubby, so I made it a little bit thinner") and by an arrangement reason — "we're building as this track goes along, so that when the band does come in we have somewhere to go." Also: gain trims done with the plugin's own input/output, not the fader, "so in case I bump it, I know where it is." Full breakdown (extra-guitar channel/pan convention, main-guitar bark EQ, octave-guitar compression) on [Guitar Group](#/chain/guitar-group). → EQ, Gain Staging, Arrangement and Song Form, [Guitar Group](#/chain/guitar-group) — Mix with the Masters (Tom Lord-Alge), Bass and Guitar sound with Tom Lord-Alge
- **A dial-in-focused companion video from the same channel adds the actual pedal-volume-balancing method this chain's inline notes reference above.** No new signal path here — same small-clean-Fender-platform philosophy — but the reusable content is the *how*: boost volume set slightly louder than clean rhythm volume; overdrive volume pushed louder than feels necessary alone to compensate for perceived volume loss from the pedal's own compression once a full band is playing; tone controls set per guitar/pickup rather than fixed; and pedal settings re-tuned whenever the amp's own volume changes (louder amp = less headroom = pedal settings come back down). Full detail on the inline 🎬 note in §1 above. — Jack Ruch, [Dial In Your Amps and Pedals for Great Clean and Overdriven TONES!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=45s77xBLZBU)
- **A second full home-studio guitar rig lands remarkably close to this chain's own signal path — same interface family, same close mic, same two-mic-blend/clean-platform philosophy — confirming rather than replacing it.** Full chain: guitar → pedalboard → amp, mic'd with Shure SM57 + Royer 121 (ribbon, not owned) → a pair of API mic preamps → Apollo interface → computer. Same fixed, repeatable capture chain reused across every session ("the guitars change... but everything else here stays set up pretty much the same"), character baked in at the amp/pedal stage rather than rebuilt each time. See the inline 🎬 notes at §1 (clean-platform-first, two-mic blend, mic-positioning-by-ear), §3 (preamp gain staging), and §5 (near-zero track processing) above for the full detail. Boss Delay Machine settings and pedal-stacking habits from the same video are on Line 6 DL4; master-bus glue-for-small-speakers rationale on [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain). — Jack Ruch, [My Home Recording Setup for Guitar](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KYTGFneEJ2A)

## Sources

Dan Austin (pink-noise alignment), Premier Guitar (spaced pair), Bedroom Producer/Hardcore Music Studio (EQ maps) — links in [FX Chain System](#/chains/system) · Kenny Beats — [Guitar Recording Process](https://youtu.be/VruZ-A0_aZk) · [How to Make a Guitar Sample](https://youtu.be/i86bG2OsOSQ) · [Recording Without Latency](https://youtu.be/Gj4_IvHFn6g) · Jack Ruch — [My Home Recording Setup for Guitar](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KYTGFneEJ2A) · [Dial In Your Amps and Pedals for Great Clean and Overdriven TONES!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=45s77xBLZBU)

chains.title: Electric Guitar DI Track
chains.routing: Electric Guitar DI → Guitar Group → Guitar Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** DI'd Fender Stratocaster — the flexible lane (re-ampable forever, no mic bleed, silent tracking). Two sub-lanes: **amp-sim** (Archetype does the amp's job) and **no-amp-sim** (preamp character in, EQ in the box — Kenny's current default).

**Chain philosophy:** amp sim → corrective EQ → color → tone → comp. Identical logic to [Electric Guitar Amp Track](#/chain/electric-guitar-amp-track) once the "amp" exists — the sim replaces amp+mic+room, everything after treats it like a mic'd source.

## 1 — Recording Setup

- **Clean signal in > expensive guitar** — "a really cheap guitar with a really, really clean signal — processing it and making it sound great doesn't even matter." Fresh-ish strings, **tune BEFORE the effects**, direct into the Universal Audio Apollo Twin MkII Hi-Z input — Kenny Beats, [How to Make a Guitar Sample](https://youtu.be/i86bG2OsOSQ).
- **Pedals-into-DI is a legit lane:** comp pedal first (Dyna Comp-style squash, "very slept on") → dirt → straight into the preamp. **Fuzz straight DI, no amp** — a Big Muff-family fuzz (Big Muff Pi) direct into the preamp "sounds amazing" — [Guitar Recording Process](https://youtu.be/VruZ-A0_aZk).
- **Latency:** buffer ~128 while tracking; if monitoring through the sim in Ableton, arm a ghost latency track (Latency-Free Tracking).
- Levels: peaks −12 dBFS, ~−18 average (Gain Staging).

## 2 — Tracking Best Practice

- **Record the clean DI even when monitoring through a sim** — re-amp forever; no comp/EQ printed (the sim wants raw dynamics).
- **Stack immediately for width:** same part twice, panned opposite (35–50 L/R), then a **contrasting layer** on a different patch/color — Kenny's guitar-sample move. Never copy-paste a take.
- **Treat the finished loop like a SAMPLE** — pitch it, chop it, "f*** it up"; recording your own guitar loop = sample-flip freedom with zero clearance — [How to Make a Guitar Sample](https://youtu.be/i86bG2OsOSQ) → Sampling and Sound Selection. This is the comp-tool lane.
- **Mono per take;** width comes from the stacked takes, not wideners.

## 3 — Source → Ableton (UAD Console)

### 1. UAD UA 610-B — Unison preamp
- Clean for the amp-sim lane · **Alt for the no-amp-sim lane: UAD Neve 1073** driven a touch — Kenny's current default is "DI through a preamp or old mixer for character, then EQ in the box"; the 1073's iron is that character here.

### 2. UAD UA 1176LN — bypass
- The amp sim wants the raw dynamic signal; compressing before a sim changes how the "amp" breaks up.

### 3. UAD Pultec EQP-1A — bypass
- Or low ATTEN @ 60 Hz only.

## 4 — Ableton Initial Processing

### 1. Morgan Amps Suite — Amp + cab
- Neural DSP's Morgan Amplification suite — boutique, low-watt voicings built on **chimey clean headroom** and touch-sensitive edge-of-breakup (the AC-style shimmer through a Strat is the sweet spot). Pick the amp voicing for the part (①): **gain low for sparkle, up for crunch** (②).
- Light **boost/OD in front** (Klon/TS-style) for lead thickness — keep it subtle on clean parts.
- Open the **cab section** — two movable mics (ribbon + dynamic, or dual 57s), same speaker-position logic as a real cab.
- Use Neural's **output section** (doubler for an instant hard-L/R double; reverb/delay pulled back) · master out ~0 VU.
- **Why:** The sim is the sound source, not an effect — first in chain, unprocessed DI in.
- **No-amp-sim lane: skip this stage entirely** — the 610-B character from §3 + EQ below is the whole tone (Kenny: "lately I'm not using Guitar Rig or Neural DSP — real amp or preamp, then EQ it").
- *(**Stopgap** — Nate owns Archetype- John Mayer X, it's just not installed yet. Once installed, revert this stage to it: Morgan is a clean/boutique lane and won't do the Dumble-style singing lead the JM plug does. `signal_chain` head → `Archetype- John Mayer X`.)*

### 2. Pro-Q 4 — Corrective EQ
- HPF 70–100 Hz · cut 200–350 mud · narrow-cut fizz 3–6 kHz (sims fizz more than real cabs)
- Stacking layers? Shelf the ~**15 kHz** super-highs per layer — stacked DI top-octave junk becomes "white-noise ringing" — [How to Make a Guitar Sample](https://youtu.be/i86bG2OsOSQ)

### 3. Ghz Tupe 3 — Tube glue
- **Tube 20%** (① — low drive) · **Tilt neutral** (②) · **Mix 100%** (④)
- **Why:** sims can feel sterile; tube nonlinearity puts air molecules back. (Thin-DI first-aid: this + 1073 drive is the owned CLA Guitars.)

### 4. Ghz Tone Control 3 — Broad seat
- **Tilt** (⑤) darker/brighter against the vocal and the mic'd guitar — e.g. Treble −1.5 dB (③) here if the DI is the bright lane — carve the two guitar lanes apart when both are in the song.

### 5. UAD UA 1176LN — Compression
- 4:1 · slow attack, medium-fast release · 2–4 dB GR — same reasoning as the amp track.

## 5 — Track FX (optional)

- 🎬 **Reverse-guitar intro swell + ValhallaDelay Pitch mode** — record a reverse guitar part copying the same chords as the main synth part (Weeknd "Escape From LA"-style intro), then run it through **ValhallaDelay with Pitch mode selected specifically** (not tape/digital) for extra shimmering high-end texture on the swell before the beat drops. → ValhallaDelay, Depth and Space — loner, [the production secrets behind the weeknd's evolving sound!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GMeZtNImaT0)
- **The "Jai Paul" guitar-sample chain** — swap stages 1–5 for: Guitar Rig funky patch → RC-20 Retro Color (variant: + very short room verb, Flux-chorus preset with wobble pulled down, widener — Doubler4/[Width Send](#/chain/width-send)). The instant lo-fi-funk loop tone — Kenny Beats, [How to Make a Guitar Sample](https://youtu.be/i86bG2OsOSQ)
- **Chorus-Ensemble** low-mix on clean funk parts.

## 6 — Bus / Send FX (optional)

Routing: **Electric Guitar DI → [Guitar Group](#/chain/guitar-group) → [Guitar Bus](#/chain/guitar-bus) → [Master Chain](#/chain/master-chain)**.

- Sends same as [Electric Guitar Amp Track](#/chain/electric-guitar-amp-track): [Reverb Send Room](#/chain/reverb-send-room) to place · [Delay Send Other](#/chain/delay-send-other) for leads · [Width Send](#/chain/width-send) only when a real double isn't available.

## Variations

- **Clean pop/funk DI (no amp):** Pro-Q → Pro-C 2 (fast, 4–6 dB) → Chorus-Ensemble — the Nile Rodgers/city-pop lane.
- **Ambient/washy:** Archetype clean channel → heavy [Reverb Send Long](#/chain/reverb-send-long) + ValhallaShimmer insert at low mix.
- 🎬 **Print-and-repurpose: consolidate a fully-processed melodic guitar part, then reverse + chop it into a SECOND, unrelated ambient texture layer.** After the melodic chain finishes (AmpliTube "clean" → valve comp → Cassette crunch → second amp preset for presence), bounce/consolidate to audio, then reverse and chop the print on a new track; filter it super ambient (low+high cut) → heavy vintage reverb (mix heavy, decay down, size a touch smaller) → half-time — the result "almost sounds like a vocal." Owned: UAD Tube-Tech CL 1B mkII (valve comp), Cassette, EQ Eight (filter), Reverb (vintage verb), Automation (half-time). → Sampling and Sound Selection, Depth and Space — loner, [making a soulful afrobeats beat for rema & wizkid from scratch (use voice notes to start ideas!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e-KvnLXHAy4)
- **Wall-of-fuzz commit:** Big Muff Pi → 1073 (no sim, no cab) — print it.

## From videos

- **Interface gain-staging rule for guitar DI: avoid clipping the input, but don't set gain so low the amp sim/modeler is starved of signal** — an amp-sim stage expects a certain input level to "function properly," so under-gaining changes its behavior, not just its loudness. **Always record the DI in parallel with the amp/Kemper signal**, via an active DI box (20 dB pad used here) with a link/thru output feeding the amp sim/Kemper simultaneously onto a second interface channel — two stated reasons: full re-ampability if the chosen tone doesn't work out later, and a high-gain amp tone obscures exactly where a note's timing/accent falls, so the clean DI makes rhythmic mistakes far easier to hear and fix. **Tone-dialing workflow, zero-up not high-down:** start amp-sim/Kemper gain at zero and work up until it suits the playing, rather than starting hot and pulling back; named mistakes to avoid are too much gain ("just mud") and scooping all the mids (mids are "where all the meat is" of a guitar tone and scooping undermines sitting in a mix); keep every knob move small — "if you have to do really big moves, probably something in the chain isn't suited for the sound you're after." An overdrive pedal run with its OWN gain at zero works as a pre-EQ stage (tightens/compacts the DI signal before the amp sim) rather than as added distortion. → Gain Staging — BERNTH feat. Daniel Fellner, 4 BEST HOME RECORDING TRICKS! - Dialing In Your Perfect Guitar Tone

- **Run compression UNLINKED (dual-mono) to fix a right-heavy stereo signal — each channel gets its own detector, so the louder side is hit with more gain reduction and the two even out, without manual gain-riding.** "So hitting it with mono, which means you know, the left and right channel operate with their own brand through this threshold, and this was a right-heavy signal, so I'm hitting the right side with a little more compression, this is evening them out ever so slightly." Paired with a static EQ pass on the same track: a resonance pulled down ~2 dB, more midrange presence, reduced hiss, boosted low end. On a separate synth-guitar hybrid track, only light compression control was applied, EQ present but inactive — a reminder that "already sounds pretty rad" is a legitimate stopping point. → Width and Stereo, Compression, Sound Selection Guide, [Dua Lipa Vocal Chain](#/chain/dua-lipa-vocal-chain) — Mix with the Masters (Josh Gudwin), Mixing Dua Lipa's vocals with Josh Gudwin
- **Consolidate/reverse/chop a fully-processed melodic guitar print into a second ambient texture layer, filtered and vintage-reverbed until it "almost sounds like a vocal"** — see the inline 🎬 note in Variations above. → UAD Tube-Tech CL 1B mkII, Cassette, Reverb — loner, [making a soulful afrobeats beat for rema & wizkid from scratch (use voice notes to start ideas!?)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e-KvnLXHAy4)
- **Reverse-guitar intro swell + ValhallaDelay Pitch mode for extra high-end texture, sourced** — see the inline 🎬 note in §5 above. → ValhallaDelay — loner, [the production secrets behind the weeknd's evolving sound!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GMeZtNImaT0)
- **Lead-guitar chain: analog mixer drive → Guitar Rig amp sim → a tape plugin for breakup, A/B'd with/without to show how much of the "amp" character was actually coming from the tape stage, not the sim alone** — a concrete demonstration that a tape/saturation stage after an amp sim isn't optional coloring, it's doing real character work; worth A/B'ing the tape stage on/off on any amp-sim lead to hear how much it's actually contributing. → Ghz Tupe 3, Saturation and Distortion — Zach Scholz, [I Tried Recording a Song Like It's 1976](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6kA1mWeTiZc)
- **Mid-song effect switch as an arrangement move, not a whole-song setting** — switching a pedal/effects unit on specifically for one section (a guitar swell mid-tune) then back off, rather than committing an effect to the whole part — a reminder that a track FX stage can be automated per-section rather than fixed to a single choice for the entire take. Also stacked a touch of tape echo on the same lead part. → Automation — Zach Scholz, [I Tried Recording a Song Like It's 1976](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6kA1mWeTiZc)
- **Chromeo's own account confirms the "Nile Rodgers lane" above is the real Chic/Bob Clearmountain technique** — guitar straight into a preamp, zero amp, flat EQ and zero compression on the raw DI ("it already sounds kind of punchy... punchier than when you go through an amp"), pickup position 2 (bridge+middle "quack"), THEN a heavy compressor pass to exaggerate the percussive attack — matches the Pro-Q → Pro-C 2 → Chorus-Ensemble variation almost stage-for-stage. Clean direct with no compression at all is also a legitimate end tone, not just a step. — Sol State, [Get Chromeo's Guitar Sound in 5 Min.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bj2dWuFYzMQ)

## Sources

Kenny Beats — [Guitar Recording Process](https://youtu.be/VruZ-A0_aZk) · [How to Make a Guitar Sample](https://youtu.be/i86bG2OsOSQ) · Guitar World — Archetype walkthrough (link in [FX Chain System](#/chains/system)) · Zach Scholz — [I Tried Recording a Song Like It's 1976](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6kA1mWeTiZc)

chains.title: Guitar Group
chains.routing: [Electric Guitar, Electric Guitar DI, Acoustic Guitar] → Guitar Group → Guitar Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** All guitars summed. The group stage decides how the guitar *section* sits against vocals, keys, and drums — per-guitar tone is already done on the tracks.

## Chain overview
Carve → light glue. The most important guitar-group move is a *cut for the vocal*, not anything additive.

## Chain

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Section carve
- Dip 2–4 kHz −1.5 to −3 dB where the lead vocal lives — **use a dynamic node sidechained from the vocal** so guitars only duck spectrally while the vocal is present
- HPF the summed group 80–100 Hz — guitars don't need what the bass owns
- **Why:** Guitars and vocals fight over the same midrange. Dynamic carving keeps full-bodied guitars in instrumental sections and clears the lane automatically when the singing starts.
- **Alt (often better):** Soothe2 on this group, **external sidechain = the lead vocal**, soft mode, boost its band selection in the vocal's midrange — it dynamically ducks only the *exact* frequencies the vocal occupies moment-to-moment, and only in the mid channel if you set it that way. More surgical than one static/dynamic EQ node.

### 2. Glue Compressor — Section glue
- **Ratio 2:1** (②) · **Attack 30 ms** (③) · **Release Auto** (④) · **Threshold for ~1.5 dB GR** (①) · **Makeup** to unity (⑤) · **Dry/Wet 100%** (⑦)
- **Why:** Slow-attack, low-ratio bus compression makes separate guitar parts move as one section without killing strum transients — 30 ms leaves the pick attack intact so the section still sounds played, not pumped.

## Diagnosis moves (before touching EQ)
- **The mute test:** play the mix, mute the guitar group. Whatever suddenly gets clearer is what the guitars are masking — cut the guitars *there*. Bring them back louder than normal: whatever *they* bury tells you the other direction.
- **Spread the boosts:** if multiple guitar layers all got the same "magic" boost (1k / 2.5k / 5k), they're fighting each other and the vocal — give each layer a different lane.
- **Pro trick:** sidechain a touch of the snare's fundamental into the guitar group (1–2 dB, subtle) — the backbeat punches through a wall of guitars without anyone hearing the duck.

## Variations
- **Guitar-driven song (guitars ARE the hook):** skip the vocal dip, give guitars the presence lane, and carve the *synths* instead.
- **Panned wall (L/R doubles):** check the group in mono — if the center collapses, back off any wideners on the tracks.

## From videos

- **Session-organization convention: a dedicated "extra guitar" always lives on channel 16, always panned dead center, and is always more distorted than the main guitars — a named favorite habit, functioning as the song's "anchor."** Tom Lord-Alge: "this track has one of my favorite things, which is what I call the extra guitar... it always lives on channel 16 of mine and is always panned at the center — is the extra distorted guitar. It's usually a little bit more distorted than the main guitars, and it's kind of what I call the anchor." A/B'd in/out against the two main guitars: without it the intro reads thin, with it the three read as one wall of sound. Also carried a small whistle-noise texture at the song's opening on this session. → Layering and Stacking, [1 Electric Guitar Amp Track](#/chain/electric-guitar-amp-track), Bass and Guitar sound with Tom Lord-Alge — Mix with the Masters (Tom Lord-Alge), Bass and Guitar sound with Tom Lord-Alge
- **Main guitars: a tight, narrow +6 dB bump around 700 Hz specifically to make the tone "bark," plus a high-pass filter and a touch of top end — nothing more.** "I'm giving a 6 dB bump at 700, a little mid-range, knock it — a very tight curve, because I want it to kind of bark, I want that mid-range to bark." Confirmed by A/B'ing the center "extra guitar" in/out against these two main guitars (see the channel-16 entry above) — together they read as one wall, without the center layer the intro thins out. → EQ, [1 Electric Guitar Amp Track](#/chain/electric-guitar-amp-track) — Mix with the Masters (Tom Lord-Alge), Bass and Guitar sound with Tom Lord-Alge
- **Octave guitars entering at the chorus (doubling the main guitar an octave up): hard/"brick wall" compression plus deliberate bottom-end removal, because the layer read "a little too chubby" and needed "its own sound" distinct from the main guitars.** Bypassed A/B confirmed the move was doing real, audible work. The same compressor was framed as doing double duty — glue/character AND overall level placement: "the compression just leaves it at the one, and it also acts to reduce the level, put it where I want it." Judged in-context, not soloed: "we're not going to be listening to this in solo... we're going to balance it in the track so when I play it in the track it sounds exactly like it should." → Compression, [1 Electric Guitar Amp Track](#/chain/electric-guitar-amp-track) — Mix with the Masters (Tom Lord-Alge), Bass and Guitar sound with Tom Lord-Alge
- **An outro-guitar bus deliberately hit harder than the vocal-chain setting for the same plugins, with wetness dropped, because it isn't a vocal.** "Some Trash. And some Soothe. Yeah, so, this isn't a vocal, so I'm hitting it a little harder than I normally would, well for vocals. I dropped my wetness down just so it's hitting it like..." Soothe2 pushed past its vocal-chain 38% Mix; Trash (iZotope, unowned — see Plugin Wishlist) for drive/character. A separate outro live-kit-plus-guitar track ran filtering → de-essing → tape emulation/saturation into a Fatso-style tape compressor (unowned — Plugin Wishlist) for glue — "whatever feels good, do it." → Soothe2, Saturation and Distortion, Plugin Wishlist, [Dua Lipa Vocal Chain](#/chain/dua-lipa-vocal-chain) — Mix with the Masters (Josh Gudwin), Mixing Dua Lipa's vocals with Josh Gudwin
- **Cut the ~15k super-high-end when stacking guitars** — DI/electric layers each throw top-octave energy; stacked it becomes "a weird white-noise ringing thing." Shelf/LPF each layer as the stack grows — Kenny Beats, [How to Make a Guitar Sample](https://youtu.be/i86bG2OsOSQ) → Masking and Carving

chains.title: Guitar Bus
chains.routing: Guitar Group → Guitar Bus → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** Final color pass on the guitar section. In your routing, groups handle relationships and buses handle *finish* — broad tone + analog glue, nothing surgical.

## Chain overview
Musical EQ → tape → density. All gentle: the bus should be almost removable without the mix falling apart.

## Chain

### 1. Sie-Q — Musical tone
- Broad strokes only: a dB of top (Höhen) if the section is dull, a dB off the low-mids if thick
- **Why:** A character EQ makes "vibe" moves that a surgical EQ makes clinical — buses want musical, not corrective.
- 🎬 *From video:* a single shared guitar-bus EQ move used to replace duplicating the same correction on every individual guitar track — "why use twelve EQs when you can use one?" Andrew Scheps builds a dedicated guitar aux specifically for one overall mid-range presence lift, on top of (not instead of) any per-track EQ. → EQ, EQ Three — Andrew Scheps (Mix with the Masters), Mixing Guitars & Bass - Andrew Scheps
- 🎬 *From video (clicky guitar):* Disclosure's guitar-bus recipe on "Talk" — **overdrive → a note-following EQ (Surfer EQ) → a small EQ to boost the click**, on a Telecaster tracked clean through a **Neve (light drive) → DBX 160** ("the best comp for clicky guitar; I'd track through one"). Note-following EQ tracks the played note so one moving band does the work of five fixed ones. → Sound Selection Guide, wishlist: Surfer EQ / DBX 160 — Disclosure, [Talk](https://youtu.be/PBbnvElf9ac).

### 2. Kramer Tape — Tape glue
- **15 ips** (④) · **Flux low, to taste** (①) · **Record low** (②) · **Playback to unity** (③ — watch output)
- **Why:** Tape compression + harmonics is the classic "guitars glued to the record" finish — subtle rounding of transients that makes parts feel produced, not just summed.
- 🎬 *From video:* hardware validation of this exact stage — bussing several guitar parts (a strummed lead, a doubling tremolo part, a harmony line) out to a physical tape deck together and consolidating them to a stereo pass produced glue he credited directly to "tape's compression and saturation." → Sony TC-630 — Zach Scholz, [Using Analog Tape to Glue a Mix Together](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xk0LYE7HGAI)

### 3. Oxford Inflator — Density (optional)
- Effect 15–25%
- **Why:** A touch of perceived loudness so the section holds up against the drums bus without pushing faders.

## Variations
- **Add an SSL-style bus compressor ahead of this chain's tone/tape/density stages when the section needs glue, not just color.** Philippe Zdar treats an SSL-style bus comp on the guitar return as capable enough alone to mix an entire record with — "if you have only this you can still mix lots of songs with only this, you don't need all of this, of course it's just a luxury." Pairs with a same-pan wet/dry double for warmth without added width. → Compression, Width and Stereo — Philippe Zdar (Mix with the Masters), Mixing Phoenix Guitars - Philippe Zdar
- **Fold guitars into a single combined "All Music" bus instead of a dedicated guitar bus.** Marcella Araica routes guitars through the same bus as samples and transitional risers (no separate guitar bus in her signal flow) and adds one shared UA 33609 there, dialed light/breathing rather than heavy — see [Inst-Synth Bus](#/chain/inst-synth-bus) for the full settings and Committing and Printing for the printing step that precedes it. Worth reaching for on a simpler session where a dedicated guitar bus (this note's default) is more separation than the arrangement needs. → [Inst-Synth Bus](#/chain/inst-synth-bus), Compression Staging — Mix with the Masters (Marcella Araica), Printing stems through analog equipment with Marcella Araica
- **Trap/pop with sparse guitar:** bypass the whole bus — one guitar loop doesn't need section treatment.
- **Rock-forward mix:** swap Kramer for Decapitator (Style A, mix ~20%) for grit instead of gloss.
- 🎬 *From video:* route a bass part into THIS bus rather than the [Bass Bus](#/chain/bass-bus) when it needs its low end deliberately capped — Peter Katis put an electric bass guitar into the guitar bus "because I did not want it to have a lot of low end," pairing the bus's own already-gentle, non-low-end-focused tone stage with a tremolo on the bass itself (Auto Pan, see Bass Design) so the part stays present without competing with the song's real sub. A genuine cross-bus routing move, not just a processing choice — worth reaching for whenever a bass-shaped part (a guitar-bass hybrid, a bass lick meant to read thin) shouldn't get the [Bass Bus](#/chain/bass-bus)'s full low-end treatment. → Bass Design, Arrangement and Song Form — Peter Katis (Mix with the Masters), [Mix breakdown with Peter Katis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o4F2EO_KMLk)

chains.title: Beatles Psych-Rock Sample Chain
chains.reference: The Beatles / psych-rock era — a from-scratch vintage sample-flip build
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a full period-accurate psych-rock "sample" built from scratch (not sourced from a real record) — a Fender Stratocaster guitar and a Höfner violin-bass replica processed to sound like a genuine 1960s/70s recording, using real research into the actual gear the Beatles and their contemporaries used rather than a generic "vintage" preset. Reverse-engineered from a loner (YouTube) breakdown, [these 1960's production secrets will change the way you make samples!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ngz_fZraTP4). Nate owns the two lead instruments this chain is built around: Fender Stratocaster and Hofner B-Bass H-Series.

## Chain overview

Two parallel instrument chains (guitar, bass) built on real-gear research, finished with hard L/R panning to opposite sides so the two elements "fill both sides" of the stereo field rather than competing for the same space — the video's own stated first lesson from studying the era.

## Guitar chain

### 1. Amp sim
- Owned equivalent: Morgan Amps Suite. Source video used Stark (Klevgrand, unowned — see Plugin Wishlist): "British Guitar A1" amp model, voiced to Drive, "Wide Large" cabinet preset, **built-in reverb turned OFF** (a dedicated reverb stage handles that later in the chain).

### 2. Vibrato pedal
- The pedal, not the amp, is called out as the more important element for the psychedelic character. Owned equivalent: Modulation (Ableton Chorus-Ensemble / kHs Chorus in a slow, shallow vibrato-style setting — no dedicated stock vibrato pedal; a slow LFO-driven pitch wobble is the general substitute).

### 3. Artificial Double Tracking (width)
- Waves Real ADT in the source (unowned, see Plugin Wishlist) — a guitar-widening use case for ADT, distinct from ADT's usual vocal role. Owned equivalent: Doubler2 or MicroShift, see Artificial Double Tracking (ADT) for settings.

### 4. Reverb — Abbey Road Chambers
- Chosen specifically because the Beatles tracked at Abbey Road Studios — a historically-motivated pick, not just a good-sounding chamber. Owned equivalent: ValhallaVintageVerb (1970s Color, Chamber-family mode) or ValhallaPlate.

### 5. Tape delay
- Arturia tape delay in the source (unowned, see Plugin Wishlist). Owned equivalent: EchoBoy or Kramer Tape feeding Echo.

### 6. Compressor
- "Just to tighten the sound up" — general starting point, no exact ratio/threshold given. Owned: Glue Compressor or API-2500.

### 7. Vintage-mic emulation
- Waves King's Microphones, "King George V" model, 3rd preset — explicitly to compensate for period mic quality, not for character alone. No owned direct equivalent; closest is UAD Century Tube Channel Strip or UAD Neve 1073 driven for coloration ahead of an EQ roll-off (see stage 8).

### 8. Finishing EQ
- Cut the low end, boost some of the highs. Owned: EQ Eight.

### 9. Pan + width collapse
- Hard-pan to one side (right, in the source) and collapse to almost fully mono. Owned: Utility (Width near 0) + track Pan.

## Bass chain

### 1. Instrument
- Höfner 500/1 violin bass. Owned real instrument: Hofner B-Bass H-Series — DI or mic'd through Fender Blues Junior per its own note. Source video used a plugin replica ("Moto Bass," near-certainly IK Multimedia MODO Bass — unowned, see Plugin Wishlist) since a hardware Höfner wasn't tracked live for this build.

### 2. Play style
- Finger-picking, muted 100% — the damped/muted setting is what reads as period-correct (short, thumpy McCartney decay, not a ringing sustain).

### 3. Amp
- Fender Bassman replica (AmpliTube in the source — unowned, see Plugin Wishlist). Real Fender Bassman amps were the Beatles' actual bass amp.

### 4. Compression
- Waves CLA-76 (unowned, see Plugin Wishlist), described as heavy compression. Owned equivalent: UAD UA 1176LN or UAD Tube-Tech CL 1B mkII.

### 5. Vintage mic roll-off
- Applying a ~100 Hz high-pass (matching the natural roll-off of many period microphones) to the bass specifically was singled out as giving "so much more of a natural feel" — a general lesson worth applying beyond just this chain. → EQ, Vintage Gear Worklist.

### 6. Pan (opposite the guitar)
- Panned opposite the guitar for the "fill both sides" effect — kept closer to center in practice on a real mix (bass, unlike the guitar, usually needs to stay mono-safe/centered for low-end translation — see Width and Stereo's low-end-mono rule), but the source video panned it as part of the same wide-stereo demo.

## Arrangement

**Where it sits:** guitar hard-panned to one side and collapsed almost to mono; flute panned **opposite**, also near-mono; bass center; vocals pushed back. That opposing-pair placement is the arrangement — see 60s - Beatles § Arrangement and Stereo Field.

**When it plays:** period logic — parts enter on overdub passes and stay. The *Blue Jay Way* move is the one real structural stunt: bounce the vocal, reverse it, and chop two sections back in as **lead-ins** to sections.

**The move — fill both sides with different things.** Stated directly in the source: dramatic hard-panning of individual instruments, not stereo widening, is what fills out a mix. Density stays low; placement carries it.

## Notes

- **Real-gear research first, plugin second:** the video's whole method is "find out what the actual period instrument/amp/mic was, then either use it (if owned) or find the closest replica" — worth following literally here since Nate owns both lead instruments the video is built around.
- **Order matters on the guitar side:** amp → pedal (vibrato) → width (ADT) → space (reverb) → time (delay) → dynamics (compressor) → color (vintage mic sim) → tone (EQ) → placement (pan) — color/movement before space/time, dynamics/tone/placement last.
- No exact plugin settings (drive amount, vibrato rate/depth, ADT detune/delay, reverb decay, compression ratio) were shown on screen in the source video beyond the presets named above — treat every device's setting as a starting point to dial in by ear.

**Sources:** loner — [these 1960's production secrets will change the way you make samples!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ngz_fZraTP4) (00:08:04, 2022-06-12) · full note: loner - these 1960’s production secrets will change the way you make samples!?

chains.title: Dez Wright Guitar Sample Chain
chains.reference: Dez Wright — "Numbers" (A Boogie), guitar-sample flip
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a processed, textured guitar sample built for a trap/R&B flip — clicked in blind first, matched to a real guitar recording second, then run through a full color/movement/space chain rather than left dry. Reverse-engineered from a loner (YouTube) breakdown of Dez Wright's production on A Boogie's "Numbers," [dez wright's synth secrets will elevate your melodies!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_8vOz54DTiY).

## Chain overview

Write the harmony blind → identify + look up the chords → record a real guitar playing them → preamp → amp → tape saturation → flanger → spring reverb → EQ, with a separate perc loop + texture layer mixed in underneath for ambience. Every stage after the amp is a color/movement/space device, stacked in that specific order — saturation first (grit), then movement (flanger), then space (reverb), then a final tonal cleanup (EQ).

## Step 1 — Write and match the chords

1. Click in a simple chord progression using whatever placeholder sound is handy — described as "a random sound," not a considered patch choice. The point is capturing the harmony, not the tone.
2. Once a progression sounds right, identify the actual chords and look them up on a guitar chord/tab site (name not given in the source video — an unidentified tool, not a plugin).
3. Record a real guitar playing those chords (the source used a **C minor** and a **G minor** voicing) directly into the DAW.
- **Why:** writing blind first, then matching to guitar-friendly voicings, is faster than composing directly on guitar and sidesteps needing strong guitar-specific chord knowledge up front. Called out in the source as "the biggest cheat code for making guitar samples."

## Step 2 — Front-of-chain tone

### 1. Preamp
- Owned: UAD Century Tube Channel Strip. *(general starting point — no exact gain given on screen)*

### 2. Guitar amp
- Owned: Morgan Amps Suite. Amp voicing to taste; this stage sets the baseline tone before saturation/movement/space are layered on.

## Step 3 — Color, movement, space

### 3. Cassette — tape saturation
- Adds grit/warmth ahead of the movement stage. *(general starting point — no exact settings given on screen)*

### 4. Phaser-Flanger — movement
- Sits between the saturation and reverb stages — color/movement added to an already-gritty signal, before space is layered on top.

### 5. Ghz DC19 3 — spring reverb
- Use the built-in Spring section for the reverb character rather than a plate/hall/room reverb. Positioned near the end of the chain, adding space to an already fully-colored signal.

### 6. EQ Eight — finishing EQ
- Closing stage on the chain — tonal cleanup after all the color/movement/space processing, not before it.

## Step 4 — Ambience layer (parallel, not inline)

- A separate **percussion loop** and a **texture layer** are mixed in underneath the processed guitar, not inserted inline in the guitar's own chain — a companion ambience bed rather than another guitar-chain stage. → Ambient Texture and Field Recording

## Arrangement

**Where it sits:** **MIDS**, with the parallel ambience layer (Step 4) reaching into **BED** and **TEXTURE**.

**When it plays:** built as a loop for a trap/R&B flip, so the sectional work happens downstream in the chop — see Hip Hop - Trap § Arrangement. The sample's job is to be four or eight bars that survive being cut up.

**The move — parallel, not inline.** Keeping the ambience on its own layer means it can be muted per section without touching the dry guitar. An inline reverb would weld the two together and cost you that.

## Notes

- **Order matters:** saturation → movement → space → EQ is the load-bearing sequence here — each stage builds on what the previous one added rather than processing the dry signal independently.
- No exact plugin settings (gain, flanger rate/depth, reverb decay, EQ bands) were shown on screen in the source video — treat every device's setting as a starting point to dial in by ear, not a quoted spec.

**Sources:** loner — [dez wright's synth secrets will elevate your melodies!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_8vOz54DTiY) (00:07:06, 2023-06-18) · full note: loner - dez wright's synth secrets will elevate your melodies!?

chains.title: Mk.gee Baritone Guitar Chain
chains.reference: Mk.gee (Two Star & the Dream Police; "Alesis," "DNM," "How Many Miles," "CZ")
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a low, almost bass-like guitar tone that swings from clean whisper to crunched-out chaos, built entirely around one idea — **the effect only reacts when you play loud.** Mk.gee has done almost no interviews; this chain is reverse-engineered from a single onstage gear Q&A (his actual instrument + pedal), the record itself, and a loner (YouTube) breakdown, [the secrets behind Mk.gee's HYPNOTIC production!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=969p5Q4JSZU).
**Signal source:** a 60s reissue Fender Jaguar modified to a **baritone range** (Mk.gee's actual gear) — no baritone guitar owned, substitute a baritone-range sampler/VST for the same low register. Works equally on a real electric guitar tracked through [Electric Guitar Amp Track](#/chain/electric-guitar-amp-track) first.

## Chain overview

Preamp/comp/amp for a dynamics-dependent crunch → chorus/flanger/tape for overall color → a **noise-gated distorted-reverb send** (the actual secret — a Death By Audio-style FX Ranger pedal with a hidden built-in noise gate) that only fires on the loudest notes. Everything downstream of the first stage depends on the source performance having a genuinely **wide dynamic range** — quiet notes stay clean, loud notes trigger both the preamp crunch and the gated reverb. A flat/compressed take defeats the whole chain.

## Step 1 — Track/select the source

- **Baritone range is the tone, not a processing trick.** If tracking a real guitar, use (or approximate with a capo/tuning) a baritone instrument, or pitch a standard guitar's DI down before the chain. If using a sampler/VST, pick a baritone-voiced patch specifically for the low, semi-bass-like register.
- **Play/record with a genuinely wide dynamic range** — some notes really quiet, some really loud. This is a hard requirement, not a style choice: the preamp crunch (§2) and the gated reverb send (§3) are both threshold-dependent on note volume. → Gain Staging

## Step 2 — Front-of-chain tone (Ableton)

### 1. Decapitator (preamp) — crunch on the loudest notes only
- Drive high enough that the loudest played notes get a crunchy, distorted texture; quieter notes stay comparatively clean. *(general starting point — no exact drive value given on screen)*
- **Why:** this is where the wide-dynamic-range performance first pays off — the distortion is a function of note volume, not a constant setting.

### 2. Compressor — light shaping
- Gentle, not flattening — the goal is to preserve the dynamic swing from §1, not squash it back out. → Compressor

### 3. Amp sim
- Best-match owned lane: Archetype- John Mayer X or Guitar Rig 7 FX for the amp stage after the preamp/comp.

### 4. Chorus-Ensemble → Phaser-Flanger → Kramer Tape — overall tone/color
- Chorus first, flanger second, tape emulation last — a general width/movement/warmth stack, not a single dramatic effect. Same three-device order reused (differently weighted) in the CZ-style synth variation below.
- **Why:** sets the baseline tone before the send-based secret sauce gets added — this stage should sound "good" on its own with the reverb send off.

## Step 3 — The secret sauce: noise-gated distorted-reverb send

Mk.gee's actual pedal (named on camera): an FX Ranger-style **distorted reverb**. The part he never mentioned describing it: **it has a noise gate built in**, so the effect only activates above a set input volume.

1. Create a send/return track (Ableton: right-click the source track → **Route to This Track**, or route via a Return track).
2. On the return, in order: **Reverb → Distortion → Compressor.**
3. Add a **Gate BEFORE all of it** — first device in the return chain.
4. Set the gate's threshold so **only the loudest notes cross it** and trigger the reverb/distortion/compressor stack; quieter notes pass through with no send at all.
5. **Push the send harder (more aggressive Reverb + Distortion) on chord/harmony parts than on the bass part** — used to fill out arrangement space on a chords pass without drowning the lower, sparser bass part.

**Why:** without the gate, the distorted reverb is just a static effect on the send level. With the gate first, the effect becomes *performance-reactive* — it only "blooms" when the player pushes, which reads as the send coming alive rather than sitting there constantly. This is the actual mechanism Mk.gee's live pedal hides.

## Arrangement

**Where it sits:** low and almost bass-like — **BASS into MIDS**, which means it needs an explicit agreement with the actual bass part about who owns below 250 Hz.

**When it plays:** the gate decides. The distorted-reverb send only opens when he plays loud, so **dynamics are the arrangement** — a quiet passage and a loud one are different sections with no parts added or removed.

**The stated move:** push the send harder on chord/harmony passes than on the bass part, to fill arrangement space without drowning the lower, sparser part (Step 3.5 above). That's slot management by send level — the same idea as Session Layout's return rules, applied inside one instrument.

## Variations — CZ-style vintage synth chain

Same core device palette (chorus/flanger/tape/distortion/compression), reordered and extended, for a Casio CZ-5000-style vintage synth part instead of guitar (Mk.gee's song "CZ"):

1. **Source:** layer two DIFFERENT CZ-emulation VSTs — "Virtual CZ" (preset **"Sharp Angle"**) + a second, different CZ emulation from Arturia. Not owned → Plugin Wishlist, Vintage Gear Worklist (Casio CZ-101 already tracked as the closest documented unit).
2. **Phaser-Flanger → Chorus-Ensemble** — movement/width, same two devices as the guitar chain, reordered flanger-first.
3. **Kramer Tape** as the tape stage — closest owned equivalent to "Reels," used in the original for its **envelope-mode noise knobs** (hiss only sounds while a note plays, not a constant bed). Real gap: Kramer Tape doesn't document the same envelope-linked noise behavior — flag if the constant-noise artifact becomes audible. → Plugin Wishlist
4. **Little Plate** — a clean plate reverb as the "reset" stage, deliberately placed *before* the final dirt stage rather than as the last effect ("plates tend to be nice and clean").
5. **Decapitator → Glue Compressor** — distortion then **heavy compression placed LAST**, which is what reveals/brings out the texture the noise (tape) and flanger stages generated earlier in the chain, rather than just leveling the part.
- Leave the **first note of every bar silent** in the synth part — copied directly from "CZ" — leaving room for the bass to start the loop instead of colliding with the synth on beat 1.
- Layer a second, loud lead synth on top for a dynamic "jolt," applying the same wide-dynamic-range principle as the guitar chain.

## Notes

- **This is a texture/sound-design chain, not a corrective one** — nothing here is EQ/de-noise; the whole point is a controlled, performance-reactive distortion/reverb interaction. Pair with a properly tracked/de-noised source if recording a real guitar ([Electric Guitar Amp Track](#/chain/electric-guitar-amp-track)).
- **Dynamic range is the load-bearing idea across the whole chain** — see Gain Staging for the "play light, then push it hard" version of the same principle applied to drums on the same record.

**Sources:** loner — [the secrets behind Mk.gee's HYPNOTIC production!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=969p5Q4JSZU) (00:11:42, 2025-01-26) · full note: loner - the secrets behind Mk.gee's HYPNOTIC production!?

chains.title: Prof Jam Trouble Now Sample Chain
chains.routing: Nylon guitar + doubling piano + vocal chops + synth bass (late) + light percussion → [[2 Guitar Group|Guitar Group]] / [[2 Inst-Synth Group|Inst-Synth Group]] / [[2 Main Vocal Group|Main Vocal Group]] / [[2 Bass Group|Bass Group]] → [[3 Guitar Bus|Guitar Bus]] / [[3 Inst-Synth Bus|Inst-Synth Bus]] / [[3 Vocal Bus|Vocal Bus]] / [[3 Bass Bus|Bass Bus]] → Master
chains.reference: "Trouble Now" — Prof Jam & Benji Price (platinum, Portugal) — a from-scratch vintage Latin/guitar sample build, later sold via sample pack and flipped by an unrelated producer into the final song
plugins: reverb + Reels "Master Vintage" preset + Pro-C2 + low-cut EQ + Goodhertz Lossy "Packet Loss"
Analog Lab piano doubling the same chords through a near-identical chain
Little AlterBoy "Double Rainbow" vocal chop (reused for a switch-up)
Analog Lab Prophet "Bass Bass" synth bass (late entrance)
2x acoustic hi-hat + open hat (band-pass EQ + tremolo)
master Reels "Master Vintage" + boosted hiss + 3-semitone pitch-down
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a from-scratch "vintage Mexican/Latin" guitar sample, built in 2019 and sold in a sample pack with no idea it would ever be used — years later it turned up, unknown to its maker, as the core of "Trouble Now" by Prof Jam & Benji Price, which went platinum in Portugal. Reverse-engineered from a loner (YouTube) breakdown, [how i made the sample that got me a platinum song!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6aHjhniTOnk). Companion to [Kendrick Lamar Soul Sample Chain](#/chain/kendrick-lamar-soul-sample-chain) (same channel, same "doubled melodic layer + vocal-chop + synth-bass" shape) and [Dez Wright Guitar Sample Chain](#/chain/dez-wright-guitar-sample-chain) (same "write chords → color chain" guitar-sample method) — this build is the simplest/most compact of the three, and the only one with a confirmed real-world commercial outcome.

## Chain overview

Five elements: a nylon-guitar chord bed, a piano doubling the exact same chords through a near-identical processing chain, a vocal chop reused twice (different notes each time) as the arrangement's switch-up device, a synth bass that enters only at that switch-up, and a barely-there percussion texture layer. The build's two biggest reusable ideas: **doubling a melodic part on a second instrument through an almost-identical processing chain** (rather than one part carrying the whole harmonic weight), and **reusing one fully-processed vocal-chop chain twice with different notes** instead of building a second vocal sound for the arrangement's switch-up.

## 1. Guitar — nylon-string chord progression

- **Instrument:** a nylon-string guitar VST (original source, "Evolution Nylon Strings," discontinued/uninstalled; current substitute unresolved in auto-captions — "the elephant of nylon guitar"). Committing to nylon over steel-string/electric sets the track's vintage-Latin identity before any processing touches it.
- **Chords:** **C♯m (i, D♯ added a semitone above the E for tension) → C♯m (i, identical shape re-voiced two octaves up) → F♯m (iv) → G♯ major (V)** — full theory writeup: Chord Progressions, Chord Inversions.
- **Realism layer:** extra connective notes added on top of the base progression, PLUS deliberately uneven strum timing within a chord (e.g. the D♯ note hitting fractionally before the other two notes) — "that's what's making it sound really realistic," not the notes/velocities alone. → Pocket and Microtiming
- 🎬 *From video:* stagger a chord's note-on times by a few ms instead of triggering every note simultaneously — a concrete, transferable humanization move beyond MIDI velocity randomization.

## 2. Guitar FX chain

1. Reverb, likely ValhallaVintageVerb ("vintage verb").
2. A tape/vintage-color plugin (auto-caption "Reels" — see Plugin Wishlist, likely AudioThing Reels), "Master Vintage" preset.
3. Pro-C2 — light touch, "just to tighten it up a bit."
4. A low-cut EQ ("loca eq" in auto-captions).
5. Goodhertz Lossy, "Packet Loss" preset — final vintage/lossy-codec degradation, "takes away the quality of it."

## 3. Piano — doubling layer

- **Instrument:** Arturia Analog Lab 4, a plain piano preset, playing the EXACT same chord progression as the guitar.
- **FX chain (near-identical to the guitar's):** the same "Reels"/Master Vintage stage → Pro-C2 → an EQ (low-end cut + a notch on "a really harsh frequency") → a short reverb.
- 🎬 *From video:* "pretty similar processing to the guitar... my processing hasn't changed too much... I use a few different plugins but for the most part for the basics it's the same" — a self-observed, repeatable "double the melody, near-duplicate the chain" method.
- **Realism layer:** some piano notes deliberately hit early/off-grid — "this is what shows that it's a really old sample." → Pocket and Microtiming

## 4. Vocal chops

- **Source:** a hook sample from Output Arcade (2019; producer now prefers Splice or his own vocals for this role — see Plugin Wishlist).
- **Chain:** Little AlterBoy, "Double Rainbow" preset — pitch shifted all the way up, formant brought all the way down, filtered (cut high end, cut low end), a heavier reverb than the guitar/piano chains got, and a tremolo control panning the result hard side-to-side.
- 🎬 *From video:* the SAME processed chain/preset is reused later in the song for a late arrangement switch-up — just different notes, not a new sound — paired with removing some of the guitar's notes in that section to make room. → Arrangement and Song Form, Ear Candy and Hiding Synths

## 5. Synth bass — late entrance

- **Source:** "Bass Bass" preset, Prophet model inside Arturia Analog Lab.
- Enters only at the same late switch-up section as the vocal-chop change — not present for the whole track. → Bass Design

## 6. Percussion — texture layer

- Two acoustic-sounding hi-hats + one open hat.
- Processing: a band-pass EQ + a Goodhertz tremolo control. Kept "very very subtle" — "just adds a little bit of texture underneath," not a groove element. → Ambient Texture and Field Recording

## 7. Arrangement

- Start with every element EXCEPT the piano → bring the piano in partway through for a lift/sense of movement → slow the whole thing down toward the end, leaning on the vocal-chop switch-up + synth bass as the closing texture. → Arrangement and Song Form

## 8. Master bus

- Same "Reels"/Master Vintage-family color stage as the guitar/piano chains, with the hiss level deliberately boosted — "because I wanted that texture in the background."
- Final pitch-down of the whole finished bounce by **three semitones**, with a pitch-shift tool (likely Waves SoundShifter — see Plugin Wishlist).

## Variations

- **The "double the melody on a second instrument through a near-identical chain" move generalizes past guitar+piano** — any two complementary timbres (guitar+EP, synth+strings) carrying the same chord progression through matched processing reads as a fuller, more "real" sample than one instrument alone.
- **The "reuse one fully-processed vocal-chop chain for a switch-up, just swap the notes" move** is a cheap, reliable arrangement device — no second sound-design pass needed for a structural pivot.

## Notes

- No exact settings (reverb decay, EQ frequencies/gains, "Master Vintage" preset parameters, Pro-C2 ratio/threshold) were given on screen beyond the qualitative descriptions above — treat every device's setting as a starting point to dial in by ear.
- The "Reels" plugin identification is medium-confidence (auto-caption garble); RC-20 Retro Color was considered and ruled out (no "Reels" module in its documented manual) in favor of AudioThing Reels, already logged separately on Plugin Wishlist from another video.
- This is the only chain in this vault reverse-engineered from a video with a confirmed real-world commercial outcome (a platinum single) — the producer's own framing of the video is as much "put your samples out there, you never know" as it is a technical breakdown.

**Sources:** loner — [how i made the sample that got me a platinum song!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6aHjhniTOnk) (00:06:45, 2022-05-12) · full note: loner - how i made the sample that got me a platinum song!?

chains.title: SZA R&B Guitar Chain
chains.reference: SZA-style R&B guitar ("Blind"-inspired, SOS) — loner recreation, not a confirmed session chain
chains.body:
**Reference/vibe:** a nostalgic, ambient R&B guitar sound built from **two layers of the same guitar part** — a dry, tightly processed signal chain, plus a second reamped pass through a hardware pedal that detunes/delays the signal out of time, layered on top as a wash. Recreated (not a confirmed session breakdown) by loner from *Blind*, on SZA's *SOS* — [the secrets behind sza's 'sos' production!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qbkFwpExtVQ).
**Signal source:** a clean electric guitar, arpeggiated chord progression, for a nostalgic feel. Works over [Electric Guitar DI Track](#/chain/electric-guitar-di-track).

## Chain overview

Layer 1 (dry) sets the main tone: EQ → compressor → spring reverb → short slap delay → flanger → shaper box. Layer 2 (texture) re-runs the *same performance* through a Montreal Assembly Count to 5 hardware pedal (set to detune/delay the signal out of time), then shaper box → EQ → reverb → pan, and sits underneath/behind Layer 1 as an ambient wash rather than replacing it. The two layers are meant to be heard together — Layer 1 carries the part, Layer 2 blurs it.

## Step 1 — Layer 1: dry signal chain

Clean guitar, arpeggiated, tracked simply — no drive/distortion at the source, since the color comes from the FX chain, not the amp.

1. **EQ Eight** — general tonal shaping. *(general starting point — no specific curve given; start subtractive, cut mud below ~200 Hz, gentle presence lift ~2–4 kHz)*
2. **Compressor** — light-to-moderate leveling ahead of the space effects, so the reverb/delay tails that follow have a consistent input to work with.
3. **Spring reverb** — a short, "boingy," lo-fi-leaning reverb character (as opposed to a hall/plate) for the nostalgic feel. No dedicated spring-reverb plugin owned; closest owned options: ValhallaVintageVerb (has a spring-modeled algorithm) or UAD RealVerb-Pro. → Reverb (effect)
4. **Short slap delay** — a tight, single-repeat-feeling slap delay (short time, low feedback) rather than a rhythmic multi-tap delay. → Echo, Delay (effect)
5. **Flanger** — Phaser-Flanger or kHs Flanger for movement/width after the delay.
6. **Shaper box** — a rhythmic/transient/volume-shaping stage as the final coloring device on the dry layer. No ShaperBox (Cableguys) owned — see Plugin Wishlist (medium-impact item, already reused across multiple videos).

**Why:** each stage in Layer 1 is doing one job — EQ shapes tone, compressor levels dynamics, reverb + delay set space, flanger + shaper add movement/texture right at the end — a fairly standard "clean guitar → space → movement" build, but kept restrained so it reads as the main, in-focus part.

## Step 2 — Layer 2: reamped ambient texture layer

Re-run the *exact same guitar performance* (not a new take) through a second processing path:

1. **Montreal Assembly Count to 5** (hardware pedal) — set to delay/detune the signal so it reads as slightly out of time with the original. No hardware equivalent owned/tracked; substitute a modulated pitch/delay device (e.g. Shifter or Pitch Loop 89 detuned + a short delay) to approximate the "out of time" character. → Plugin Wishlist
2. **Shaper box** — same role as Layer 1's shaper stage, on the reamped signal.
3. **EQ** — carve this layer so it sits behind/around Layer 1 rather than competing with it (e.g. scoop the frequencies Layer 1 already owns). → EQ Eight
4. **Reverb** — a second, likely larger/washier reverb than Layer 1's spring, to push this pass further back in the mix. → Reverb (effect)
5. **PanMan** — pan the finished ambient layer, last in the chain, to place the wash in the stereo field (spread wide or offset from center, distinct from Layer 1's placement). → Width and Stereo

**Why:** reamping the *same* performance (instead of a new take) through a second, differently-processed path guarantees the two layers stay rhythmically/melodically identical while sounding texturally distinct — the ambient layer reads as an aura around the dry part rather than a separate, competing element.

## Arrangement

**Where it sits:** two layers of the *same* part — the dry chain in **MIDS**, the reamped detuned wash in **BED/AIR**. One performance, two slots.

**When it plays:** the wash layer is the section device. Dry alone for a verse, both layers for the hook — the part never changes, the second layer's send does. Same timbre-over-density habit as Psych-Pop (Tame Impala).

**Watch for:** the ambient layer is out-of-time by design, so it blurs anything sharing MIDS with it. Give the strummer the gaps or move one of them (Session Layout § guitar adds).

## Variations

- If the Count to 5 pedal isn't available, a modulated delay (long-ish time, moderate feedback, pitch-modulated repeats) run through the same shaper → EQ → reverb → pan stages gets close to the "detuned, out-of-time double" character.
- The same two-layer dry/reamped-texture idea generalizes beyond guitar — any clean melodic source (Rhodes, synth pad) can use the same "process it straight, then reamp the same performance through a wilder chain and blend underneath" structure.

## Notes

- **No confirmed link to SZA's actual session** — this is loner's from-scratch recreation inspired by *Blind*'s guitar tone, not a documented chain from SZA's engineers/producers.
- Pair with Little AlterBoy's formant-automation vocal technique from the same beat (same video) for the full "Blind"-inspired arrangement.

**Sources:** loner — [the secrets behind sza's 'sos' production!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qbkFwpExtVQ) (00:08:06, 2022-12-26) · full note: loner - the secrets behind sza's 'sos' production!?

chains.title: Delay Send Other
chains.routing: Return track — vocals, leads, throws → Vocal Bus
chains.body:
**Role:** The rhythmic/synced delay — dotted-8th and quarter-note repeats, ping-pong, ad-lib throws. Where slap adds *size*, this adds *motion and energy* (synced repeats push the groove; reverb just smears it).

## Signal chain

### 1. EchoBoy — Synced repeats
- **Echo Type: Ping-Pong** (①/⑧ — bounces L↔R) · **Time: dotted 1/8** (③ — the pop/U2 default; 1/4 for a slower throw) · **Feedback 22%** (④ — 2–4 audible repeats) · **Style: analog/tape character on** (② · ⑨) · **Low Cut 200 Hz / High Cut 8 kHz** on the feedback (⑥ — repeats sit behind the dry) · **Mix 100%** (⑦ — it's a return)
- **Why dotted-8th:** it lands off the main beats, so repeats fill the pockets *between* the vocal phrases instead of stacking on them.

### 2. Pro-Q 4 — Filter
- HPF 300–500 Hz · LPF 4–6 kHz — repeats always duller than the source.

### 3. Pro-C 2 — Duck (sidechain from dry vocal)
- 2–3 dB GR keyed from the lead · medium release
- **Simpler alt:** Ableton's stock Echo has **built-in ducking** (one knob + threshold) — use it when this return runs Echo instead of EchoBoy.
- **Why:** Repeats hide while the line is sung and answer in the gaps — you can run a hot send level and never lose a lyric. Same trick as the long reverb.

## EchoBoy deep tricks
- **Dual Echo polyrhythm:** 1/16 on one side, 1/8 on the other — the classic percussion/vocal stereo motion you hear everywhere without noticing.
- **Rhythm mode as a drum machine:** taps programmed like steps — run a plain hat through it for patterns you'd never write by hand.
- **It contains a chorus and a reverb** (in the style presets) — in a pinch, EchoBoy alone covers delay + chorus + verb on one return.
- **Section automation:** shorter delay in verses, longer in choruses; or build an Audio Effect Rack with chains (slap / 1/8 / 1/4 / ping-pong) and switch per section.
- **Throw track workflow:** for big word-throws, copy the word to a dedicated throw *track* (half-note ping-pong + reverb + a little distortion, 100% wet) instead of automating the send — more control, reusable. 🎬 *From video:* a working pro example of this exact pairing — EchoBoy delay throw + a hall reverb riding directly behind it, printed only on select verse lines rather than run continuously — Kevin Davis (Mix with the Masters), [Mixing Vocals from 'Dancing With A Stranger' with Kevin Davis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQIZONdZvk8)
- 🎬 *From video:* Disclosure keep a **second, quick out-of-time stereo delay** just for throws (separate from the main synced delay) — Disclosure, [NO CAP](https://youtu.be/kz5dmb3QdI8); and a **feedback delay ridden to self-oscillation** makes a DJ-friendly extended outro / transition — Disclosure, [Help Me Lose My Mind](https://youtu.be/FPgLRkgKoMU).

## Usage
- Hook vocals · **ad-lib throws:** automate the send up on the last word of a line (the classic rap throw) · synth leads (this send is their main space) · guitar solos.
- 🎬 *From video:* run TWO instances of this send together at the chorus — a standard synced eighth-note delay (as documented above) PLUS a second, wider eighth-note delay panned hard to the extremes for a panoramic left-right spread — Elmhirst's own description: "there's two different delays, there's an eighth note just doing standard eighth note, and then there's this other eighth note going off to the canyon... so it's much more panoramic, left and right." Both are introduced at the SAME structural moment (the chorus), on top of a reverb send already brought in one section earlier at the bridge — see Arrangement and Song Form for the full staged build. The wide pair reads as "a bed of lovely atmospherics behind her vocal" without eating up room in the mix, despite being two simultaneous delay returns. → Arrangement and Song Form, [Reverb Send Long](#/chain/reverb-send-long), [1 Main Vocal Track](#/chain/main-vocal-track), Width and Stereo — Mix with the Masters (Tom Elmhirst), Tom Elmhirst breaks down his mix of 'Rolling in the Deep' by Adele

## Variations
- **Trap quarter-triplet throws:** time 1/4T, feedback higher (40%), automate in for single words.
- **Dub/experimental:** feedback 50%+ momentarily and *ride it* — self-oscillation as a transition FX.

## From videos

- **Confirms this send's own §3 duck (Pro-C 2 sidechained from the dry vocal) as a universal, plugin-agnostic recipe — usable to duck any reverb or delay, not just ones with built-in ducking.** Pair with a 200–400 Hz EQ dip on the return (this send's existing HPF/LPF plus that specific masking-range carve) as the second half of the fix. → Sidechaining, Masking and Carving — Sage Audio, [The 5 MOST IMPORTANT Vocal Mixing Tips](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rXk1lvT6AhU)
- **Two instances of this send run together at the chorus — a standard eighth-note delay plus a second, wider eighth-note delay panned hard for a panoramic spread — see the inline 🎬 note in Usage above.** → Arrangement and Song Form, [Reverb Send Long](#/chain/reverb-send-long), Width and Stereo — Mix with the Masters (Tom Elmhirst), Tom Elmhirst breaks down his mix of 'Rolling in the Deep' by Adele
- **A short tap plus a quarter-note tap, built inside one combined reverb+delay plugin instead of two separate sends.** "We'll do a little delay here, and then the second one will be quarter note" — CLA reaches for Waves CLA Epic (unowned) specifically so the short-tap+quarter-note pairing lives in one plugin ("it's all in one... rather than trying to build something from scratch"). Owned-lane equivalent for the same pairing: this send at **Time 1/4** (instead of the default dotted-1/8) running alongside [Delay Send Slap](#/chain/delay-send-slap) for the short tap. *(qualitative — feedback/mix not given)* → [Delay Send Slap](#/chain/delay-send-slap), Reverb (effect), Plugin Wishlist — Chris Lord-Alge (Mix with the Masters), Chris Lord-Alge processing vocals
- **EchoBoy delay throw + hall reverb, paired directly and printed only on specific verse lines, not two independent sends.** "I also had a delay throw in here with a reverb on it on certain lines that he said in the verse. I'm using the EchoBoy for that delay throw. Followed by a hall verb." — confirms this send's throw-track workflow as a real pro recipe, with the specific addendum that the reverb rides the same selected words as the throw for a bigger accent than either alone. → ValhallaRoom, Reverb (effect) — Kevin Davis (Mix with the Masters), [Mixing Vocals from 'Dancing With A Stranger' with Kevin Davis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQIZONdZvk8)
- **One EchoBoy setting, five subdivisions** — his 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, slap and 1/2 sends are the *same* EchoBoy patch varied only by note value, band-limited with EchoBoy's internal high/low cut — every delay in the song shares one tone family — Kenny Beats, [New Vocal Chain 2022](https://youtu.be/-SvBNOBWJ_8)
- **The throw/effects track** — drag the last word of a line onto a dedicated track with a loud **insert** EchoBoy (high end cut, subdivision changed per throw) + a ducked long-reverb send: the delay throw as an arrangement event, not an always-on send — Kenny Beats, [New Vocal Chain 2022](https://youtu.be/-SvBNOBWJ_8) → Automation

chains.title: Delay Send Slap
chains.routing: Return track — vocals mainly → Vocal Bus
chains.body:
**Role:** Single short echo (80–140 ms) — the "thickener" delay. Reads as size and attitude, not as an audible echo. THE hip hop and rock'n'roll vocal effect (and the sound of every 50s Elvis record).

## Signal chain

### 1. EchoBoy — The slap
- **Echo Type: Studio Tape** (①, Slapback style ②) · **Time 110 ms, unsynced** (③ — slap is a physical size cue, not rhythmic; syncing to tempo usually makes it worse) · **Feedback 5%** (④ — ONE repeat) · **Wow & Flutter on** for tape character (⑤) · **High Cut ~6 kHz** on the repeat (⑥) · **Mix 100%** (⑦ — it's a return)
- **Why:** One fast, slightly-degraded repeat fools the ear into hearing a bigger performance rather than an effect — thickness without the pitch-wobble of chorus or the wash of reverb.
- 🎬 *From video:* Disclosure reach for **slapback (+ a short "toilet"-sized room verb) to put a vocal *in a space* rather than flood a cathedral** — reads as "mic in a room," more natural/human; and on a chorus bus a slapback keeps it **present/"right there"** while other sections use long verbs (a very Lennon/Beatles move) — Disclosure, [Deeper](https://youtu.be/SM0FZ58ckVw) / [Waterfall](https://youtu.be/sL5CG444qwQ). Often run as a **track insert**, not just this send.

### 2. Pro-Q 4 — Filter
- HPF 250–400 Hz · LPF 3–5 kHz — the repeat should always be *smaller* than the source (duller + narrower = sits behind). EchoBoy note: its low cut sits *before* the delay circuit, high cut *after* — use the high cut for taming, and remember darker repeats read as *moving away* (free depth).
- Stereo control: EchoBoy's tweak panel has a **L/R offset** (~25 = repeats spread off-center; 0 = mono slap dead behind the voice — both are valid looks).

**Combine, don't choose:** slap + [Delay Send Other](#/chain/delay-send-other)'s 1/8 running together is the standard pro vocal setup — slap does thickness, the synced delay does motion.

## Usage
- Lead vocal (rap verses especially — slap instead of reverb keeps it dry-but-big) · ad-libs · lead guitar stabs.

## Variations
- **Doubling effect:** pull time down to 60–90 ms and pan the return slightly off-center — fake double.
- **50s/Beatles slap:** more EchoBoy wobble + saturation, time ~120–140 ms.

## From videos

- **The general principle behind this send's own "sidechain-duck the return to the lead" entry below: this works on ANY reverb/delay plugin, not just ones with built-in ducking — put it on an aux, sidechain a compressor to the dry vocal, done.** Pairs with an EQ dip at 200–400 Hz on the return for the vocal-masking-range half of the fix. → Sidechaining, Masking and Carving — Sage Audio, [The 5 MOST IMPORTANT Vocal Mixing Tips](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rXk1lvT6AhU)
- **Howard's one-slap rule** — a single, extremely short delay repeat, very low in the mix, on almost anything (vocals, drums, instruments): "it makes it sound like you're in a small club — that's where things sound good" — Disclosure, [Remix Stems Stream](https://youtu.be/IOSPhXcXT_8) → Depth and Space
- **Band-limit inside EchoBoy** — use EchoBoy's built-in high/low cut on the return instead of a separate EQ after it: one less device, same tail control — Kenny Beats, [New Vocal Chain 2022](https://youtu.be/-SvBNOBWJ_8)
- **Sidechain-duck the return to the lead** — compressor on the delay return keyed from the main vocal: tails tuck while words happen, bloom in the gaps — Kenny Beats, [Vocal Template](https://youtu.be/X_iDENABLmk) → Sidechaining

chains.title: Parallel Comp Send
chains.routing: Return track — drums mainly, vocals sometimes → Master
chains.body:
**Role:** The "New York" crush bus — a destroyed copy of the drums blended *under* the clean ones. Adds weight, sustain, and room excitement while the dry signal keeps all its transients. Parallel = you can crush without consequences.

**Theory:** serial compression trades transients for control. Parallel compression sidesteps the trade: the dry path keeps the punch, the crushed path brings up all the quiet detail (ghost notes, room, decay), and you mix in just enough of the wreckage.

## Signal chain

### 1. Pro-Q 4 — Pre-EQ (the "NY" part, optional)
- Smiley: +2–3 dB lows (~100 Hz) and highs (~8 kHz) *before* the comp
- **Why:** The compressor slams the boosted extremes hardest, exaggerating the thick-bottom/crispy-top character of the classic NYC drum sound.

### 2. UAD UA 1176LN — The crush
- **All-buttons-in mode** (push all 4 ratio buttons) · attack FAST (7) · release FAST (7) · input cranked for **10–20 dB GR — pin the needle, it cannot be too much here**
- **Why all-buttons:** the ratio goes nonlinear and program-dependent, adding explosive harmonic excitement — famous on drum busses for 50 years. The fast release creates the pumping that drags up room sound and sustain.
- Alt flavors: Devil-Loc Deluxe (even more destroyed) · FETish (same 1176 trick, native).
- 🎬 *From video:* on a **film/game percussion stem**, this exact fast-1176-into-EQ shape gets reused lighter — a Chris Lord-Alge-style 1176 blended (not slammed) with a Pultec-style EQ pushing top end, aimed at "snap" rather than NYC-style crush; framed as necessary because media delivery is separate stems, not one locked mix, so the whole stem gets parallel-compressed as a unit instead of the finished mix Andrew Scheps-style. → UAD Pultec EQP-1A, Parallel Processing, TRANSIENT Slot — Mix with the Masters (Alan Meyerson), Adding impact to percussions with Alan Meyerson

### 3. Pro-Q 4 — Post-tame (optional)
- HPF 40 Hz · shave any harsh 3–5 kHz the crush created.
- 🎬 *From video:* an alternate top-end stage in this same slot — Pultec-style EQ pushing "top end" for snap, positioned as an addition to the crush rather than a tame — worth trying instead of/alongside the HPF+shave move above when the goal is more snap, not less harshness. → UAD Pultec EQP-1A — Mix with the Masters (Alan Meyerson), Adding impact to percussions with Alan Meyerson

## Usage
- 🎬 *From video:* related pattern worth cross-checking against this send's single-crush design — a **four-aux system**, not one send, where each aux rebuilds a specific quality lost to heavy bus compression (transient spark, tonal attention, kick character) rather than one aux doing everything. See [3 Drums Bus](#/chain/drums-bus) for the full aux-by-aux breakdown and Parallel Processing for the philosophy — Mix with the Masters (Jaycen Joshua), Jaycen Joshua on creative drum mixing
- 🎬 *From video:* PSP Vintage Warmer 2 (unowned) auditioned as an alternate/additional color source on this exact send, specifically for its "snap" character — with an explicit latency caution named before committing another device to the bus. Reusable habit: treat added latency on a parallel send as a real risk to check for, not something PDC always makes a non-issue. → Plugin Wishlist — Mix with the Masters (Alan Meyerson), Adding impact to percussions with Alan Meyerson
- **Send selectively, post-fader:** kick, snare, toms YES — **cymbals, overheads, and hats NO** (cymbals + heavy compression = splatty wash). This per-element choice is exactly why it's a send and not an insert on the group.
- Blend the return from silence until the kit feels bigger, then back off 1 dB. Should be *felt disappearing* when muted, not heard. Soloed, it's *supposed* to sound ugly — "be aggressive, be a little nasty with it."
- **The chorus move:** automate the *crush return* up +1 dB in choruses instead of the drum faders — energy lifts without the drums getting louder.
- 🎬 *From video:* a harder-committed version of the chorus move above, confirmed on a hit record — instead of a gradual +1 dB automation ride, the whole parallel-comp path is withheld entirely until one structural landmark (the outro-chorus lift) and then switched on across THREE separate signal groups at once: kit close mics, room mics, AND stomp tracks simultaneously. Toggling it in/out is audible as a sudden jump in drive/excitement, not a slow build. → Parallel Processing, Arrangement and Song Form — Mix with the Masters (Tom Elmhirst), Tom Elmhirst breaks down his mix of 'Rolling in the Deep' by Adele
- **Vocals:** a quieter parallel-crush send under a lead adds density on hooks (send less than drums).

## Variations
- **Crush + tape:** add Kramer Tape driven hard *after* the 1176 on the return — compression + tape wreckage is the full old-school NY chain.
- **Pumping as an effect (EDM/hip hop):** turn the return UP until the pump is audible and rhythmic — a creative choice, not a mistake, if it grooves.

chains.title: Reverb Send Long
chains.routing: Return track — receives sends from features/hooks → Vocal Bus
chains.body:
